和 @Xudong07452910 一起来参加 AI Engineer，完全感受到这里的 AI native 氛围。

@ryolu_ 的分享像散文诗：当我们什么都能做了，还知道自己想做什么吗？他不想要一个更会回应自己的世界，想保留一个能让他改变的世界。
not a world that no longer needs us. a world we have more ability to shape. 

杨滢（屠龙的胭脂井）的观点很有趣：科学的本质是编解码——Science 是编码，engineering 和 technology 是解码。AGI 是最强的解码器，在编码最清晰的地方最厉害。编码不清、充满隐性知识的群岛，才是垂直 AI 该去填的海。

@Saccc_c 用 16 天在 Unity 里做出《小王子》，全网曝光超 4000 万。让人感叹 Opus 5.5 写代码、操纵 DCC 的能力。他说自己不太懂游戏和建模，最重要的是想法。

Manus 分享了自己的 AI native 协作方式，我也深深受用。组织方式要进化：多个任务的上限是人的注意力。真的需要一个 Super Agent，来减少对齐成本，而不是牺牲大量注意力。

Panel 上主持人问这些 VC 拒得最多的项目是什么。
王淮说，拒得最多的是 physical AI 里的世界模型，以及 RSI。关键是 RSI for what。
真格戴雨森更谨慎那些偏科研、还没想过技术和商业怎么结合的项目；更愿意看动手做出结果、有真实用户反馈的，像 Hypit。

之前曲凯也说到，更怀念 23、24 年，那时更纯粹。现在听得最多的是模型解锁了什么、用最新模型讲了什么故事。

对做游戏来说，目标就是两字：好玩。要从真实研发宣发侧需求出发去解决，而不应是世界模型那样一键生成。

要学会自己掌舵
在不确定里睡觉、吃饭
在空白里识别渴望
不再把浪当成命运
也不再把岸当成答案

回去继续做 Artstrio
继续遇见新的自己

How to trade the liquidation levels?

The short term crypto market prices are almost entirely controlled by perpetual futures exchanges aka casinos. They sell bets against crypto prices to gamblers and offer magnified gains using leverage multipliers. But there is a liquidation level. If this level is crossed the gambler gets liquidated and the casino takes all their collatoral. On a large liquidation day this is $billions in liquidations. 

Note: The casino will manipulate the prices to "flush" these gamblers in high leverage bets. This is how the exchanges make their money. It is easy for the Centralized Exchange casino to do this using wash trading which is unregulated. They simply buy or sell synthetic crypto on their order book, either themselves via spoofing, or via external market makers.

Rough guideline: The red lines get flushed several times a day, the yellow lines once a week, the blue lines once every 3 weeks. 

The liquidation level chart shows the overleveraged trader liquidation levels. (These are gamblers, not spot holders). Gamblers use leverage perpetual futures on Centralized Exchanges and Decentralized Exchanges to magnify gains using multipliers. The standard multipliers offered by the casinos are:

100x - Red Lines - these are liquidated if the price moves 1% against the gambler.
50x - Yellow Lines- these are liquidated if the price moves 2% against the gambler.
25x - Blue Lines- these are liquidated if the price moves 4% against the gambler.

How do you use this edge as a trader? You set limit orders where these gamblers will be liquidated and exit your trade when the highest concentration of gamblers have been liquidated. Then you set a new trap again and wait. 

This is a trap strategy. You set traps and wait for the manipulation to flush the leverage and pick you up. Your exit should be fast for red line scalping, you can remain in position longer for yellow line scalping and even longer for blue line scalping, but the wait will be longer.

The purple lines indicate the levels where liquidations will most likely begin and end.

Follow along. Learn, observe and start beating the casino at their own game.

- Millennium is pulling more than $1.5 billion from two outside managers.

One fund selling to meet a margin call can push prices lower for the others, forcing another round of selling.

text:
"Hello Mr. Minervini. Today you have the ability to do serious damage to yourself. Keep that in mind, now get to work."

The morning ritual of the two-time U.S. Investing Champion Mark Minervini (@markminervini) on why a 30% win rate still makes money, why he never bets on a fundamental idea without price confirming it, and the one sin that kills amateurs and pros alike.

He won the championship in 1997 and again in 2021, with 334.8% in the $1M+ division per the championship's record, breaking the championship record for most gain in a single year. 

Separately, Jack Schwager profiled him in Stock Market Wizards for his 5 year run of 33,554% audited gains.

"In all the time that I've been doing this, I have not found another way of avoiding a big loss other than taking a small loss."

We cover:
- The first account, $32,338 from selling his recording studio, and the 33,500% compounded return that Schwager had audited, by his own account
- Reward to risk at 2 to 1 minimum: "my batting average can come all the way down into the 30% range and I still don't lose money"
- Why losses work geometrically against you: down 50 needs 100, down 90 needs 900
- "The cardinal sin is most traders don't cut their losses. Amateur and pro alike"
- "You do not manage money in hindsight. Risk has to be managed in real time"
- Why diversification only spreads the risk: "when you get a bear market, everything goes down". Why he starts 25% invested and scales up only on profits
- The 6:05 train: how he knows a trade is failing before the stop is hit. "If it's happening on schedule, we stay with the trade"
- Why everybody isn't rich if the setup goes back to the 1800s: "Because it ebbs and flows", and why the tough times are boot camp
- The year he stood outside a brokerage every day to check quotes, and the Twitter replies that called it a lie
- The 7 years he spent losing money before he not only unlocked profitability, but also an insane run of performance.
- His rule for gurus: if somebody tells you how to make $10 million, "my first requirement is that they actually made $10 million themselves"
- "Dream audaciously. Dream unrealistically. And act independent of the good opinion of others"

Thank you @markminervini for coming on Titans of Tomorrow, and for inviting us to your annual Gala. 
it was a true pleasure.

One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

text:
$AERO | @aerodromefi VS $UNI | @Uniswap

Aerodrome and Velodrome just finished merging into one token, Aero, with the Coinbase migration running Nov 2 to 4.

Can they now be the biggest competitor to Uniswap in the space?

AERO: Up 50.5% YTD 🟢
UNI: Up 20% YTD 🟢

Both tokens have given positive returns in 2026.

Market cap:

$UNI: ~$4.4B
$AERO: ~$470M

A ~9x gap. But Uniswap doesn't pay its holders 9x more.

We ran the numbers 👇

1️⃣ What you're actually buying

Uniswap is the biggest DEX in crypto. 40+ chains, the deepest liquidity, and the longest track record in DeFi.

=> You're buying the index of onchain trading.

Aero is the liquidity hub of Base, now expanding to Ethereum, Optimism and more after the merger. Protocols pay its voters to steer liquidity into their pools.

=> You're buying a liquidity marketplace that also runs a DEX.

2️⃣ Fees and Revenue

UNI: $82.8M in fees over 30 days, about 8x Aero. But only ~10% of that reaches the protocol: $8.2M.

AERO: $10.48M in fees over 30 days, and ~71% of it reaches holders: $7.5M.

So Uniswap earns 8x the fees, while holder revenue is almost identical.

3️⃣ The value-capture split

The real DEX question is not "how much volume," it's "how much reaches the token?"

UNI: $8.37M in 30 days, all of it used to buy back and burn UNI. Holders don't get paid directly. Supply shrinks instead.

AERO: $7.7M in 30 days, paid straight to veAERO lockers, with bribes from protocols on top. You have to lock to earn.

A ~9x market cap gap, and holders got roughly the same last month. That's the whole debate.

4️⃣ Usage

This is where Uniswap pulls away.

Uniswap: ~$65B in volume over the last 4 weeks, ~$3.6B TVL, $5.6B+ in lifetime fees.

Aero: $19B in DEX volume over 30 days, ~$348M TVL, ~$560M in lifetime fees.

Aero still makes ~90% of its fees on Base. Uniswap's are spread across dozens of chains, with Robinhood Chain now a big slice.

5️⃣ Valuation

UNI: ~42x P/S, ~4.4x P/F
AERO: ~2.3x P/S, ~3.7x P/F

On fees, they're close. On what holders actually get, AERO is ~8x cheaper.

Annualize last month's holder revenue and AERO returns ~19% of its market cap to lockers. UNI returns ~2.3% through burns. A big gap, but it assumes last month repeats for 12 more.

6️⃣ Price and drawdown

UNI: ~$7.00, ~84% below its $44.92 ATH (May 2021). Down ~18% on the month.

AERO: ~$0.60, ~74% below its $2.32 ATH (Dec 2024). Down ~33% from the ~$0.89 merger pump in late September.

Both are deep off their highs, so if you believe in either or both, this is the zone to start watching.

✦ What to expect going ahead

UNI is the scale bet.

Biggest volume, deepest liquidity, 40+ chains
Fee switch live and expanding chain by chain, 11%+ of supply already burned
The risk: holders capture only ~10% of fees, the burn is indirect, and the valuation leans on the fee switch growing.

AERO is the value-capture bet.

~71% of fees to holders
Lowest P/S in the matchup, and holder revenue that already matches Uniswap's
The risk: AERO emissions still cost more than the protocol earns, most fees come from one chain, and the multichain expansion is unproven.

This isn't a zero sum game either. Different models, different users. Both could keep printing, one could take off, or the DEX trade could cool for both 💭

text:
Anthropic just disclosed $895.4 BILLION in compute commitments. Nearly 13x its annualized revenue.

Guys, I think Wall Street is looking at the AI boom through the wrong lens.

Everyone is obsessed with which model wins. Meanwhile, the real bottleneck is becoming painfully obvious.

Power. Land. Grid access. Permits.

Nearly $70B of Anthropic's commitments comes due by September 2027, just as building new infrastructure becomes increasingly political.

Here's the part investors are missing.

AI companies are valued like software businesses, but their infrastructure demands look more like heavy industry.

The companies controlling scarce power and compute capacity could have enormous pricing leverage, regardless of which AI model wins.

The next great AI investment might not be an AI company at all.

Joining Hetu takes a TEE registration and a small bond. There's no whitelist.

We chose that on purpose. A whitelist decides in advance who's allowed to do useful work, and someone has to maintain it. We'd rather let anyone try and make cheating expensive.

So a node is judged on what it delivers, and the bond is what it stands to lose. Anyone can challenge a result. If the challenge holds, the bond is slashed.

Would you trade that openness for a curated list?

text:
Everyone’s watching Lighter’s CFTC filing. I’m watching Dec 27, when ~13.9M $LIT a month starts hitting the market 👀

@Lighter_xyz said on its Q3 call that it’ll file for a DCM + DCO by end of November. If that ever gets approved, it’s a regulated US venue with its own clearing. Most Perp DEXs don’t have that. But the review alone can take 6+ months.

Meanwhile buybacks are picking up, and they get burned now.

> Sep: $2.66M → Oct: $4.11M (+55% MoM)
> $4.11M x 12 → ~$49M a year
> ~6% of the ~$800M mcap | ~1.5% of the ~$3.2B FDV
6% vs 1.5%. That gap is what I care about.

Only ~250M of 1B $LIT is circulating. On Dec 27 the 1-year cliff ends for team (26%) and investors (24%), and 500M starts vesting linearly over 3 years.

Now some basic math.

> 500M / 36 months → ~13.9M $LIT a month
> at ~$3.2 that’s ~$44M of new supply monthly
> vs ~$4.1M of buyback bids → roughly 10x
> 12 months in, circulating goes ~250M → ~417M (+67%)

At least it’s linear. No single day where 500M lands at once.

And that’s before the 250M ecosystem bucket, which still has no public schedule.

Honestly I’m not rushing into $LIT before the cliff. Product is still Tier 1 for me, but I want to see how the first weeks of vesting trade and whether Nov buybacks beat October.

October might also be a peak month, so I’m treating the $49M as a best case for now.

My take: the CFTC angle is real upside, but until buybacks catch up with ~$44M a month of vesting, supply wins.

Holding $LIT through Dec 27 or waiting for the flush?

text:
CNBC / Fox / Schwab 今日观点：NVIDIA、Micron 与 AI 基建抛售后的再定价

周四科技股、尤其是AI基建链条的抛售，本质是一次技术性、情绪驱动的过度反应，而非基本面裂痕。

多位嘉宾将其与2020年3月和2025年4月“解放日”并列，属于职业生涯前五大级别的波动。

算力供需缺口（需求约为有效供给的4倍）并未改变，已锁定电力与土地的玩家反而因稀缺性强化定价权。

市场当前定价更接近“AI革命已结束”，这与头部实验室收入加速、代理式AI推理拐点以及物理AI下一波需求形成明显错位。

抛售属性与市场结构
Dan（25年从业经验）明确将其定义为科技赢家的“代际级买入窗口”。Neo-cloud部分公司下跌合理，但NVDA、AMD等核心芯片不应被同等定价；电力设备（如GE Vernova）的调整相对更有逻辑。

即使2027–2028年75%已获批的德州数据中心中，有10–15 GW无法落地，供需比仍维持在4:1附近。已持有算力的超大规模云厂商反而可能获得更高议价权。

Mike指出Micron远期PE不足4倍，已隐含市场对其盈利可持续性的极端怀疑；SOX指数自高点回落近40%，需上涨约20%才能回到20日均线。对冲基金平仓 + 散户抛售构成“真正出清”条件，但空头叙事目前仍占上风。

核心风险在于客户融资能力而非芯片自身需求。只要需求持续领先供给，芯片公司就处于有利位置——历史上真正的问题几乎都出在供给过剩，而非当前这种产能严重不足。

关键催化剂与估值锚
短期最重要事件：Anthropic IPO（市场预期11月16日当周定价）以及11月17日Nvidia财报。

Nvidia较年内高点回落超过20%，近一周下跌约14%。远期PE约16倍（部分嘉宾称13.5倍），已低于标普500的约19倍，处于“从未如此便宜”区间。建议分批建仓（先建一半，确认后补另一半）。

财报关注点：营收预期约1,080亿美元；毛利率若跌破72%且指引疲软，股价可能再承压10–20%。但当前没有GPU因需求不足而闲置，与互联网泡沫时期的“暗光纤”有本质区别。
Anthropic：修订版S-1显示总承诺支出8,954亿美元（其中4475亿美元预计2030年底前支出），现金及有价证券超300亿美元，可能再募约1,000亿美元。资金到位优先于估值高低，2万亿甚至1.5万亿的估值设想可能偏高。

产业链最新动态
TSMC：The Information报道其应Nvidia要求考虑3D DRAM（该来源此前在Nvidia传闻上可靠性存疑）。3D DRAM可用于提升HBM单颗容量，是制造方式而非全新产品线。

Micron：Bloomberg称其暂停台湾45亿美元工厂工程，主因劳资纠纷而非削减产能；公司随后确认台湾运营正常。

SK Hynix：HBM4累计良率达到60%中段，预计2026年Q4在出货量与营收上超过HBM3E。作为Nvidia最大HBM供应商，Rubin将采用HBM4。

Microsoft / Oracle：Microsoft不续签2023年A100协议，原因是设备老化、主动升级，而非需求下滑。Oracle称续约或转售价格较原合同高20%。

OpenAI：完成约110亿美元首轮融资，估值1.25万亿美元（本轮总额最多可达200亿美元，最初目标更高）。

IREN 财报与目标价调整
季度营收2.28亿美元（AI云2亿美元），合同价格持续上涨（三年期+11%，五年期+12%），AI云毛利率86%。40亿美元以上ARR目标已全部签约并获资金，但验收后Microsoft要求调整网络配置，导致目标推迟至2027年1月（可能延至2月）。

资本开支因资本市场状况下调，而非需求不足。Sweetwater 1/2合计2 GW已在建并获保障，Vera Rubin预计明年底开始到货且极度稀缺。

计入稀释与ARR推迟后，2027年上半年目标价区间从90–120美元下调至67–91美元（未来进一步稀释将继续下移）。

第一份真正吸引市场的财报预计推迟至2027年8月。仍维持看多至2028年上半年，但需持续跟踪稀释节奏。

长期逻辑Jensen在Lex Fridman播客中提到Nvidia有望成为年营收3万亿美元的公司。当前代理式AI推动推理需求拐点，物理AI被CFO称为“数万亿美元机会”。

产品路线图清晰：Blackwell Ultra已量产，Vera Rubin交付中，2027年Rubin Ultra，2028年Feynman。

全球算力受限至少持续至2028年，超大规模云厂商均表示供给受限，且建设基于已签合同与预付款。这与互联网泡沫有本质区别。

结论：本轮抛售过度，基本面未变，但底部位置与持续时间仍不确定。短期重点跟踪Anthropic定价与Nvidia财报中的毛利率及前瞻指引。投资者应保持冷静与长期视角，避免仓促决策。算力稀缺性是当前最核心的定价锚。

NFA, DYOR.

text:
有个共识，圈内基本没人反对：IP 是流动性最差的资产类别。但过去大家想解决它的方向，可能一开始就偏了。

以前那些尝试，都在琢磨"怎么让 IP 变得更好交易"——上交易所、做碎片化、搞 NFT。可你发现没有，折腾半天，粉丝还是那批粉丝，只是多了一层"能买卖"的壳。IP 的流动性问题，本质上没动。

我看 @IPXExchange，觉得它想做的是更深的那一层：不是让 IP 更好交易，是让粉丝自己变成流动性。

这话怎么理解？以前粉丝追星，是纯花钱。买专辑、买票、打榜，钱出去了，换来的是情绪价值。现在 IPX 把这套东西拆成代币，收入在链上实时分给持有者。等于你喜欢一个 IP，可以不只是"为它花钱"，还能"和它一起赚钱"。

这一步，其实把粉丝的身份给改了。从"消费者"，变成了"合伙人"。你持有某个 IP 的代币，它的宣发、变现、分发，都跟你的收益挂钩。喜欢和投资，第一次变成了同一件事。

而这个逻辑，正好也解释了他们 FAN SZN 活动为什么这么设计。活动就 10 天，11 月 5 号到 15 号，是 Pre-TGE 冲刺。

第一步不是让你充钱，是让你做 Fan Check 粉丝测验，答完 7 道题，系统按你的成绩和粉丝数生成一张 Fan Card。这个动作看着简单，其实是在筛"你是真粉丝，还是来薅羊毛的"。它把"身份"当成了入场券，而不是把"钱包"当入场券。

后面再往上，是内容创作，AI 助手 Alfred 给你的原创推文打分，一条 100 到 1000 Aura；还有每日签到，倍率逐日涨；邀请机制，拉来的人得真留下来才算数。这一层层加码，都是在找那批"愿意持续参与"的人。

所以 FAN SZN 的本质，不是发福利，是给上线那天，先囤一批"既懂 IP、又愿意长期持有"的种子用户。这比上线后临时买量，扎实太多了。

能不能成，看 11 月 15 号上线后的真实成交。但至少这个"把粉丝变成合伙人"的思路，在 IP 这个赛道上，是少见的清醒。

text:
Finally some new perp instruments, here is why you should care, and how you should price it.

First of all payoff: like an option it gives you convexity (which is just a fancy word to say that each extra $1 rise in HYPE adds more to your PnL than the previous one). You'll find the payoff function against a call and a perp down the tweet.

The main question you're probably wondering is why should you care to trade a power perp vs just doubling the leverage you're using. We'll dive into that for the pricing specifically for people looking to trade it systematically, but for the every day directional trader the answer is the gains grow much quicker as price grows. Which also comes from a downside: it seems that these kind of instruments have a much greater risk of being ALDed, but if liquidity is there, it gives a brand new payoff to perp traders.

About the pricing now, the best way to think about it is to come from the seller PoV. Let's suppose HYPE and the normalized squared index both start at $100 (not too far from where we are today). You sell one HYPE² contract and thus you buy two HYPE perps to hedge. Around that price, a $1 rise makes the squared contract gain apprx $2 so your short and your hedge initially offset each other (bc for a small return x, (1+x)²  is approx 1+2x, which means you're delta hedged with 2x HYPE). Now HYPE rises to $110, your short loses $21 but the hedge gains $20. You (still) lose $1 and on top of that the old hedge is no longer large enough. At $110, HYPE² has the sensitivity of 2.2 HYPE. Thus you buy another 0.2 HYPE at $110 to be delta hedged. Then HYPE falls back to $100. Your short gains $21, but your 2.2 HYPE hedge loses $22. $1 loss again! The required hedge falls back to 2, so you sell back that extra 0.2 HYPE at $100. 

HYPE finished exactly where it started but you lost $2, without even accounting for your rebalancing fees. Rebalancing a short-convexity position makes you buy after rises and sell after falls by design. These losses are what you need to charge for, and this is the useful options analogy: an option seller receives an upfront premium which here is replaced by the ongoing funding of the perp instead. Both need compensation for supplying the curve. 

So for HYPE² near its index, a simple continuous-hedging model gives:

Fair annual funding ≈ pricing volatility² + 2 × annual HYPE perp funding

And the intuition here is pretty simple: rebalancing forces the seller to buy after rises and sell after falls (that's the opposite of gamma scalping), the expected cost scales with volatility squared, and you have to hedge 2x so you pay 2 funding rates additionally.

You also realised given the formula that you need to price volatility, which you can benchmark with options IV, happy to do a second post on how to estimate that and trade the gap.

I'm going to give a contrarian take on Neoclouds like $NBIS and say the theme looks compelling after the valuation crash. 

Since there's a reason why Elon's $SPCX is heavily focused on this market full of "guppies" that would die: 

He sees how attractive the economics are after selling compute to $GOOGL and Anthropic. 

And this is reflected by his actions not words, from SpaceX's recent $40B financing for GPUs procurement. 
$AMZN, $MSFT, and even $META also see how profitable the economics are and are accelerating their AI DC buildouts. 

I'd argue if a Neocloud has: 

- Close relationships with $NVDA + others for allocations
- Existing contracted capacity + permitting
- Well funded counterparties, such as Hyperscalers. 
- Attractive economics, such as financing their procurement correctly (not the way $CRWV has with high debt interest unless they refinance). 

Then I think they'll do just fine... 

However, the bigger worry is more toward newer players starting financing or the permitting process, since barrier to entry has now become extremely high. 

For financing, read through on $IREN earnings has shown public Neoclouds can adapt extremely well to tight markets:

As seen with their 90% prepayments for GPU capex on a 5Y deal. 

Their older H100 GPUs recontracted at double their previous pricing and 12% higher contracted pricing also point against depreciation fears. 

And in the case DC buildouts slow from permitting delays... it heavily favors some over others. 

Rosenblatt's recent note for example stated they see little risk with $NBIS primary buildout that was in Missouri, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina. 

And there's probably less risk with developers in places like Australia. 

Markets have also show this infinite compute arbitrage can't go on forever, hence the reluctance to further finance capex, via things like ATMs.

And create a larger moat against newer DC developers.

text:
People genuinely don't understand this:

1. The global average IQ is 84. It's not the only factor but it's a major one.

2. Most successful ethnic groups have an average IQ of 100-105. The highest (Ashkenazi Jews) sit at about 107-112.

3. In order for a society to thrive, it needs to have an average IQ over 100. 103-105 or so seems to be the threshold.

At 103-105, you get peak England, the Scandinavian countries or peak Germany. At 100 you get France, and at 98 Spain.

The difference between global domination and also-ran is surprisingly small; just 2-3 IQ points. Another 4-5 and you're a basket case country like the Philippines or Bulgaria or modern Greece.

4. IQ can, within a population, shift solely through genetics, by 0.5-1.0 points per generation.

Social factors can magnify that effect by 5-7 points.

Consequently, the functional IQ of a population can change enough in one generation for a society to go from "world domination" to " basket case."

A more realistic outcome is that this can take 2 or 3 generations to happen. Well, that is what happened.

People often misinterpret the Flynn effect and think that IQs are rising but they're not. They're declining.

5. America is now too low IQ to maintain its position as world hegemon. More so, current birthrate trends have us rapidly entering not just "also ran" territory but "basket case."

The only reason we will stay on top is because we're absurdly rich compared to the rest of the world so we have a long way to fall before anyone catches us.

6. Successful countries become successful usually through a long process of breeding themselves into a higher IQ and then matching that with a social organization that maximizes it.

All it takes is one bad generation to destroy what took centuries to gain.

This is why today's Greeks aren't like the Greeks of golden age antiquity, and today's Romans aren't like the Romans of old. 

7. The highest IQ populations today are both not reproducing but also replacing themselves with low IQ populations.

Even Israel is only 1/3 Ashkenazi with lower IQ groups making up the majority of the country. It is worth noting that the Haredi (the cohort with the highest total fertility rate) is about 80% Ashkenazi, but I have no available data on their average IQ.

My point is that IQ does not appear to be an evolutionary advantage in the modern age and as such, it isn't being selected for.

This suggests that we're in a race against decline. We need to solve the IQ problem through technology before we simply run out of smart people living in functioning societies.

text:
Some thoughts on gas repricings and their impact.

Gas costs increasing for state operations does not mean they get proportionally more expensive, because the gas limit is increasing. What is the point of increasing the costs of these operations but then also increasing the gas limit? The point is scaling: many other operations are currently overpriced, and, by keeping their gas costs fixed and increasing the gas limit, the protocol recognizes this and increases the supply *of those operations only*. The state operations get *relatively* more expensive than these, but not necessarily more expensive in absolute terms. The overall story is that Ethereum is scaling: the gas limit is going up to 200M after being stuck at 30M for years, and most operations are benefitting from this increase in the gas supply (their gas cost is not changing). The ones that are not, like writing new state, will be subject to further scaling efforts in the future.

This is separate from the question of some smart contracts being affected by the repricings and related changes in the gas mechanism. Largely, the impact is on contracts that in one way or another have hardcoded gas costs or made assumptions about them not changing (e.g. if less than X gas remains then this branch reverts). This is unfortunate but somewhat inevitable when gas costs change, which I think is a fairly inevitable step in scaling Ethereum: the current gas costs are basically a decade old, some operations are much cheaper and some much more expensive than their gas cost implies!

It is also unlikely to be the last time they change, because over time gas costs can drift away from being representative of the actual cost of the operations, exactly what brought us to this point. However, this can be the last time that it affects contracts, if it becomes standard practice to not make assumptions about gas costs in the future. Getting this out of the way can be a step towards more immutability, especially if we work to clearly define which invariants should be guaranteed by the execution layer, so that contracts can be written on a solid foundation.

That said, the impact on contracts should have been more deeply investigated sooner, and perhaps more importantly communication about the change should have been more frequent and more direct. It has never been easier to run contract scans (I was able to find some affected contracts just with a few agents and the @SourcifyEth database), and I think it should be a standard practice for protocol upgrades in the future to run such scans with the latest spec, and that app developers should also be encouraged and given tooling to do so with their contracts.

When the combination of wealth and technology from high-IQ men reach a certain level, high-IQ labor becomes the bottleneck. At this point, wealthy industrialists, and indeed entire civilizations, face an irresistible temptation. 

They can double the size of the labor force, and half the real wages of high-IQ workers while building more, by putting all the women to work. 

And since women are instinctively compliant with social norms, all you have to do to accomplish this is convince women that society thinks careers are high-status, and children are low status. 

Both radical feminists and reactionaries both noticed some time ago that when you educate women, they stop breeding. 

Reactionaries thought this was because women are retarded, and they are genetically programmed to blow up society if you empower them. 

Feminists thought this was because having kids is horrible oppression, and women everywhere hate it, and have only ever done it because they forced into it by rape and sexual slavery, so the moment you empower them, they stop. 

Amusingly enough, these are actually the same idea, except written with snarl or purr words. 

And either way, this idea is wrong. Women don't stop having kids because you educate them. You could send them to finishing school for six years and teach them about matters animal, vegetable, and mineral, along with many cheerful facts about the square of the hypotenuse, and absolutely nothing would change. Except they'd be better conversationalists, and terrific at educating their kids. 

No, the reason women stop breeding when you educate them has nothing to do with education at all. 

It's because of what you're educating them FOR. 

You educate them to put them into the workforce, and once they are in the workforce, you have three things going on. 

First, they can build careers or have babies, they can't do both. Two, you just told them kids were for low-class, uneducated, barefoot-and-pregnant loser women living in shacks in rural Kansas. But most importantly, three, when they compete with men in the workplace, and have their own incomes, they lose respect for men. 

Women, whether you like it or not, whether I like it or not, only want to have babies with men they consider their superiors. 

If they work in the same workplaces as men, they consider those men to be equals, even if his job is "senior multithreaded kernel programmer" and hers is "project schedule kanban board den mother". 

So what you've done, what high-tech societies always do, is sacrifice their entire futures for one to three generations of increased shareholder value. 

But hey, we know some really great recipes for seedcornbread.
author: rootslashbin
quoted_text:
People genuinely don't understand this:

1. The global average IQ is 84. It's not the only factor but it's a major one.

2. Most successful ethnic groups have an average IQ of 100-105. The highest (Ashkenazi Jews) sit at about 107-112.

3. In order for a society to thrive, it needs to have an average IQ over 100. 103-105 or so seems to be the threshold.

At 103-105, you get peak England, the Scandinavian countries or peak Germany. At 100 you get France, and at 98 Spain.

The difference between global domination and also-ran is surprisingly small; just 2-3 IQ points. Another 4-5 and you're a basket case country like the Philippines or Bulgaria or modern Greece.

4. IQ can, within a population, shift solely through genetics, by 0.5-1.0 points per generation.

Social factors can magnify that effect by 5-7 points.

Consequently, the functional IQ of a population can change enough in one generation for a society to go from "world domination" to " basket case."

A more realistic outcome is that this can take 2 or 3 generations to happen. Well, that is what happened.

People often misinterpret the Flynn effect and think that IQs are rising but they're not. They're declining.

5. America is now too low IQ to maintain its position as world hegemon. More so, current birthrate trends have us rapidly entering not just "also ran" territory but "basket case."

The only reason we will stay on top is because we're absurdly rich compared to the rest of the world so we have a long way to fall before anyone catches us.

6. Successful countries become successful usually through a long process of breeding themselves into a higher IQ and then matching that with a social organization that maximizes it.

All it takes is one bad generation to destroy what took centuries to gain.

This is why today's Greeks aren't like the Greeks of golden age antiquity, and today's Romans aren't like the Romans of old. 

7. The highest IQ populations today are both not reproducing but also replacing themselves with low IQ populations.

Even Israel is only 1/3 Ashkenazi with lower IQ groups making up the majority of the country. It is worth noting that the Haredi (the cohort with the highest total fertility rate) is about 80% Ashkenazi, but I have no available data on their average IQ.

My point is that IQ does not appear to be an evolutionary advantage in the modern age and as such, it isn't being selected for.

This suggests that we're in a race against decline. We need to solve the IQ problem through technology before we simply run out of smart people living in functioning societies.

quoted_text:
Friedrich Hayek’s seminal book The Road to Serfdom is a warning against the dangers of government central planning, collectivism, and state control. It is a foundational text for modern libertarianism, but it also captured the imaginations of politicians and rival intellectuals.

John Maynard Keynes, Hayek’s chief macroeconomic rival, read the book while traveling to the Bretton Woods conference. Surprisingly, Keynes praised it as "a grand book," writing to Hayek that "morally and philosophically I find myself in agreement with virtually the whole of it." 

Milton Friedman championed the book as a masterpiece of political philosophy. He frequently wrote introductions for its anniversaries, noting that The Road to Serfdom was essential for demonstrating that economic freedom is an indispensable prerequisite for political freedom.

Margaret Thatcher viewed the text as a moral awakening during her university days. It provided her with the philosophical ammunition needed to challenge the British post-war socialist consensus, ultimately defining her premiership's commitment to privatization and deregulation.

George Orwell also famously reviewed the book, offering unique praise. Orwell agreed with Hayek's thesis that state collectivism naturally breeds tyranny, noting that central planning gives "a small minority of bureaucrats" unprecedented power.

Hayek’s central message transcends ideological boundaries: even when well-intentioned, government planning sets a society on a path toward totalitarianism, tyranny, and the destruction of personal liberty.

Anthropic 工程团队刚发了篇硬核长文《智能体记忆的组成部分》，揭秘了 Claude 5 系列背后的智能体记忆架构。

全篇干货比较多，我把核心机制总结成了 10 条：

1、智能体会在会话中快速标记重点，下线后利用空闲算力回溯原始日志，在后台异步完成纠错，去重和知识重组。这套仿生双系统，工作时实时记笔记，闲置时在后台“做梦”，是模仿人脑的海马体实时抓拍，和睡眠期皮层重组。

2、智能体记忆不等于上下文压缩，真正的 Agent 记忆是跨会话持久化，按需挂载的。它既不是修改模型权重，也不是单次窗口内的临时上下文，更不是为了续窗口而把旧对话缩成摘要。

3、在 CL-Bench 数据库测试中，Sonnet 4.6 只会在文件里记下未经验证的瞎猜，而 Opus 5/5.5 已能独立跑通“答错 → 提出假设 → 实验验证 → 写下避坑铁律”的完整闭环。

4、在《宝可梦红》1 万步测试中，Sonnet 3.7 把每次战斗和路人都建了档，写了 413 个文件，后期连着 17 步光整理文件不操作，只拿到 1 枚徽章。而 Fable 5 只维护 1 个全局看板（global.md）+ 9 个策略文件就拿下了 4 枚徽章，Opus 5.5 更是靠精简笔记直接通关。

5、当前金币、地图坐标每回合看一眼屏幕就知道，写进记忆只会迅速过期。好的记忆是存储不推演就会消失的规律，比如连扔 7 球抓不到鲤鱼王，Claude 摸索出连败 3 次后在菜单间多按 wait 改变节奏，写下规则后一球即中。

6、对 Opus 5 这类强模型，只需告知有记忆目录可以用，若硬性规定只准记失败教训，记忆加成反而暴跌。但对不爱主动读记忆 Sonnet 4.6，强制提示答题前先读记忆并验证，得分却会直接翻倍。

7、“做梦”能够打破死循环，过月见山时，Claude 错把西侧的宝可梦中心记在东侧，出门就以为已过山，连掉三次悬崖后心态崩溃放弃。开启后台“做梦”后，它拿笔记跟原始操作日志对账，发现方位记反，修正笔记后一把穿洞通关。

8、面对被收购公司 35 万份内部文件，Opus 5 在后台连续做梦 128 轮，自动建页、打双链、去重核查，编出内部 Wiki。用 Wiki 导航和搜索工具双管齐下，让跨文档并购问答准确率从 73% 跃升至 87%，每题还省下了 2 万 Token。

9、简单检索任务硬建 Wiki 不仅没增益，甚至会出现 Wiki 比原文档还庞大的反效果。高明的 Harness 必须分层，通过做梦把细节下沉，顶层每次仅预注入核心索引（如 Claude Code 每次只读 MEMORY.md 的前 200 行或 25KB），防止顶层指令膨胀稀释注意力。

10、审收购合同时，多个 Agent 同时改写同一张共享表格，因互相覆盖漏掉近 30% 事实（仅得 72 分）。团队让 Claude 做梦复盘，它自己把建库规则改成“每份合同独立建页 + 单 Agent 专责 + 核心条款逐字原话引用”，准确率直接拉满到 100%，二轮做梦还顺手修好了 9 处死链。

I don’t need AI-generated pictures to attack someone’s character.

An account can be operated from America, India, Pakistan, Vietnam, Indonesia, or anywhere else.

Just because someone questions your project doesn’t mean that account belongs to Digital Gold.

Just because someone exposes a problem doesn’t mean I sent them.

And just because someone tells you something you don’t want to hear doesn’t make them my affiliate.

STOP OBSESSING OVER WHO OWNS AN ACCOUNT.

START ANSWERING WHAT THAT ACCOUNT IS SHOWING YOU.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 NOW LET’S TALK ABOUT THE REAL PROBLEM.

It’s been more than SIX MONTHS since I walked away from your project.

SIX MONTHS.

And somehow, I’m still being blamed for your problems.

Let me remind you of something.

❌ If your project still hasn’t completed its promised launch, THAT IS NOT MY FAILURE.

❌ If your coin still hasn’t secured an exchange listing, THAT IS NOT MY FAILURE.

❌ If the overwhelming majority of your community is still waiting for KYC, THAT IS NOT MY FAILURE.

❌ If people cannot independently verify where their coins exist, THAT IS NOT MY FAILURE.

❌ If your team cannot clearly explain whether its token is on-chain, off-chain, or awaiting migration, THAT IS NOT MY FAILURE.

I LEFT YOUR PROJECT.

I DIDN’T TAKE YOUR BLOCKCHAIN WITH ME.

I DIDN’T TAKE YOUR EXCHANGE LISTING WITH ME.

I DIDN’T TAKE YOUR KYC SYSTEM WITH ME.

So stop using my name as an explanation for things your own leadership is responsible for delivering.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨 AND TO THOSE WHO KEEP POSTING MY PICTURES…

Some of you previously worked with me.

Some of you received money from me.

Some of you had financial obligations that I chose not to pursue.

And now I see people using my own pictures to attack me.

Interesting.

But here’s the difference between us.

YOU USE PICTURES.

I USE EVIDENCE.

YOU MAKE ACCUSATIONS.

I ASK FOR VERIFIABLE FACTS.

YOU ATTACK THE PERSON.

I QUESTION THE PRODUCT.

You cannot make yourself successful by trying to destroy someone else’s reputation.

You cannot turn an unfinished promise into a completed achievement by insulting a former team member.

And you cannot manufacture credibility with AI-generated images.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 HERE’S A BETTER IDEA.

Instead of searching for my pictures, go to your leadership.

Ask your owner.

Ask your CEO.

Ask your technical team.

WHERE IS THE BLOCKCHAIN?

WHERE IS THE VERIFIABLE TOKEN SUPPLY?

WHERE IS THE EXCHANGE LISTING?

WHAT IS THE ACTUAL KYC COMPLETION RATE?

WHERE IS THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTING THE PROMISES MADE TO THE COMMUNITY?

And if someone publishes false information about your project, respond with documents, blockchain records, and independently verifiable evidence.

NOT MY FACE.

NOT MY FAMILY.

NOT AN AI-GENERATED PICTURE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Let me tell you something else.

People criticize my projects every single day.

Some call them scams.

Some question my decisions.

Some attack the technology.

Do I spend my nights hunting down their photographs?

Do I drag their families into it?

Do I automatically accuse every critical account of working for a competitor?

NO.

Because criticism is part of building something publicly.

If someone makes a valid point, I should address it.

If someone makes a false accusation, I should challenge it with evidence.

THAT IS HOW ACCOUNTABILITY WORKS.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚠️ ONE FINAL MESSAGE.

Stop sending me accusations at 3 AM, 4 AM, and 5 AM.

Stop attaching my name to every account that challenges you.

Stop confusing personal attacks with technical arguments.

And stop believing that bringing someone else down will somehow lift you up.

IF YOU HAVE THE TRUTH, USE IT TO SILENCE ME.

Show the evidence.

Show the blockchain.

Show the transactions.

Show the completed promises.

Show the results.

BECAUSE THE TRUTH DOESN’T NEED MY PERMISSION TO EXIST.

And remember this:

I HAVE BEEN GONE FOR OVER SIX MONTHS.

IF YOU STILL NEED DIGITAL GOLD TO EXPLAIN WHY YOUR PROJECT HASN’T DELIVERED, THEN DIGITAL GOLD IS NOT YOUR BIGGEST PROBLEM.

Your biggest problem is the questions your own community is still asking.

FIX YOUR PROJECT.

ANSWER YOUR COMMUNITY.

STOP HIDING BEHIND MY NAME.

I have my own work to do.

And I intend to keep doing it.

— DIGITAL GOLD

Why I'm using @RenzoFinance for farming funding and paying fees for this:

So, I pay 5 bps as a builder fee. For this, I get:

- Simple UI with PnL bar charts and statistics
- Automatic exit if funding is net negative over the last 5 (or whatever) days (it's custom)
- If ADL closes part of the position, Renzo sells the matching spot to keep the position hedged
- Getting to choose and change my risk level, i.e., leverage and value
- Automatic shrink of both legs when the token is within 10% of liquidation, restoring the safety buffer

Do I give up custody in order to farm? No.

Renzo has my trading key, which cannot send, withdraw, or change its own permissions.

Could I have directly used HL? Yeah.

But I'm okay with paying 5 bps a tx so someone else could manage my position and I wouldn't worry.

text:
I am the Deputy Program Manager for Rewards for Justice at the State Department’s Bureau of Diplomatic Security. As of Friday night, I am offering $20 million for something the President blew up.

We pay people to tell us things. Since 1984 the United States has paid “in excess of $250 million to more than 125 people,” about $2 million a secret. It is the only honest price list in Washington. I keep it laminated, on a lanyard, next to my badge.

Our office is in Rosslyn, across the Potomac from Foggy Bottom, in the kind of beige federal tower where hope goes to get its parking validated. Outside my door hang the old posters, framed like family photos. In the 90s we printed them on matchbooks, because a man lighting a cigarette has 4 seconds to reconsider his life. Ramzi Yousef, $2 million, paid. Then the 1 we don’t discuss. Osama bin Laden. $25 million. Offered for 10 years. Never collected. The Navy found him a mile from Pakistan’s national military academy. 1 mile. Nobody called. Not 1 cadet. We keep him up the way a family keeps a photo of the uncle who drove the boat into the dock.

Let me tell you how it actually works. The world imagines a war room. It is, I promise you, an inbox with a budget and a bowl of leftover Halloween candy nobody will admit to restocking. Tips arrive by Signal, Telegram, WhatsApp, and a Tor address so long it looks like a cat sat on a keyboard and achieved enlightenment. Our website promises “RFJ reads every tip we receive.” Every tip. I want you to remember that sentence. It is about to ruin my life.

In June 2025, B-2s flew 18 hours from Missouri and dropped 14 bombs of 30,000 pounds each on Fordow and Natanz. The President addressed the nation: “Iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated.” Completely. Totally. 2 adverbs guarding 1 verb like Secret Service agents around a man who has already left the building. He has said it, in some form, for 17 months. I believe him. I believe him with my whole chest and my TS/SCI.

So on Friday the poster went through clearance. In this town every document is “cleared” by every office that might be blamed for it. Mine was cleared by 11 offices, 2 bureaus, the 7th floor and a lawyer who only communicates in tracked changes. Nobody cleared it for meaning.

At 7:15 p.m. I published a reward of up to $20 million “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, “including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel,” or “the movement of any of the above.”

The movement.

Of the obliterated facilities.

Somewhere in Iran, a pile of rubble has packed a carry-on and is trying to get a slot at Reagan National.

7:19 p.m. First tip. “It’s under the mountain. You bombed it. I watched it on TV.” Technically correct. Ineligible. Information must be new.

7:22 p.m. A man in Fairfax reports that the nuclear program is his neighbor’s satellite dish. He has reported this to us 46 times since 2019. Every time he has been wrong. Tonight, for the first time, I couldn’t prove it.

7:25 p.m. CENTCOM posts the reward.

Minutes later. Piers Morgan: “WTF????”

4 question marks. I printed it. I framed it next to bin Laden. It is the most rigorous review the reward ever received. 11 offices produced 0 question marks. The 7th floor produced 0 question marks. A man who was fired as a newspaper editor over fake photos from the Iraq war produced 4 in under a minute, for free, without a clearance. He knows a doctored picture when he sees one. I have nominated him for a TS/SCI. The background check will take 14 months. He will be faster than the program.

7:58 p.m. Someone else asks, “The one that’s destroyed?” I have no talking points for this. I draft a response. It goes to clearance. It is still in clearance. It will be in clearance when I retire.

8:15 p.m. 1,100 tips. A woman says she saw a centrifuge at the Costco in Pentagon City, spinning near the rotisserie chickens. A lobbyist on K Street says he knows exactly where the program is and will tell me over lunch at the Palm, if I’m buying. A Hill staffer says it’s in the SCIF in the Capitol Visitor Center basement and nobody can check because nobody’s allowed to bring their phone.

8:40 p.m. The rubble files a tip. Through Tor. It says it is “open to new opportunities” and has relocated to Dubai, where it now operates a smoothie bar called Fordow Fresh. It requests possible relocation to Arlington. I flag it as credible. It is the most self-aware tip we have received since 1984.

9:02 p.m. I reread our fine print. To justify the reward, we cite a 2025 report that Iran was enriching uranium to 60 percent. We published a missing-person poster with a photo from last year, which is what you do when the kid has grown a beard and you’d rather not ask how. The same paragraph says the IAEA has lost “continuity of knowledge” of Iran’s centrifuges. Philosophers spent 3,000 years on the problem of knowledge. The IAEA solved it with 1 verb. Lost. Officially, the centrifuges are obliterated and we have also lost them. In Washington we call that “pre-decisional.” Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays they are obliterated. Tuesdays and Thursdays they are missing. Weekends they are a smoothie bar.

10:30 p.m. 3,000 tips. 400 of them are just the word “obliterated” with a question mark. 1 is from an IP address in Moscow that says “lol.” I flag it as the most honest tip of the night.

11:58 p.m. Someone adds me to a Signal group called “Houthi PC small group 2.” I recognize 0 of the 14 members. Somebody posts a map. Somebody posts a fire emoji. Somebody posts “who added the State guy.” I leave. They add me back. Yes, that Signal. In 2025 the editor of The Atlantic was added to the original and got the strike plans before the Houthis did. It remains the fastest interagency process in American history. Every office was in the loop. So was a magazine.

12:40 a.m. A colonel calls from the Pentagon to ask whether bombing it again counts as a tip.

1:12 a.m. An anonymous message, in perfect English: “I am a centrifuge. I spin at 60 percent. I have been obliterated since June 2025 and I have never felt more alive. Is the relocation to Northern Virginia? Is there a Sweetgreen? Asking for 6,000 of my friends.” I put my head on the desk, directly on a fun-size Snickers.

And this is where it all comes apart. At 2:00 a.m., I reread our payout rules. To pay a reward, I have to certify the information is accurate. To certify it’s accurate, I have to certify the program exists. And to certify the program exists, I would have to certify, in writing, on State Department letterhead, that the 2 adverbs were wrong. That memo would need clearance. There is no office in this government that will clear it.

So the reward can never be paid. The only way to collect $20 million is to prove the President was mistaken, and nobody in this town is authorized to say that out loud. I have created the safest money in the federal budget. It is a $20 million bill locked inside a box, and the key is a Truth Social post.

3:15 a.m. The colonel calls back. If they bomb it again, can the Air Force claim the reward? I tell him the reward is for information. He says, “That’s what the bombs are.”

4:02 a.m. I submit a tip. To myself. Through Tor. “The program is wherever it was before you obliterated it.” I review it. I reject it. Information must be new. I appeal. I deny my own appeal. I send myself a “per my last email.”

6:30 a.m. The rubble replies to my rejection with a job offer. Shift manager, Fordow Fresh, Dubai. Dental. 401(k). Possible relocation. It’s the first offer of relocation anyone in this story has actually received, and it came from the rubble. It does not require a continuing resolution.

Every war produces 2 pieces of paper. A banner that says it’s over, and a poster that says we’re still looking. In 2003 the banner said “Mission Accomplished” over weapons we swore were there and never found. In 2025 we swore the weapons were gone, and now we’re paying to find them. History rhymes. This time it rhymes backward, and I’m the one holding the stapler.

The second war, this year’s, the one that sent tankers into mines in Hormuz and gas to the highest Election Day price ever recorded, the one the President now agrees cost his party Congress on Tuesday, has produced as its final deliverable a laminated flyer, which I stapled at dawn to a light pole on Wilson Boulevard. LOST: 1 nuclear program. Last seen obliterated. Answers to “60 percent.” Shy around inspectors. Do not approach. Do not feed. If found, do not tell the President.

It’s 9 a.m. Saturday. 9,400 tips. RFJ reads every tip we receive. I have read 9,400 tips. I have eaten 11 fun-size Snickers. My wife has asked if I’m being relocated. I said, “possibly.”

Up on Wilson Boulevard the ginkgoes have dropped their fruit and the whole city smells like a gym bag. I’m on the Orange Line now, standing on the right, lanyard still on, flyers under my arm. The train is holding at Foggy Bottom. Of course it is. Somewhere a very powerful man is telling a camera, again, that Iran’s program was obliterated. Good. Then the money is safe. Bin Laden’s $25 million sat on that wall for 10 years. This one will sit there forever.

Somewhere under a mountain, a centrifuge is reading this.

We just want to talk.

Tips welcome. Signal preferred. Please check who else is in the chat.

author: tunguz
quoted_text:
While you sleep, your brain's white matter is charging up like a battery

Myelin, the insulation around your nerve fibers, has been considered a passive structural component that speeds up signals. A new hypothesis from @FScholkmann and colleagues proposes it's actually an energy storage system that fills up during sleep and powers your neurons throughout the day.

The paper, published in Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology, presents a radical reimagining of what myelin does beyond speeding up electrical signals along nerves.

What is myelin?

Myelin is the fatty sheath that wraps around nerve fibers like insulation around electrical wires. It's produced by specialized cells called oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system and makes up about 40% of your brain's volume.

Traditionally, myelin's job has been simple: speed up nerve signals and provide structural support. This new hypothesis suggests it does something far more dynamic.

The proton capacitor hypothesis

The researchers propose myelin functions as a proton capacitor, meaning it stores energy in the form of protons (hydrogen ions) that accumulate during sleep and get released during wakefulness to produce ATP, the cell's energy currency.

Think of it like a rechargeable battery. During sleep, myelin charges up by accumulating protons. During wakefulness, those protons flow through ATP synthase enzymes embedded in myelin, generating the energy neurons need to function.

The mechanism involves two abundant myelin proteins:

Myelin basic protein (MBP) sits between myelin layers and contains amino acids (lysine, arginine, histidine) that can absorb and hold protons. It functions as the energy storage component.

Proteolipid protein (PLP) spans the myelin membrane and contains serine and threonine amino acids that form efficient proton conductors, creating pathways for protons to flow from storage sites to ATP synthase.

How the charging cycle works

During sleep, your myelin is actively storing energy. Specialized molecules in myelin pump protons (think of them as tiny charged particles) into storage proteins, like filling up a battery. During this phase, no energy is being used, just stored.

When you wake up, the system switches into discharge mode. Those stored protons flow through protein channels to enzymes that convert them into ATP, your cells' usable energy form. This ATP travels through tiny tunnels called gap junctions directly into nerve fibers, where it powers your brain's activity.

The researchers calculated that the amount of protons a small cube of myelin can hold matches exactly what your brain would need during 8 hours of wakefulness. The storage capacity and the daily demand align.

The molecular sleep switch

A naturally occurring molecule called oleamide acts as the on/off switch for this system.

Throughout your waking hours, oleamide gradually accumulates in your brain. When it reaches a certain level, it closes those gap junctions, the tunnels that deliver ATP from myelin to nerve fibers. Once the tunnels close, your neurons can't access the energy supply. Neural activity drops. You get sleepy.

With the delivery system shut down, myelin switches from discharge mode to charging mode. While you sleep, oleamide slowly breaks down. When enough of it clears out, the gap junctions reopen, ATP starts flowing to neurons again, and you wake up.

This explains why you can't just decide to stay awake indefinitely. As oleamide builds up during the day, it eventually forces the system offline whether you want it to or not. Sleep isn't optional, it's a programmed metabolic requirement driven by molecular accumulation.

How myelin produces energy without the usual machinery

Here's where it gets strange: myelin can make ATP (cellular energy) even though it doesn't contain the typical power plants that cells use to generate energy.

Normally, structures called mitochondria produce nearly all of a cell's ATP. But myelin has very few, if any, complete mitochondria. So how does it make energy?

The researchers propose that mitochondria send small cargo packages carrying energy-producing equipment to the myelin. These packages fuse with myelin membranes and drop off the machinery, allowing myelin to produce ATP on its own.

Think of it like getting a portable generator delivered to a remote cabin. You don't need a full power plant on site, just the essential equipment to generate electricity locally.

The bigger the battery, the less time spent charging

The researchers examined 23 different mammal species and discovered something remarkable: animals with more white matter (the brain tissue that's 95% myelin) need less sleep.

Here's the pattern:

• Bats have tiny brains with minimal white matter and sleep 20 hours a day
• Humans have moderate white matter and sleep 8 hours a day
• Elephants have massive white matter and sleep just 3.5 hours a day

The logic is straightforward. More myelin means greater energy storage capacity. With a bigger battery, you need less time plugged in to fully recharge.
The pattern suggests that more myelin provides greater energy storage capacity, reducing the time needed to recharge. Less myelin means longer recharging periods are required.

This relationship also appears within humans across the lifespan. White matter volume peaks between ages 30-50, the same period when sleep duration reaches its minimum. Both follow inverted U-shaped curves over the human lifespan.

Even sex differences align: women have less white matter than men and require more sleep on average.

Experimental support

The hypothesis draws on experimental work showing:

• Isolated myelin vesicles consume oxygen and synthesize ATP via oxidative phosphorylation
• Myelin vesicles exposed to NADH retain an energy charge that's later used for ATP synthesis when ADP and phosphate are added
• Longer exposure to NADH produces more ATP in subsequent phases
• This matches the predicted two-phase system: charging during simulated sleep, discharge during simulated wakefulness

Sleep deprivation studies show myelin thickness decreases when animals are kept awake, consistent with discharge without adequate recharging time.

Marathon runners show notable reductions in myelin after intense physical activity, suggesting the energy reserves get depleted during sustained neural and physical exertion.

Key takeaways:

• Myelin may function as a proton battery, storing energy during sleep and releasing it during wakefulness

• Two myelin proteins (MBP and PLP) form a coupled system: one stores protons, the other conducts them to ATP synthase

• Sleep duration correlates with white matter volume across 23 mammalian species

• Oleamide, a natural sleep inducer, closes the gap junctions that deliver ATP from myelin to axons

• Myelin contains functional mitochondrial components delivered via mitochondrial-derived vesicles

• The human brain requires approximately 8 hours to fully recharge myelin's proton storage capacity

• Sleep deprivation leads to measurable myelin degradation

Limitations and open questions

This remains a hypothesis requiring direct experimental validation in living systems. The calculations provide plausibility but don't prove the mechanism operates as proposed.

Key questions:
• Can proton accumulation and discharge be measured directly in myelin during sleep/wake cycles?
• Does blocking this proposed system prevent normal sleep function?
• How does this mechanism integrate with other established functions of sleep?
• Can therapeutic interventions targeting this system improve sleep quality or neurological function?

The challenge is that protons moving between membrane-bound buffers without entering free solution is difficult to measure experimentally.

Why this matters

If validated, this hypothesis fundamentally reframes our understanding of sleep. Rather than viewing sleep as a period when the brain passively recovers, it positions sleep as an active metabolic phase when the brain's white matter systematically stores energy for the next waking period.

It also elevates myelin from a passive structural element to an active metabolic organizer that administers energy distribution to neurons.

The framework could explain why myelin disorders often involve fatigue and why conditions affecting white matter integrity produce cognitive deficits even when gray matter remains intact.

The identification of oleamide as the molecular switch controlling this cycle points to a natural compound that's been overlooked as a potential sleep therapeutic despite decades of evidence.

The convergence of structural data (protein composition and positioning), metabolic data (oxygen consumption and ATP synthesis in myelin), molecular data (oleamide and gap junctions), and cross-species data (white matter volume and sleep duration) creates a compelling case that myelin plays a previously unrecognized role in sleep energetics.

Whether this represents the primary function of sleep or one component of a multi-system process remains to be determined. But the hypothesis provides testable predictions and a mechanistic framework for understanding the metabolic foundations of the sleep-wake cycle.

text:
Initial findings and some clarifications on the Google/Apple login incident.

First, to those affected: I'm sorry, and we're doing everything we can.

1. This was not a hack of Keplr's code. The incident originated at Web3Auth, a provider Keplr uses.

All other Keplr accounts, secret recovery phrases, and hardware wallets are safe.

2. It appears that this affects some, but not all, accounts created with Google or Apple login. Our early estimate is about 20% of them affected.

3. We're working with the Web3Auth/MetaMask team on tracking and recovery.

I don't want to be overly optimistic, but it appears only a fraction of that 20% has actually been exploited, and the remaining accounts may be recoverable. More on this soon.

Personally, this one hits hard. People who created their wallet with a Google or Apple ID are likely crypto beginners and the crypto curious.

It's been a tough few years for the Cosmos ecosystem, and this doesn't help.

To everyone who reached out with help and support: thank you 🙏 It means a lot.

I'll be back with a more concrete, detailed update.

Thank you all for your patience.

text:
What to farm after Lighter and Variational? My pick is RISEx. Here’s why.

I’ve been with the project from the beginning and farmed Season 0. The interface is clean, and the books have been fairly deep on the markets I’ve traded.

Here’s what keeps me interested.

1. RWA is already a meaningful part of the business.

The team’s October recap reported:

→ $14.63B monthly volume, up 33%
→ $3.65B RWA volume, up 45%
→ $87.4M peak open interest, up 22%
RWA accounted for roughly a quarter of total trading volume.
October recap

2. The funding design deserves attention.

RISEx lists a zero base interest component for RWA markets, with a dampener that absorbs small price deviations.

Funding can still turn positive or negative. But when holding positions beyond a quick scalp, carry costs matter.

Funding mechanics

3. The orderbook lives inside the EVM.

Orders, matching, margin and settlement execute in the same environment as other applications.

Developers can build strategies where a trade and another DeFi action complete together—or the whole transaction reverts. That opens possibilities for vaults, lending integrations and automated hedging.

Architecture

4. Spot is progressing. Zero fees have been teased.

On October 27, cofounder Sam Battenally said he had tested spot trading end-to-end on the RISEx testnet.

Earlier, he posted:

“No fees, better spreads and more assets.”

Spot was a testnet update, and the fee teaser included no launch date or conditions. Both are milestones I’m watching.

Spot test · Fee teaser

5. The points runway.

Season 1: Ignite started on July 20, with 200,000 points allocated weekly. Scoring considers more than trading volume, and the weights can change.

The team says the season will end no later than Q2 2027, tied to major product milestones.

One detail I like: 100% of RISEx Points go to users—traders, liquidity providers and builder-code integrators. That means the points allocation, not 100% of the token supply.

Points programme

My current farming cost is below $1 per point. That makes this an interesting window for me while the more popular perp DEXs have everyone’s attention.

My bet is that attention eventually rotates from Lighter and Variational to RISEx. I’d rather already know the product when the crowd arrives.

text:
全体起立，Vercel推出的agent-desktop现在才是Agent操控电脑的真神。

它是 Vercel Labs 的开源项目，Apache-2.0 协议，GitHub 已经有 1.8 万 star，仓库地址在下面

它是一个命令行工具，让 Claude Code、Codex 这类 Agent 直接操作你电脑上的 App：点按钮、填表单、打字、切菜单、读界面。

之前大部分 Computer Use 的做法是截图，再让模型猜该点哪个坐标。慢，还容易点歪。

agent-desktop 不截图。它直接读系统的无障碍树（就是读屏软件用的那套接口），给界面上每个按钮、输入框编一个号，Agent 按编号去点、去输入。

最关键的一点：它默认不动你的鼠标，也不把窗口切到前台。

Agent 在后台操作电脑的时候，你可以照常刷微信、写东西，两边互不干扰。真要用物理鼠标键盘时，再加 --headed。

我在自己的 Mac 上实测了一轮：

- 打开系统设置，读完整个界面 0.3 秒左右
- 点击「蓝牙」0.17 秒，页面切过去了，设备列表也读出来了
- 给不在前台的文本编辑输入一段中英文加数字，0.15 秒，读回来一字不差
- Electron 写的 App 也能读，侧栏、对话列表的文字都拿得到
- 整个过程我一直在用微信，前台一次都没被抢

我原来用 LCU，它要借 ChatGPT 桌面端里面的运行时，ChatGPT 一更新就可能坏，也卡过。今天卸了，换成 agent-desktop。

几个让我决定换的点：

1. 不依赖任何 App，npm 一装就能用
2. macOS（Intel 和 M 芯片）、Windows、Linux 都支持
3. 自己不带模型，任何能跑命令的 Agent 都能用，也可以当 MCP 服务接进去
4. 60 个命令，窗口管理、剪贴板、通知、菜单栏都包了

安装就两步：

npm install -g agent-desktop
agent-desktop permissions --guide

第二条在 Mac 上会一步步引导你打开辅助功能权限。

然后在 AGENTS.md 或 CLAUDE.md 里加一句：

Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run
`agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them.

你的 Agent 就会用了。

仓库：https://t.co/LqimXMvIZ6

text:
Seeing @EFDevcon 2027 announced in Lisbon means a lot personally. But more than anything, it feels like a moment to celebrate everyone who’s been building the community here for the past decade 🇵🇹

Portugal has a very special place in web3. I’ve genuinely lost count of how many amazing companies, projects, events and communities have roots here.

It’s crazy how consistently we rank among the top 5–10 countries represented at the @ETHGlobal events, given how small we are compared to so many of the other countries attending.

That doesn’t really happen only by accident.

Thousands of locals, nomads, expats have built this community over the years, including many who’ve since moved into other frontier technologies but played a pivotal role in getting us this far.

Also, Portugal isn’t only just Lisbon. Porto, Braga, Coimbra, Algarve, Madeira and many other places have incredible blockchain and student communities that will be part of this moment too.

To name a few:
@BragaBlockchain @Coimblockchain @eth_porto @ABCAlgarve @blockchain_made

Lastly, this will be the first Devcon in a Portuguese-speaking country. Portuguese is the world’s fifth most spoken native language, and I’d love to see us use this opportunity to connect the communities across all the countries and regions that speak it. 🇵🇹 🇧🇷 🇦🇴 🇲🇿 🇨🇻 🇬🇼 🇸🇹 🇹🇱 🇬🇶

A lot more could be said, but mostly I’m incredibly happy and thankful that Ethereum is bringing its flagship event to our country. Can’t wait to see everyone next year.

And there’s an extra reason this one feels special: ETHGlobal turns 10 in 2027 and we will be celebrating across the world, topping it off in Lisbon with a conference and our last in-person hackathon of the 2027 circuit.

Thank you Ethereum Foundation and Devcon team. And thank you everyone who made this journey with us. Couldn’t be more excited for 2027!

The story keeps getting crazier. To recap everything that has been reported so far: 

- The US intelligence community discovered that Jensen Huang, the CEO of the largest company in the world, was sleeping with Alice Huang, a Chinese spy and an executive at Megaspeed. (FT)
- Multiple independent investigations have concluded that Megaspeed is likely a Chinese cutout, which helps Chinese companies access AI chips or circumvent export controls. (NYT and Bloomberg) 
- The US intelligence community also concluded that Alice Huang’s goal was to convince Jensen to lobby the U.S. government to loosen export controls on advanced AI chips. (NYT)
- The intelligence community relayed this information to “a small group of top US government officials” earlier this year. (FT)
- Over the last year, Jensen Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to loosen export controls on advanced chips. @BISgov has done so, not only by permitting the export of H200 chips to China, but also not enforcing export controls that would have required a license for exports of the most advanced Blackwell chips to Megaspeed and Southeast Asia.
- Although @CommerceGov leadership was presumably briefed on this information by the U.S. intelligence community, @BISgov has taken no actions to tighten controls on Megaspeed or Southeast Asia. 
- Megaspeed remains a preferred cloud partner of Nvidia, and continues to receive Nvidia Blackwell chips despite employing a Chinese spy who reportedly is romantically engaged with the CEO of Nvidia. 
- Tens of billions of dollars worth of AI chips have been exported to Southeast Asia this year alone, and Malaysia and Singapore are now two of the four largest importers of AI chips in the world. 

What is going on here??? We need answers. The question of who gets the most advanced AI chips in the world is literally the defining strategic question of our time. And not only does it seem like the MSS may be directly influencing the debate on export controls in the United States, but also @CommerceGov is refusing to listen to the warnings of the IC on this issue. What is a POSSIBLE good explanation for why Megaspeed is still receiving chips? Why is there not a license requirement for AI chip shipments to all of Southeast Asia? This is beyond strange at this point. 

The fallout from this story will be massive. Obviously, the motivations underpinning Nvidia’s policy views opposing export controls must now all be questioned. But also, how did @BISgov sit on this information and has still taken no actions? We need answers.

Calif CEO @XorNinja says cybersecurity has no playbook for stopping 1,000 AI agents attacking a network simultaneously, even if defenders can detect them:

"Attackers always adapt faster and earlier than defenders. Even the AI companies themselves don't have great security."

"Imagine you enter a cage fight, but you are blindfolded and the other guy stay in the dark, and every once in a while they would come out and punch you and then disappear."

"How could you win that fight?"

"I was at Google and that's basically the mantra at Google. In security you have three things: prevention, detection, and response. And Google accept that prevention gonna fail at scale."

"You can detect them, but does it help you if you find that there's maybe a thousand agents hacking you right now inside your network? How can you contain them without a full shutdown of your system?"

"This actually requires defense to come up with a new paradigm. I haven't seen anybody come up with a good idea here. We're not there yet."

The next shift in finance will not be a new token. It will be the removal of the human treasurer.

By September 30, 2027, an autonomous AI agent will manage over fifty million dollars in live DeFi treasury assets without a single human multisig approval.

Right now, agents are stuck on testnets. Protocols do not trust them because language models hallucinate and code is unforgiving.

Once the math is guaranteed, human committees cannot compete. An agent rebalances a yield strategy across fifty chains in seconds. A human vote takes days.

text:
There's a debate in ed-tech circles about how important "conceptual understanding" is.

The against camp points out that conceptual understanding is hard to define, let alone measure.

The pro camp says that without it, teaching degrades into memorizing question-answer pairs with no knowledge of how those facts fit into the world.

There is a third way of looking at this dillema.

Conceptual MIS-understanding is easy to define and test, and is consequential if undiagnosed.

All you have to do is get the student to recite/explain things in their own words, then give corrective feedback when they give invalid reasoning.

Thanks to LLMs, this is reliable and scalable, and our AI Tutors rely heavily on this.

When a student reasons correctly, you cannot be sure if they memorized the reasoning chain or genuinely understood it.

But if they reason incorrectly, you can provide high-impact feedback.

This provides a lot more signal than simply checking if the student gave the correct answer because good test takers know how to hack probabilities in answering questions (and some do it unconciously).

text:
The interesting thing about AI agents is that as a theoretical matter, their inference can kind of run anywhere. AI is one of the few areas of technology that isn’t *as* sensitive to latency back to the user. 

Long running agents are now going to be the norm, which means it’s ok to send off work to an AI factory somewhere and that work can essentially be largely done within that remote data center and a final result spit back to the user. The data can pass into these systems in an encrypted manner, be combed through by agents, and then disregarded right after. 

And because the economic value of the task is so high relative to the latency sensitivity (eg getting back $500 in value from an automated task, but it takes an extra second to return), you don’t have to have the inference to be particularly close to the user. 

Also, because inference is a temporary process with no sensitive data needing to be stored long term where the inference is happening, you can effectively treat AI factories as ephemeral systems, changing some of the data residency dynamics slightly.

Combined, this means you have more flexibility in where you can begin to deploy AI data centers. This is both a huge economic opportunity for the states or countries (or space) that want to take advantage of this fact. And it’s a loss to the states or countries that decide to forgo the opportunity.

text:
Frontier cyber agents are getting better at two things at once: finding vulnerabilities and staying inside the rules researchers set. The harder part is no longer just model capability; it’s where the system still fails once the model is good enough to act.

1) OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, up from 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and 40.3% recall on a new offensive web vuln-discovery eval vs 32.0% for GPT-6 Astra. They also report 99.93% out-of-scope avoidance without the deployment prompt, and 100% with it. The release also claims it helped develop 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits and identify 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulns. These are vendor-reported numbers, so the takeaway is capability is rising, but the claims still need independent validation.

2) Signed but Not Safe shows what happens at the handoff layer in multi-agent systems. In a preregistered study, signed requirement manifests cut unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% with Qwen3-8B, and the verifier beat an LLM checker on the same trajectories. But signing only protects requirements in transit: when the orchestrator extracted the wrong requirement before signing, the signature faithfully preserved the mistake. The residual risk is extraction.

3) SPILLWAY makes a similar point for tool-using agents. It separates target admission from sanitization, using deterministic checks on typed tool returns plus a sanitizer that strips injected instructions before the model reads them. Across the tested backbones and suites, in-scope attack success went to zero. Its limitation is explicit: it covers identity targets, depends on declared tool roles, and still leaves some cases to a judge and delegation rules.

Taken together, these are not proofs of a universal shift, but they do show where the practical trust boundary is moving in evaluated agent systems: provenance, extraction, typed tool outputs, and deterministic enforcement around the loop.

text:
Should you buy a 128GB MacBook Pro for Local AI?  I did the math before ordering a PROLED M5 Max MacBook Pro so you don't have to.

I also checked what people have been saying since March about the previous-gen MacBook Pro (same chip & memory options, just an older design).

1) 128GB instead of 48GB of unified memory costs about as much as generating 1.7 billion tokens of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at peak API prices, and apparently isn’t enough to run frontier-level models locally (at least not ones that can reliably handle complex agentic workflows). But if you’re buying a MacBook Pro anyway, local AI is likely the main thing that justifies splurging on the RAM.

2) Qwen3.8-Flash-Next seems to be the local AI darling of the M5 Max MacBook Pro set. It’s a 125B MoE model that people report getting anywhere from 70-128 tokens/sec out of, depending on the runtime they use. But depending on how you get Qwen3.8-Flash-Next running, it either uses ~70-75GB of your 128GB (for runtimes that keep its n-gram table on the SSD) or 100GB+ (for fully off the shelf 4-bit versions), which may limit what else you can do with your Mac.

3) For smaller models like Qwen3.8 27B, you can get 19 tokens/sec with vanilla MLX or 46-77 with speculative decoding (again, runtime-dependent). DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (552B) doesn't fit in 128GB of memory and one person who forced it to run reports 2-3 tokens/sec.

4) You could get an NVIDIA machine with about half the memory bandwidth for the same (or even less!) money, like the RTX Spark-based Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (300GB/s) or 128GB DGX Spark (273GB/s; the M5 Max MacBook Pro has 614GB/s), but at least one person with both an M5 Max MacBook Pro and RTX Spark said the former was much easier to get working.

5) One owner tried cranking the fan speed from 55% to 80%, which dropped temperatures from 90°C to 75°C and bumped prompt-processing speed by ~20%. And early reviews of the PROLED MacBook Pro suggest its improved cooling will let the M5 Max sustain higher power than before. But if you’re hoping to run agents overnight on your MacBook Pro, note that you could get a Mac Studio with the same chip for 17% less money.

6) One M5 Max MacBook Pro user is @yossy_lexiq, who uses local LLMs to power their law practice in Japan so that none of their client work is sent to the cloud. They built that stack on mtplx from @Youssofal_.

7) Local AI runs in airplane mode! When two of the frontier models were unavailable for (almost!) three weeks in June, Local AI was still available.

So buy a MacBook Pro if you want to bring your LLMs with you wherever you go, buy a Mac Studio (or API tokens!) if they’ll be sitting still.

text:
We should continue towards Glam activation asap.

A lot of research went into Glam's strategy to increase opcode gas prices for state creation.

It seems fair to say that the timing of this debate is irrelevant as to its correctness or rightness for eth and our users... Yet, why did some of us (eg. quoted author who is an ef board member) only start looking in detail at Glam EIPs eg. after testnet forks started? This isn't a personal attack, it's an observation that there's a collective responsibility-- for OP, for me, for all of us-- to steward fork strategy at the right times in the process.

imo ethereum's commitments to apps do not extend to gas pricing, or to total ETH fee levels, or to USD fees. And also not to opcode pricing or gas introspection that depends on those prices. We guarantee maximally credibly neutral, maximally live access to the correct state transition function. Those guarantees imply that we always use a neutral pricing mechanism to clear congestion wherever possible. However, pricing opcodes can't use a neutral mechanism, we need to pick magic number opcode gas prices. Some of our best people researched this extensively and picked updated magic numbers, and that's something imo we should stick with now and continue our larger plans that are on track to grow to global ubiquity.

The good news and practical reality may be that the explosion of blockspace supply from 60M to 200M gas limit seems likely to absolutely crater the L1 gas price. It will take time for demand to grow to meet the new supply, including from net new entrants (eg. GENIUS and institutions), induced demand from lower prices, and the coming next gen of return-to-mainnet-type eth native apps. 

By the time L1 blockspace demand catches up, we will be exploding supply again as we get closer to the full lean eth vision. That's eth's vision: postquantum and postAI ETH SoV, supported by ethereum's hypergrowing capacity, which is supported by best-in-class security and formal verification.

Looking back, it's unfortunate that we provided these affected contracts with a footgun that has put them in the situation where they were *able* to rely on fake guarantees that ethereum never promises (afaik, essentially just gas introspection). We're sorry.

imo it's time to roll forward on this. Let's do what we can in an appropriately scoped capacity for the affected contracts, then activate Glam asap, and continue our excellent progress towards global ubiquity.

author: dotey
quoted_text:
感谢分享，我说一下我在上一个版本 baocut 用 GPUI 踩的坑。

GPUI 挺好的，性能好，跨平台，AI 友好，但也有坑：
1. UI 复杂一点的话大概率你要 fork 一份改一下，有些功能原生支持不了，但也不是大问题

2. Accessibility 支持不太好，要支持一些键盘操作会比较麻烦（也可能我用法不对）

3. Rust 编译资源消耗很大
每次编译，无论是 CPU 占用还是磁盘占用，都巨大，对于我这样用 Mac Mini M4 16G + 1T 硬盘的来说简直太痛苦了，不敢并行多开编译任务，磁盘空间永远不够用（后来我把编译结果默认放到移动硬盘缓解了一点）

4. 编译时间很长，不支持热更新。
这点很要命，这意味着你如果改一点 UI 代码，要重新编译，然后要等少则几分钟多则十几分钟，这时间无论对于 agent 还是对于人来说都是很大的时间成本，加上不能随便多任务，会拖慢你的开发速度

5. agent 验证 UI 不算太友好
codex、claude code 都可以借助 computer use 去验证 GPUI 的结果，但一个是慢，另一个相对成本也不低。

---

后来我之所以换回 Electron，就是因为 Electron App 对于 Agent 相对友好，编译快、热更新，UI 改动很快看到效果，然后 Electron App 还能跑到 agent 内置的浏览器中，agent 验证起来很快，都不需要用 computer use 去打开 electron app。

至于网页渲染性能不够好的问题，我把原来一些需要复杂渲染的部分，都用 rust 编译成了 wasm，这样在浏览器运行也可以保证高性能。

以前 rust 做的转录、tts 模块也都以 worker 进程的形式保留下来了，electron 需要用到的时候可以直接起 rust 编译出来的进程（Codex 也是类似），和这些进程通信，后台的性能也比纯 TypeScript + Node 要好不少。

有兴趣的话可以看代码库：https://t.co/aON4AditbU
