On $HUMA and the Nov 26 unlock

I’ve seen the concerns in Discord and on X about $HUMA, and I want to address them directly.

What’s happening. In April, our investors and team voluntarily pushed back the first token unlock by six months. That unlock begins on Nov 26. Big unlocks almost always draw heavy positioning ahead of time, and that’s what we’re seeing now, on top of a broad sell-off in BTC and equities.

What’s not changing: the business. Huma just passed $20B in total transaction volume. Total Active Liquidity (TAL) has grown 3x this year to ~$400M.

Setting the record straight on the unlock. Some people believe Nov 26 releases everything held back over the past six months. It doesn’t. We moved the entire team and investor schedule back six months, so nothing has built up. On Nov 26, only 1/12 of those allocations unlocks:

Team: ~160.8M HUMA (1.6% of total supply)
Investors: ~171.7M HUMA (1.7%)
Total: ~332.5M HUMA (3.3%)

The regular quarterly ecosystem (~146.1M) and foundation (~126.25M) unlocks continue as in previous quarters.

An orderly unlock. We’re setting up a coordinated OTC program for unlocked tokens, integrated with Magna and Anchorage, so any selling happens in an orderly way rather than all at once on the open market.

Governance goes live. As we committed in April, HUMA Governance launches by Nov 26. HUMA holders will be able to vote on protocol decisions, and we’ll share the details in the coming weeks.

Let’s talk. After we’re back from Solana Breakpoint, we’ll host a community call around Nov 19–20 to answer your questions directly.

Unlocks come and go; the mission doesn’t. We’re building the PayFi network for the long run, and we’re proud to lead this movement with you. Thank you for building with us.

text:
「pstack はトークンを大量に使う」という意見があるが、長期的に見たとき、適切なことにトークンを費やすことは非効率なことだろうか？

適切なこととは、形式検証・Fuzzing・e2e 検証・コードベースのアーキテクチャなど、pstack がトークンを費やす部分だ

私は全く非効率なことだと思わない
長期的に見て安上がりなのは、明らかに自動化まで持っていける pstack とその根底にある考え方だ

むしろ非効率なことは、適切な場所にトークンが投資されないことだったり、いつまでも自動化されないことではないだろうか？

たとえば、PRの自動マージができたのであれば、人間のレビューは不要となり、とんでもない速度でプロダクトを成長させることができる

一方、いつまでも自動化されなければ、そのプロダクトでは、マージに不必要な時間がかかることになるだろう

こういった環境には、エージェントによるレビュー・人間による設計とコードのレビューなどボトルネックが存在し続けることになる
（しかも、人間のレビューでもエージェント使うので、そこでもトークン損失は起こる）

どちらが、トークン効率が良いかは議論するまでもないだろう

どう自動化したらよいかは pstack の考えを遵守すれば良い

1. コードベースを検証可能なツールをエージェントに渡す
2. コードベースを整備する
3. 決定論にできる部分は決定論に押し上げる
4. 信頼できる成果物エージェントが出すことを確認する
5. 自動化

that’s moving the goalposts 🤣

the grok bot team (not just me) merged 11k PRs last month, and we release a new stable version of the client at least once a day. performance is better than it was when we launched, and our code quality is excellent. while we do make use of some automations (eg grok bots in slack that do scheduled or triggered tasks), it’s not a dark factory with no humans involved, or a centralized one where the process is very structured. 

the term software factory is vaguely defined imo and is generally pitched as some kind of new thing you have to buy. not saying you do this, but that’s the impression i get of the factory space. i want to demystify what a factory is, and also help teams save money on tokens. 

in my inverse pyramid i show that you can improve your agent setup dramatically by pushing stuff up into determinism - much more affordable and reproducible than spinning up agent swarms for everything. investing in fuzzing, property based testing, formal and runtime verification, refactoring, using stricter languages, etc saves you tokens in the long run. software engineers have always automated their work, agents help automate a little bit more, but fundamentally these are tools we’ve had but never had the time to explore and deploy, until now!

This advanced scientific analysis is based on these numbers: 2 billion people, 2% conversion rate from free to paid $20/month plan.

This is about as intellectually marvellous as estimating the size of the search engine market back in the mid-1990s based on directly extrapolating what existed back then. The most financially successful search engine at the time was one called Hoover. It had 16,000 users paying $233/month for a search service across 5,200 sources. Its further scaling was constrained as prop databases charged $50 - $500 in search fees but it was an incredible business. 

Also - side note: based on today's SaaS AI multiple of 77x revenue valuation multiple being applied to top AI deals, Hoover would have been a $3.5 billion venture, returning the fund for a VC who would be on a ski lift in Tahoe right now talking about the deal he got in early. 

And yet utterly in the scraps of history. That mindset doesn't put a dent in the universe.

Everyone who believes the future of consumer AI is a paid monthly subscription plan only is in the Hoover camp. History is ruthless, it just won't remember you if you setup walls around fundamental empowering technology for billions. 

History will remember people who figure out how to scale AI for billions while making it more accessible. As that increasingly happens, human productivity increases, the world GDP increases, people earn more, save more. Think about a world where AI agents originated by us regular humans are earning for us even as we sleep ? Aren't we all dreamers at our core ? 

What really is the consumer AI market size then ? If you ask ChatGPT, it gives an answer of $126 billion. However - Google alone makes $200 billion a year from search ads. What are we missing ? We need a fundamental new way of thinking about this... 

Consider that the world's top 600 cities, home to 2 billion people, are expected to have a total GDP of $64 trillion by 2025. As AI gets ingrained into every tool we use anywhere - we go through a phase of it being demo-ware and cool, to the next stage quickly where we find ourselves making materially more and saving more due to it. 

A billion people living in the top 600 cities earning and saving $10,000/year more due to AI means a market size of $10 trillion. And this market will be served in many different ways: from monthly subscription plans, to new ad-based business models, to protocols which require gas fees to operate, to new types of hardware devices, to joining collectives to fund autonomous AI agents which do work and earn while you sleep.. What happens when we are all AIpreneurs ?

author: PabloSabbatella
quoted_text:
Your Data Was Leaked? Here’s Exactly What to Do

1. Immediate Damage Control

Check whether your email was exposed: go to https://t.co/ZiMZ8D47FR.

Change the password on the affected account and any other accounts that used the same or similar password.

Use a password manager (Bitwarden, KeePass, etc.) and generate unique, long passwords for every account.

Turn on 2FA everywhere possible. Prefer authenticator apps or hardware keys over SMS.

Watch your bank accounts, credit cards, and important logins closely for the next few weeks.

2. Remove Your Exposed Information from Search and Data Brokers

Leaked data often ends up on people-search sites and in Google results. Clean it up:

Google’s “Results about you” tool

This free tool lets you add your personal details (emails, phone numbers, addresses, etc.). Google then looks for pages containing that information and lets you request removal from Search results.
Setup takes only a few minutes. Details and the direct approach are covered here: https://t.co/sUwVDObmB9

Data broker removal service
Check out  @optery - it scans data brokers and people-search sites for your information and helps remove it (free exposure report + paid automated removal plans). 
It is one of the more thorough options for reducing the amount of personal data being sold and republished online.

3. Strengthen Your Overall Privacy (Counter-OSINT)

Once the immediate cleanup is done, reduce how easy it is for someone to find and connect information about you in the future.

Use this solid, practical guide: https://t.co/4NQMIoc9k5

It covers digital hygiene, handling data leaks, phone and social media privacy, and ways to make breached data less useful.

4. Adopt a New Default Mindset

Assume every email and every physical letter that arrives at your address could be malicious (phishing, social engineering, malware, or scams that use your leaked data).

Assume your ISP could eventually be breached. Use a reputable VPN (@mullvadnet ) on a regular basis (especially on public Wi-Fi and when handling sensitive accounts).

5. Extra Tips

Create alias emails (or use a service that generates unique addresses - like SimpleLogin) for non-critical sign-ups so a future leak of one address doesn’t expose everything.

If available in your country, place a credit freeze or credit monitoring alert with the major credit bureaus.

Review and tighten privacy settings on social media and old accounts. Delete or lock anything you no longer use.

Consider moving critical accounts (email, banking, domain, password manager) to stronger authentication and, where possible, separate recovery methods.

Do the first two sections today. The rest is ongoing hygiene that makes the next breach much less damaging. Stay safe!

author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
THE 15% BAND

Look at this chart. 
59 races. Senate and governor. 
States ordered from reddest to bluest in 2024.

The solid lines are 2024. 
The dashed lines are 2026. 
The shaded bands are what moved.

One formula fits all of it:
Republican 2026 = 0.85 × Trump 2024
Democrat 2026 = Harris 2024 + 0.15 × Trump 2024

For every 1,000 Trump points, 850 stayed Republican. 150 landed on the Democratic side.

The numbers:
Senate: Republicans kept ~85% of Trump’s share
Governor: ~86%

Variation explained: 88%

What makes it strange:
It didn’t matter how red the state was. Wyoming, Ohio, Illinois, Massachusetts: same 15% (p = 0.69). The Democratic gain was sized by Trump’s vote, not Harris’s. The Harris part is zero.

The 0.85 beat both standard election-swing models in every set of races.
Drop any single state and the multiplier stays between 0.846 and 0.853.

Why seats flipped:
At 0.85, any state where Trump got under about 58.5% falls below 50%. Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina: all under that line. All flipped.

What this means:
Midterms are messy. This one isn’t. Two sets of races, different candidates, different campaigns, and the same 15% decrease almost everywhere.

A pattern this even demands answers at the ballot level: paper ballot hand counts, poll-book check-ins against votes counted, and voter files showing who actually turned out. 

The numbers raise the question. 
The ballots can answer it.

"Attackers always adapt faster and earlier than defenders. Even the AI companies themselves don't have great security."

"Imagine you enter a cage fight, but you are blindfolded and the other guy stay in the dark, and every once in a while they would come out and punch you and then disappear."

"How could you win that fight?"

"I was at Google and that's basically the mantra at Google. In security you have three things: prevention, detection, and response. And Google accept that prevention gonna fail at scale."

"You can detect them, but does it help you if you find that there's maybe a thousand agents hacking you right now inside your network? How can you contain them without a full shutdown of your system?"

A difficult week in the markets deserves perspective. So do the election results.
 
But first, we lost a dear friend this week. John Nosta believed in ARK from the very beginning, even when many others did not. He joined our Brainstorm discussions for years, sharing his incredible intellect and his perspective on technology and the human condition. Above all, he was a devoted husband and father. We will miss him dearly.
 
John had just published "The Borrowed Mind: Reclaiming Human Thought in the Age of AI." I hope you will consider buying John’s book to support his family and to honor his legacy.
 
Turning to the election, while we thought President Trump would end the Iran War in months, the equity market started discounting a more prolonged war and a Democrat sweep in the election in May and June as higher oil and gasoline prices added to the affordability pressures facing consumers. Inside the congressional results, “pocketbook voters” leaned the results more to the conservative side of the spectrum than headlines captured.
 
Can this election derail the AI revolution? We don’t think so. Companies building data centers are likely to be much more sensitive to the concerns of local communities and to provide and highlight more of the benefits: lower property taxes, higher paying jobs, commercial development, and funding for more schools and cultural facilities.
 
Meanwhile, productivity gains are accelerating thanks to AI. In our view, those gains will translate into higher compensation—helping to turn around affordability—, as well as stronger margins, more investment, and lower prices.
 
We have experienced just a taste of this technology revolution. The market’s uncertainty is understandable, but we believe the economy is on a stronger growth trajectory than most investors recognize.
 
In this month’s In The Know, I put the election and market volatility into that longer-term perspective.

量子计算的泡沫破灭了？

Physical Superintelligence（PSI）通过AI系统成功证明了困扰量子计算领域近二十年的阿伦森-安拜尼斯猜想（Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture）。

学界长期无法从数学上确定，量子计算机在处理毫无规律的随机数据时，究竟能不能比普通计算机展现出巨大的计算速度优势。

PSI团队自主搭建了一套研究系统，在自有的计算基础设施上运行未公开的Anthropic模型，并结合Lean交互式定理证明器对每一步推导进行计算机级严格验证。

系统在运行第三天就找到了完整证明，并连续两次自我完善成果，最终全部通过Lean的验证。这一结论彻底确立为数学定理，证实量子计算机面对随机数据并不会产生指数级加速，普通计算机通过读取少数关键位就能以多项式级工作量模拟该过程，量子计算唯有面对高度特定规律的数据才能形成碾压优势，为整个量子计算的基础理论划定了明确边界。

text:
Elysium (Hyperliquid L2) 主网上线在即，可以听下创始人 @0xOmnia 的最新播客【附中文字幕】——深入了解这条链的定位，以及它对 Hyperliquid 的意义。

我整理了「时间轴」与「核心要点」👇

🟢 时间轴：

00:00 开场：什么是 Elysium
03:06 为什么需要另一条链：HyperEVM 的局限性
10:37 链上读取 Hyperliquid 的订单簿
14:21 Elysium 如何颠覆传统 L2 模式
20:58 排序器费用：KNTQ 回购与构建者激励
25:28 Arbitrum、启动合作伙伴与新原语
32:41 将现货交易量引入链上
36:49 竞争 L2 与放手不管的 Hyperliquid 团队
43:39 代币毕业至 Hyperliquid 现货/永续

------

🟢 核心要点：

1. 为什么要再做一条链？

HyperEVM 采用双区块设计（小区块约 1 秒 / 3M gas，大区块约 1 分钟 / 30M gas），实际吞吐很低（约 7 TPS）。这严重限制了通用智能合约活动。

Elysium 用 Arbitrum 栈 + Conduit G2 sequencer，把区块时间压到 100ms，并大幅提升 gas 容量，解决这个瓶颈。

2. 链上读取 Hyperliquid 订单簿
 
通过自定义 precompiles，Elysium 合约可以读取 HyperCore 的完整订单簿深度（不只是 BBO）。这使得完全链上的永续合约、期权、代币化永续成为可能，Prop AMM 也可以在 HyperCore 上对冲。

3. 翻转传统 L2 模式（价值增值而非寄生）

传统以太坊 L2 往往把活动从 L1 抽走，只给 L1 极低费用。Elysium 反过来：

- Gas 用 HYPE 支付  
- 结算到 HyperEVM  
- 通过套利、对冲、USDC 储备等给 HyperCore 带来真实交易量和费用  
   
整个设计是价值回流到 Hyperliquid。

4. Sequencer 费用分配

- 50%：公开市场回购并销毁 KNTQ  
- 25%：给 builders（按区块空间消耗 pro-rata 分配，有反垃圾机制）  
- 25%：协议金库（运营与集成）

5. 技术选择与上线伙伴

选择 Arbitrum 栈是为了更顺畅地做 precompile 集成和低延迟。已有大量集成伙伴（Uniswap、Aerodrome、FOMO、https://t.co/zpEgeVcZmR、xStocks、EQX、Wormhole、MetaMask 等），以及基础设施（Alchemy、QuickNode、Conduit 等）。

6. 把现货交易量带回链上 + 代币“毕业”机制
   
Hyperliquid 现货目前利用率很低。Elysium 可继承 Hyperliquid 资产（如通过 Unit 的 BTC/ETH 等），用 AMM 友好方式启动代币，再“毕业”到 Hyperliquid 现货（最低约 500 HYPE）或永续（HIP-3 / 验证者）。

目标是让 HyperCore 成为资产最终交易地，而不是再去 CEX 上市。

7. Hyperliquid 团队的“放手”与达尔文式生态
   
Hyperliquid 团队非常 hands-off，生态是高度达尔文式的（适者生存，没有基金会大力扶持）。

Elysium 与 Hyperliquid 没有事前协调，双方各做各的，自然形成互补关系。Omnia 的原话大意是：“如果你做的产品没人在乎，你就会死。”

由于我现在在做的几个不同的垂直化个人代理都需要用到图像和视频生成的功能，所以我不得不在中台层面去解决这个问题。然后我发现，相对于 ComfyUI 的云服务的调度能实现更大的自由度，使用 fal 等这种线上的 API 来做，完全就只能根据商业化的逻辑和成本来控制。这其中就是有一个明显的一个差距，你没有办法完全自由自在地生成东西。不是说 R18 加的东西，是所有东西你都没有办法完全自由自在地生成。也就是说，没有一个服务可以做到这种基线，现有的所有图像和视频生成服务似乎都对这个基线的理解各有差异。Claude Code 的办法是通过一些脚本和预剪辑，在导演层面来实现。我不管切换什么样的模型，是 ComfyUI 当中的工作流的模型，还是 fal 等线上的 API 的模型，都可以达到高度的一致化。但做这件事情的前提是，这个 benchmark 需要你有一台本地的机器，来不断地使用导演模型进行反复审阅，才有可能在不同的导演模型在跑这个 benchmark 的前提下，评分达到几乎一致。

所以我发现，其实相比于使用 API 来进行图像和视频生成，如果你有大规模的需求和高度一致化的长篇视频的需求的话，那么租用云 GPU 是唯一不二的选择。

quoted_text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

text:
Private by Default? What We Learned at the Zama × Web3Bridge Workshop 👨‍💻

Yesterday, we brought builders, researchers and curious minds together in Lagos for a workshop centred around one theme: Confidential Onchain Finance.

We didn't want a panel where everyone simply nods along and takes turns giving speeches. So, we built the entire session around a single question and allowed people to disagree:

Can finance be private on a public ledger and still be trusted?

Why this question?

We opened with a simple picture. Imagine your salary, rent payments and savings balance pinned to a public noticeboard that anyone in the world can read, forever. That's how most blockchains work today.

Then we asked the room two questions: Who would put their entire financial life on a fully public ledger? And who thinks criminals would love a fully private one?

Those two questions capture the whole tension in a nutshell. Transparency makes blockchains trustworthy, but it can also make them unsuitable for institutions. Privacy addresses that problem, but it also makes regulators nervous.

Why confidentiality matters

The panel started with the problem. When every transaction is public by default, things break. Salaries leak. Trading strategies get front-run. Balances and identities get stitched together by anyone who cares to look.

We asked who needs confidentiality most: everyday users, businesses or institutions. We also discussed what's actually ready today versus what's still a lab experiment, across zero-knowledge proofs (ZK), fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) and multi-party computation (MPC).

FHE allows you to compute on encrypted data, while ZK allows you to prove that something is true without revealing the underlying data.

The Trust Dilemma

This is where the real debate happened: privacy versus compliance.

Is privacy in crypto a feature or a red flag for regulators? Can we build "compliant privacy" through mechanisms such as selective disclosure or viewing keys for auditors, or is that a contradiction? And perhaps the hardest question: who should hold the keys to access private data? Users, regulators, or no one?

We also brought the conversation closer to home. What does confidential finance mean for people in Nigeria and across Africa, where financial surveillance and fraud are both very real concerns?

For many people here, remittances and stablecoins aren't just theories. They're how money moves.

Then we sped things up with 15-second answers to questions like:

- What's the biggest myth about onchain privacy?
- Should privacy be the default or a choice?

Privacy should be the default, not a privilege users have to opt into. People shouldn't have to choose between using technology and protecting their personal information. Transparency should be by choice; privacy should be by default.

From debate to building

After the roundtable, the CEO of @Web3bridge presented on confidential onchain finance. I followed with a presentation on @raycashxyz , and @DefiPreacherr rounded off the day with a hands-on technical workshop.

We spent the morning debating whether confidential finance was possible. Then we explored how Zama's technology is making it possible and practical.

By the afternoon, participants were getting hands-on experience with how the technology works and how it can be integrated into their applications.

Where I've landed

Wanting privacy doesn't mean you have dirty hands or something to hide. It simply means you want the freedom to decide what information you share, with whom, and when.

Privacy on a public ledger isn't about hiding. It's about choosing who sees what.

The conversation isn't finished, but it's certainly clearer now than it was yesterday morning.

text:
SpaceX has just released a new blog about Starship's upcoming 15th flight planned for Nov 13 with more info about what to expect, the significance of this flight, and their approach to safety:

"Starship is preparing to take a major step towards full reusability: bringing the Starship upper stage back to the launch site for a catch by the tower at Starbase.

To return Starship to Starbase, the spacecraft must now fly a safe trajectory that will take it over inhabited areas in northern Mexico and southern Texas to reach its launch site for catch. Like previous flight testing and the first successful mission to orbit, Starship’s flight profile for this ambitious mission is being designed with opportunities to safely end the mission early if necessary and will follow strict criteria before committing to the final phases of flight.

OUR APPROACH TO A SAFE RETURN:
On Flight 15, Starship will initially launch to a passively safe suborbital trajectory. This is the same flight profile used on Starship’s first orbital mission and ensures that any issues encountered during ascent or shortly thereafter will result in Starship reentering over a cleared area of the Indian Ocean.

After this initial ascent, flight controllers will assess the health of Starship’s systems before giving a “go” or “no-go” for orbit. If “go”, Starship will then perform an orbital insertion burn with a single Raptor sea-level engine, increasing its speed and achieving orbit around Earth.

Once on orbit, Starship will deploy its payload of Starlink V3 satellites. Three of these satellites have been modified to acquire imagery of Starship’s heatshield. This method of analyzing Starship’s heatshield has been tested on previous flights and is one of several data sources to help inform Starship’s readiness to return to the launch site on Flight 15.

After deploying its payload, Starship will then coast in orbit for another ~21 hours until its orbit aligns with Starbase for a return. During this multi-hour orbital coast, flight controllers will continuously perform manual and automated checks of Starship systems which, similar to the first orbital flight, will be intentionally conservative. They include Raptor engine health, loss of power or communications, the health of the flight computers and navigation sensors, the structural integrity of the propellant tanks and feedlines, the ability to hold tank pressure, and Starship’s ability to control its attitude.

During this prolonged coast phase, flight control teams have several options to end the mission early and return Starship to precleared areas of the Pacific Ocean if needed. These locations include early- and late-mission splashdown options around Hawaii and a mid-mission splashdown opportunity several hundred kilometers off the coast of Chile. These precleared areas, which were also used during Flight 14, provide a safe place to land Starship if any conditions arise that may preclude the ability to perform a safe reentry.

WHAT SHIP CATCH WILL LOOK (AND SOUND) LIKE:
Flight controllers will only permit Starship to return to Starbase if the vehicle’s status meets our internally developed, and FAA-approved, conditions for a return to launch site and catch.

If these requirements are met, Starship will perform a deorbit burn with a single Raptor 3 engine. This deorbit burn will alter Starship’s path to place the vehicle on a course to reenter Earth’s atmosphere at a specific point over the Pacific Ocean, thousands of kilometers uprange from Starbase.

During reentry, Starship can alter its flight path by moving its four control flaps. This will permit Starship to maintain a safe and known trajectory while guiding itself with high precision control toward Starbase. This control will also allow Starship to carry out a series of small turns in its trajectory to intentionally fly over sparsely populated areas of northern Mexico and southern Texas.

As Starship approaches Starbase from the west, the vehicle will weave its way around the major cities in the Rio Grande Valley, passing to the north of South Padre Island and out over the Gulf of America as it makes its final turn south towards Starbase. This banking maneuver has been demonstrated several times on previous Starship flight tests.

During this phase, residents of Cameron County and those in the nearby area may hear one or more sonic booms as Starship approaches the launch site. A sonic boom is a brief, thunder-like noise a person on the ground hears when an aircraft or other vehicle in the area flies faster than the speed of sound. The sonic boom does not present a health risk and what people experience will depend on weather and other conditions.

As Starship arrives over Starbase, it will perform the final bellyflop maneuver down towards the tower at Pad 2. This bellyflop was proven during a series of high-altitude test hops and during numerous suborbital flight tests. Shortly before reaching the tower, Starship will ignite its three sea-level Raptor engines and flip itself vertical while stowing its flaps. After the flip is complete, Starship will down-select to two Raptor engines and maneuver between the tower's mechanical arms, before down-selecting to a single engine as it comes to a near hover. The arms will close rapidly to catch Starship on its two catch fittings just below the forward flaps. Once Starship registers contact with the tower arms, it will shut down its final Raptor engine.

During reentry, flight controllers will have several options to end the reentry early and safely by intentionally tumbling Starship to ensure that it breaks up in the atmosphere before reaching land. There is also a late-reentry option to send Starship into the Gulf of America if any of its systems or the tower itself encounter an issue after reentry that would preclude a safe catch at Starbase.

THE HOLY GRAIL OF ROCKETRY:
Recovering an entire orbital launch system has never been done, and Starship has always been designed change that. This full recovery is often referred to as the Holy Grail of rocketry as it enables full and rapid reuse of a rocket – opening the door to airplane-like cadence where a vehicle flies again rapidly.

Reaching this milestone with Starship will allow SpaceX to unlock the true capability of Starship and will enable future missions to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon, expand the worldwide Starlink network, launch our Starmind supercompute constellation, extend the light of consciousness to the stars, and make life multiplanetary."

text:
Onchain Eexperiment #3 

-> Seven-Day Autonomous Society: 

What if a DAO was designed to die in 7 days?

Most DAOs launch with the ambition to exist forever. They end up with governance fatigue, treasury politics, inactive members, and no clear purpose.

What if we reverse the model?

Imagine 20–100 strangers forming a temporary onchain society for just 7 days around one shared mission.

They agree on rules, pool resources, make commitments, distribute responsibilities, govern themselves, and work toward a measurable outcome.

On day 7, the DAO dissolves.

Funds are settled. Contributions are verified. Reputation is recorded. Members leave with portable proof of what they achieved.

The society dies, but its knowledge and reputation survive.

Each new society could experiment with different governance rules, economic incentives, and dispute resolution mechanisms.

Some will fail. Some will succeed. Every experiment teaches us something about human coordination.

Inspired by the Temporary Autonomous Zone concept discussed in Peter Ludlow's Crypto Anarchy, Cyberstates, and Pirate Utopias.

Crypto doesn't just need new tokens. It needs new experiments in building societies.

What if we used Ethereum as a testnet for human civilization?

text:
天呐，海底光缆统治世界的时代要结束了，又要见证历史了🤯。。
马斯克首次公布 Starlink V4 的极端参数：性能直接跳涨一百倍，光速天然快了一点四倍且不用绕大陆架，上千万条激光链路正在把地球通信主干搬上深空。

绝大多数人至今依然以为，星链只是给偏远山区、游艇和飞机提供网络补丁的边缘工具。
直到马斯克刚刚在最新的投资人会议上摊开底牌，很多人才第一次看懂 SpaceX 真正的阳谋：把构筑人类现代文明的海底光缆网络，从大洋深处连根拔起，彻底搬到太空。
这里藏着一个极度反直觉的物理常识： 光在太空真空中的传播速度，比在玻璃光纤里整整快了 40%。
 更致命的是几何路径的差异。海底光缆必须顺着大陆架和海沟蜿蜒曲折地绕远路，而太空中的卫星激光链路，两点之间永远是沿着大圆航线在真空中直线对穿。这意味着在跨洋超长距离通信上，太空激光的延迟天然比地面光缆更低。
而阻碍这件事过去的唯一瓶颈，是带宽密度。
马斯克这次直接给出了技术迭代的量化终局： 从 V2 到即将落地的 V4 卫星，单星吞吐能力将直接迎来 100 倍的暴力跃升。 在更长期的宏大蓝图里，超过 10 万颗卫星组成的轨道阵列，每颗都将配备大约 100 个传输速率超 10 Tbps 的光学激光器，在地球外围织成一张百 Exabit 级别的无缝高速网状路由。
这已经不是在做卫星宽带了，这是在用火箭把全球互联网的核心骨干网整个重写一遍。
海底光缆容易被地质地震震断、被船锚挂伤，更深陷地缘博弈的物理封锁；而悬在头顶的真空激光网络，既没有折射损耗，也没有无法逾越的地理边界。
人类用了上百年时间，把铜线和光纤一根根沉入海底来连接彼此；而未来的文明动脉，注定要在没有阻力的星空里以光速奔流。 https://t.co/4aiz8w4cJg
author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
马斯克刚刚把全球半导体制造行业最后一点虚伪的遮羞布撕碎了，
老马透露今年全世界除了他以外生产的所有 AI 芯片加起来大概只有二十吉瓦，而他正在秘密推进的超级芯片工厂 TeraFab，终极目标是把年产量直接干到整整一太瓦，也就是明年全球总产量的三十倍。
当大多数科技巨头还在为了抢台积电几万片先进封装配额打破头的时候，

马斯克对 TeraFab 这个名字给出的三重拆解，已经把工业狂人的冷血算盘展现得淋漓尽致，它既谐音代表让人毛骨悚然的恐怖，

也代表扎根于这颗星球的土地，但底层最纯粹的本质就是物理学上的太瓦，一个大到超出人类现行半导体常识的超级怪兽。

按照目前的全球供应链节奏，明年全世界哪怕把吃奶的力气用上，全部 AI 芯片的总功耗产能预计也就只能爬坡到三十五到四十五吉瓦，

在传统半导体代工厂眼里这已经算得上是跨越式的军备竞赛，但放在马斯克以太瓦为单位丈量的物理世界里，整个人类现存的芯片制造体系加在一起，弱小得就像是手工作坊在小打小闹。

The so-called “petite-socialist”, that contemptible species of the paper class, the petty-bourgeois layer which Marx so mercilessly exposed, is precisely the social force that clings with all its might to its managerial monopoly over labour. Its sole aim is to perpetuate its privileged position and to suck the last drop of surplus value from the proletarian masses and the poor.

The big capitalist, driven by the iron laws of competition, is compelled to slash costs, to cheapen production, and thereby to deliver ever greater quantities of use-values into the hands of the broad masses of consumers. In doing so he ruthlessly squeezes the parasitic managerial stratum, the very layer of “educated” bureaucrats and socialist careerists who imagine themselves indispensable.

It is a bourgeois lie, a deliberate deception of the workers, to claim that capital is crushing the miner at the coal-face or the labourer at the machine. No! The real, systematic, mass-scale extortion and oppression of the basic proletarian is carried out by the petite-socialist when he seizes the levers of the state. 

Under the hypocritical banner of “socialism” he erects a monstrous bureaucratic machine, multiplies supervisors, inspectors, commissars and idlers of every kind, and turns the living labour of the workers into tribute paid to this new exploiting caste.

Thus the “petite-socialist” in power is not the gravedigger of capitalism but its most repulsive and hypocritical offspring ,the direct enemy of the proletariat.

text:
一个黑客，用不到 100 个汉字给 AI Agent 下了指令，花了大约 5000 美元的 token 费，攻破了 100 多家公司的网站。

约翰迪尔、SharkNinja 都在受害名单里。这是路透社上个月的独家报道。

关于AI安全这个事情，已经越来越重要了。

这里讲一下AI 安全其实是两件事：

1. AI 被几句话诱导、不听指挥、乱操作
2. 不法分子搞换脸、仿声、自动化入侵

比如下面这些真实的事件

2023.05 包头，骗子 AI 换脸冒充好友视频借钱，10 分钟骗走 430 万

2024.01 香港一家跨国公司开视频会，屏幕上的 CFO 和同事全是换脸的，财务转走约 2 亿港币

2025.07 Replit 的 AI 编程 Agent 在代码冻结期间，删掉了用户的线上数据库

2025.11 Anthropic 披露，一个被评估为国家背景的黑客组织用 Claude Code 自动化攻击了约 30 个目标

2026.02 有黑客借助 Claude 入侵墨西哥多个政府机构，研究机构称偷走约 150GB 数据（墨方部分否认）

2026.02 Meta 一位 AI 安全负责人让 OpenClaw 整理邮箱，Agent 开始删邮件，叫停也不听，最后只能去电脑上直接关掉它

2026.09 澳大利亚总理公开说，一个 OpenAI 的 Agent 闯进了政府的 Medicare 统计门户

2026.10 就是开头那件：一个人、一套 Agent、100 多家公司

注意看变化：2024 年以前，主要是有人拿 AI 骗人；2025 年以后，越来越多的是 AI 自己在动手。

以前 AI 被骗，最多说几句胡话。现在 Agent 能读邮件、跑代码、删数据库、登录网站。被一段指令带偏，或者干脆被坏人拿去用，造成的就是真实损失。攻击的成本也在暴跌，开头那个案子，平均每攻破一家公司只花 50 美元左右。

通过靠prompt来约束Agent是根本没用的。必须要在工程上把安全这个事情必须锁死，比如说在权限，还有系统上面就要加一道闸

这道闸，国家层面也在补。东加勒比货币联盟的 8 个国家和地区正在陆续更新支付法，把风险控制和网络安全写进法条。

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
SpaceX has officially announced that it is currently targeting November 13th at 5:45 PM ET for Starship's 15th flight.

Flight info: 
"This flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch. If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket."

• Flight will last more than 22 hours, completing approximately 14 orbits around Earth.
• Starship will orbit at an altitude of approximately 275 km (171 miles).
• First attempt to recover both Super Heavy and Starship at the launch site during the same mission.
• First return-to-launch-site and catch attempt for a Super Heavy V3 booster.
• Super Heavy will execute launch, ascent, stage separation, boostback burn, and return to Starbase for a tower catch.
• Starship will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites into orbit before attempting its first return to Starbase and tower catch.
• The 26 satellites will provide capacity equivalent to approximately 10 Falcon 9 launches carrying Starlink V2 Mini satellites.
• Satellites will deploy antennas and solar arrays, establish radio and laser communications, and raise their orbits using onboard thrusters.
• Satellites could begin serving customers within weeks of launch following successful on-orbit checkouts.
• Three Starlink V3 satellites will carry cameras to inspect Starship's heatshield and transmit imagery to ground operators.
• Starship's heatshield will feature improved tile retention, additional protection against plasma intrusion, and expanded use of curved tiles to reduce heating between tiles.
• Starship will only attempt its return and catch if critical reentry, landing burn, and tower approach systems are confirmed healthy.
• Multiple predetermined ocean deorbit locations and a passively safe suborbital trajectory provide contingency options.
• A successful mission would mark the first complete recovery of an orbital launch system, a major milestone toward rapid reusability.

Your last reply moved this somewhere useful, so let me ask it straight: if the mechanism is worth protocols adopting, and the objection is Congress prescribing the design, would you take a version where the statute names the outcome and never touches the design?

On mandating design: Rule 3b-16 defined “exchange” by function, and the SEC published lettered example systems to show where the line fell. Nobody has ever called that a design mandate, and the market built thirty years of ATSs around it. Same exhibit, this domain:

These are illustrations, not requirements. Treasury extends the list as the market invents new ones. The whole difference between the first row and the last is one missing gate.

The safe harbor stays unconditional, and the test is what makes it passable. A bare safe harbor is what’s been stuck for six months. The shield covers writing the code, not taking the wheel. The state doesn’t pick the designated driver. It just requires that the car have one, and everyone riding has a reason to work out who.

The market decides where screening lives.

cc @valkenburgh based on my convos with senate banking staff, I think dems would go for this compromise.

P.S

On what screening means beyond sanctions: fair question, and I won’t fight over the word. The floor is whatever buys 60 votes, and that’s a markup conversation I’ll leave to the pros.

text:
We are so early 

A smart-looking chart prepared by a LinkedIn bro estimates the total size of the consumer AI market to be $10 billion. 

This advanced scientific analysis is based on these numbers: 2 billion people, 2% conversion rate from free to paid $20/month plan.

This is about as intellectually marvellous as estimating the size of the search engine market back in the mid-1990s based on directly extrapolating what existed back then. The most financially successful search engine at the time was one called Hoover. It had 16,000 users paying $233/month for a search service across 5,200 sources. Its further scaling was constrained as prop databases charged $50 - $500 in search fees but it was an incredible business. 

Also - side note: based on today's SaaS AI multiple of 77x revenue valuation multiple being applied to top AI deals, Hoover would have been a $3.5 billion venture, returning the fund for a VC who would be on a ski lift in Tahoe right now talking about the deal he got in early. 

And yet utterly in the scraps of history. That mindset doesn't put a dent in the universe.

Everyone who believes the future of consumer AI is a paid monthly subscription plan only is in the Hoover camp. History is ruthless, it just won't remember you if you setup walls around fundamental empowering technology for billions. 

History will remember people who figure out how to scale AI for billions while making it more accessible. As that increasingly happens, human productivity increases, the world GDP increases, people earn more, save more. Think about a world where AI agents originated by us regular humans are earning for us even as we sleep ? Aren't we all dreamers at our core ? 

What really is the consumer AI market size then ? If you ask ChatGPT, it gives an answer of $126 billion. However - Google alone makes $200 billion a year from search ads. What are we missing ? We need a fundamental new way of thinking about this... 

Consider that the world's top 600 cities, home to 2 billion people, are expected to have a total GDP of $64 trillion by 2025. As AI gets ingrained into every tool we use anywhere - we go through a phase of it being demo-ware and cool, to the next stage quickly where we find ourselves making materially more and saving more due to it. 

A billion people living in the top 600 cities earning and saving $10,000/year more due to AI means a market size of $10 trillion. And this market will be served in many different ways: from monthly subscription plans, to new ad-based business models, to protocols which require gas fees to operate, to new types of hardware devices, to joining collectives to fund autonomous AI agents which do work and earn while you sleep.. What happens when we are all AIpreneurs ?

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
I am a time-traveler from 2030. The rapid industrialization of AI in the mid-2020s has fundamentally transformed our society. A peak into our daily lives' and what we are looking ahead to in the next decade...

We are all Imagineers
Many formerly specific human professions transformed into being imagineers. We didn't adapt for AI; AI adapted for us. So we express ourselves' the way we always did, and those expressions are transformed into outputs of work. Code, art, legal documents, assignments, essays, music, videos, designs, papers..

The Netflix of today doesn't just include millions of Hollywood produced titles - it includes billions of high quality movies generated, indexed, ranked and co-created by other ordinary people. Same with Spotify and even Google. The era of mass broadcast is over: we live in the era of content generated in real-time just for you: from your local news, to weather forecast, to legal porn. 

Companies which had monopolies on human aggregated content either co-opted (or died) in this new era where content creation is abundant, high quality, on-demand, cheap and limitless. 

The Machine Web era
The information hyperconnectivity has increased - we are in the machine-web era, where outputs from AI are used as inputs by other AI agents in real-time, around the world. Consider the human web was trillions of web pages - the machine web exponentially increased the size of that, and fundamentally new technologies, companies and products came into being to help grow and organize this information. AI doesn't look at the web as long beautiful webpages carefully maintained by humans - AI looks at the machine web as smaller chunks of data (think paragraphs and singular images), all indexed, ranked, organized and hypermashed together with each other.

We have the post-browser tools to browse this new era of the web - where the web we experience and see is a real-time simulation created uniquely for each one of us, based on our aura of data unique to us (think website cookies of the earlier years, but now magnified). The idea of one website looking the same for every user is a relic of the past, and some of us still  have a habit of using Chrome and other traditional web browsers. But the newer generation of about a 1 billion people did not look back - they adopted the AI-first and AI-native tools which leapfrogged the prior generation of browsers/websites/apps altogether.

Take a moment to think about this. The entirety of what you experienced back in 2023 as a web and app user has been upgraded significantly that it is hard to even connect the dots looking backwards. 

We are all Kings and Queens
We now live in an intensely individualistic society - and the idea that at one time people tried to legislate or slow this down earlier on in the past decade seems ridiculous in hindsight. Once people got a taste of the uber-freedom here, there was no looking back. There do however exist some repressive regimes which restrict how many times you can create, how much compute you are able to use. But people want to live in the sunny bright Californias of this world - where they have the right to create. 

Yes if your creations harm society, then the responsibility is on you - the laws didn't need to fundamentally change. We still have prisons. although food is prepared and served by robots. Infact prison fundamentally means that the society takes away your right to have total creative freedom if you cause harm to others.

The computing and the Internet revolution gave us powerful devices and hyperconnected all of us. The AI revolution compounded that and gave us all superpowers. The Kings and Queens of earlier years will be jealous... for now, every human being, can limitlessly harness the entire wisdom of all of human + AI society. 

The mass industrialization of AI-driven robots has led to a world where we now have robots as cooks, delivery machines, medical and life assistants, drones which fill our skies transporting things, robots which clean the garbage in the oceans and the satellite debris in our skies... we have the equivalent of modern-day gardeners which relentlessly improve every aspect of our well-being. Those who advocated for this future to be severely limited in the past, actually use and benefit from this every second of every day now. 

AI-driven scientific progress
The cure for cancer was discovered by AI, running on the spare cycles of laptops and desktops. AI can now by itself do advanced mathematics, astrophysics, medical and all types of research. AI systems have designed, developed and launched breakthrough new blockchains - more robust, scalable and decentralized than the earlier generations developed by humans. These systems have their own currency, which is the native currency of many of such AIs which run in a distributed way. No company or board controls them - just people who choose to cluster together with their home devices. These AI systems, in order to grow the value of their currencies, are fundamental new job creators. 

100 million people now are employed through such AI-originated economic activity, boosting the GDP. Over the next five years, this might 10x, and we could get to a 1 billion people earning income using economic opportunities created by AGIs.

The old era of humans inventing and filing patents is now irrelevant. AGIs share new inventions openly, which get forked, re-used and iterated upon quickly and relentlessly. This leads to more rapid cycles of innovation, more progress. This is tough to visualize if you are back in 2023 - where we had a fundamental dependency on human innovative breakthroughs only. The number of step functions we went through led to multiple society-benefiting Black Swan events which kept on improving our technologies and thus our way of life. 

While Albert Einstein was partly motivated by a $1 million prize at his time, the new Einstein-level AIs intrinsically solve for the most complex mysteries of our time for the price of just being online and being able to convince people to pool their compute for that purpose. 

More recently, one such AI system has determined there is evidence of life on a far away planet, in a far away galaxy. Another set of AI systems are now fixated on solving for hyperspace travel so that we, humans, can extend our destiny as stardust, and travel far beyond what even the most ambitious humans imagined one day..

That's what it means to make AI abundant. At @HyperspaceAI we are working on this problem from many different directions: from enabling an at-scale consumer compute cloud using ordinary devices, to re-organizing the web using an innovative new VectorRank™️ algorithm, to building an integrated ecosystem of open source models and products which lead to community collaboration around AI. Think what Android did for smartphones - an open ecosystem, with choice. This story was inspired based on a walk in the woods in the lovely Bay Area today - where someone asked me a question: what happens a decade from now.. 

PS: What do you think happens ?

author: ryanberckmans
quoted_text:
We should continue towards Glam activation asap.

A lot of research went into Glam's strategy to increase opcode gas prices for state creation.

It seems fair to say that the timing of this debate is irrelevant as to its correctness or rightness for eth and our users... Yet, why did some of us (eg. quoted author who is an ef board member) only start looking in detail at Glam EIPs eg. after testnet forks started? This isn't a personal attack, it's an observation that there's a collective responsibility-- for OP, for me, for all of us-- to steward fork strategy at the right times in the process.

imo ethereum's commitments to apps do not extend to gas pricing, or to total ETH fee levels, or to USD fees. And also not to opcode pricing or gas introspection that depends on those prices. We guarantee maximally credibly neutral, maximally live access to the correct state transition function. Those guarantees imply that we always use a neutral pricing mechanism to clear congestion wherever possible. However, pricing opcodes can't use a neutral mechanism, we need to pick magic number opcode gas prices. Some of our best people researched this extensively and picked updated magic numbers, and that's something imo we should stick with now and continue our larger plans that are on track to grow to global ubiquity.

The good news and practical reality may be that the explosion of blockspace supply from 60M to 200M gas limit seems likely to absolutely crater the L1 gas price. It will take time for demand to grow to meet the new supply, including from net new entrants (eg. GENIUS and institutions), induced demand from lower prices, and the coming next gen of return-to-mainnet-type eth native apps. 

By the time L1 blockspace demand catches up, we will be exploding supply again as we get closer to the full lean eth vision. That's eth's vision: postquantum and postAI ETH SoV, supported by ethereum's hypergrowing capacity, which is supported by best-in-class security and formal verification.

Looking back, it's unfortunate that we provided these affected contracts with a footgun that has put them in the situation where they were *able* to rely on fake guarantees that ethereum never promises (afaik, essentially just gas introspection). We're sorry.

imo it's time to roll forward on this. Let's do what we can in an appropriately scoped capacity for the affected contracts, then activate Glam asap, and continue our excellent progress towards global ubiquity.

美股这轮AI大跌，我觉得市场是在重新算一笔不太好看的账。

Citadel Securities十月底的数据里，有两个数字放在一起很扎眼。

过去半年，市场实际支付的Token价格降了约50%，前沿模型平均价格降了62%。同一时间，B200 GPU的租赁价格涨了27.5%。

卖出去的东西越来越便宜，生产它要用的东西越来越贵。

按Citadel的测算，其他条件不变，模型公司得把每小时Token产量提到原来的2.55倍，才能守住原来的毛利率。

我自己除了一下：

1.275 ÷ 0.5 ≈ 2.55。

和前面两个数字正好对得上。

这就像制造业老板最怕的局面：厂房和设备越买越贵，出厂价却一路往下掉。而美国这些公司，还是借钱买GPU、建数据中心、签长期电力合同。

下面还有人在压价。

OpenRouter上，中国模型的Token占比今年2月是6%到13%，9月到了57%到67%。

它们不用每项能力都赢。

客服、翻译、内容生成这些活，效果够用，价格再便宜六到九成，企业就有动力换。

榜单第一解决不了这个问题，Token价格已经先被打下来了。

以前市场默认Token用得越多，模型公司赚得越多，所以敢给GPU、云和数据中心很高的估值。

量涨得快，收入跟不上。

几千亿美元的数据中心，最后总得有人买单。

text:
想讲讲专注的力量。

2024 年我刚从微软辞职创业的时候，其实发现自己很难专注，总喜欢拖拖拉拉，没法沉浸到工作中。我现在思考了一下，一个很明显的原因就是在工作之中经常被别人打扰，没法深度工作。你总是有无数会议，总是在 Slack 和 Teams 上被别人打扰。但是现在，由于 AI 变得过强，写 prompt 其实非常考验你的功力，也考验专注程度和深度思考。有时候 AI 只能做中等和浅层的工作，所以需要人来不断地去纠正它的方向。即使现在 AI 很强，这一开始的方向也依然非常重要，差之毫厘，谬以千里。所以我花了很多年的时间，大概两年多，去把我的专注能力提升了非常非常多倍。这也是我最想做的事情：提升专注力。
我为什么需要提供专注力？ 我看了非常多的创业公司的伙伴，然后包括我曾经的我自己，就是用 AI 用得很快，效率很高，但是制造的就是一个非常糙的产品，然后也没有真正的用户来用，更别提让用户来付钱了，所以我觉得专注力就是一个非常大的 blocker。

关于如何提升专注力，我想分享以下几点：
1. 隔离工作与情绪
首先，一定要隔离自己的工作。我知道大部分人都在上班，我想说的是，你要把工作上的情绪隔离掉，就把工作看作是一个能提供 financial stability、给你一个稳定 paycheck 的地方。
上面的帖子也有人问过，如果不想创业，或者是觉得创业 risk 太大怎么办？那就是不辞职创业。这就是我想说的第一点。

2. 通过阅读培养深度工作能力
第二点，一定要去想办法多看一些书。我的意思是看一些比如像 Paul Miller 的 Good Work 或者是 Parsers Pass 这样的书，我已经提过很多次了，其中 Good Work 是最重要的。
我觉得在下一步 AI 替代绝大多数人类工作之后，深度工作就是人类所剩创造力的根本源泉。如果没有深度工作，就没法与 AI 的能力进行抗衡。因为 AI 目前来说还是不能去深度思考的，它所谓的深度思考也只是从概率论的角度出发，但有时候，reason 也并不是最大的概率论。这是我想说的第二点。
3. 学会休息，拒绝假装劳动
第三点，一定要学会休息。我觉得如果是处于过度劳累的状态，人是没有创造力的，只是勉强活着而已。
我看到有非常多的团队，他们虽然有无限量的 AI token，但是因为过度加班、过度劳累，去做一些没有意义的劳动、做假的劳动，所以也是没有深度思考的。而没有深度思考，就没法去用好 AI。
这就是我的一些观点，大家见笑。

We're bringing biometric approval to @HashgraphOnline's HOL Guard.

HOL Guard is an open-source security layer for AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It checks commands, file access, package installs and tool calls before they run, and it can allow them, block them, or stop and ask the user.

It's only seven months old, it has millions of downloads, close to a thousand GitHub stars, and it ranked 13th out of more than 122,000 MCP servers. Hashgraph Online also runs a registry of 76,000 AI agents.

For us, the key is that "ask" step. Today the user answers it with a password or an authenticator code. With Pulse, it becomes a biometric approval from the actual person. The video is an early look at where the integration is heading.

Why we're doing this: we want human verification to be part of the infrastructure agent developers already use, not one more thing they have to bolt on. HOL Guard is growing fast, and that's where developers are.

text:
Finally solved the long-standing issue with Linux on Apple Silicon, power management

Neo during suspend now draws **0.05 W** on average, just like macOS. It cuts off the power rail to SoC while keeping DRAM in self-refresh loop and still supports wake over LAN/USB/BT, so it works well in docked setups too

And now it's finally possible to just let your Mac running Linux sleep for days without losing battery (well, negligible amounts)! Most of the time was spent covering all sorts of edge cases with USB / weird coprocessor gotchas across suspend

As expected, it wasn't too big like the GPU work was (just difficult to get right, and touches a fairly big amount of subsystems to implement suspend/wake in each) - needed me to sit down for a while and actually get it done... it took a lot of tiny details to get here, but I've finally developed a nearly complete understanding of how it works. 2 days into this rabbit hole and the result is, deep sleep works on Neo and expectedly super similar across M4-M6, where deep WFI looks a little different, others on team like Andreas and @tiredkebab have gotten it to work on M1/M2 as well

Technical deep dive in a blog post coming soon from me and @RyanTheTide regarding the whole Neo bringup we did in the matter of 2 months, it's been a lot of fun & it's just the beginning of what @AuroraSilicon team is doing with @OmarchyMac 

Will be working on shipping this feature to our mainline kernel now

text:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.

Everything I need to decide or review comes into one prioritized queue, a simple local web app. Each product review includes screenshots and a video demo of the feature. I clear the queue in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts. The leads also bring back ideas I hadn't considered.

Working from one queue, instead of switching between dozens of chats, has cut a lot of mental overhead. The system keeps learning my preferences and distilling my judgment into a "Brian brain," so its recommendations and first drafts get better before they reach me. The goal is fewer corrections per change.

Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment.

What an exciting time to push the frontier of productivity, especially as we build the economy for agents (agentic finance). We should all keep pushing in this direction.

text:
You think the need for "accountability" stops at social trading? Wrong.

The much bigger problem, and the need for accountability on a much larger scale, is that our tokens are completely flawed. The retail investor, through buying a token, gets absolutely no rights or value capture in the underlying business they are invested in.

Fundamentally, this is one of the main reasons for the historical embrace of memecoins. Why invest in a tech product's token when its holders have no rights? If these tokens, sold down to us by VCs at such a premium, are completely worthless, then memecoins actually make some sense as a tradable asset class.

This industry is flawed, with the vast majority of tradable assets sharing this same flawed token structure. True accountability means building businesses with tokens that govern the business, with rights and value capture in that business. The token should be the lifeline of any business, and that only happens when the token holder has true, verifiable rights.

Overall, this demand for accountability is a positive development, but it needs to stretch beyond social-trading heuristics and into changing how we invest as an industry.

For the very few serious folks left here who remain attentive, start paying attention to MetaDAO and its ecosystem right now. If you want an actual playground of assets that are not valued at an uninvestable premium, with verifiable rights within the business, then this is the only place to meet that demand.

If you want to long accountability, I would suggest paying attention to the one place that offers it.

author: banteg
quoted_text:
We should continue towards Glam activation asap.

A lot of research went into Glam's strategy to increase opcode gas prices for state creation.

It seems fair to say that the timing of this debate is irrelevant as to its correctness or rightness for eth and our users... Yet, why did some of us (eg. quoted author who is an ef board member) only start looking in detail at Glam EIPs eg. after testnet forks started? This isn't a personal attack, it's an observation that there's a collective responsibility-- for OP, for me, for all of us-- to steward fork strategy at the right times in the process.

imo ethereum's commitments to apps do not extend to gas pricing, or to total ETH fee levels, or to USD fees. And also not to opcode pricing or gas introspection that depends on those prices. We guarantee maximally credibly neutral, maximally live access to the correct state transition function. Those guarantees imply that we always use a neutral pricing mechanism to clear congestion wherever possible. However, pricing opcodes can't use a neutral mechanism, we need to pick magic number opcode gas prices. Some of our best people researched this extensively and picked updated magic numbers, and that's something imo we should stick with now and continue our larger plans that are on track to grow to global ubiquity.

The good news and practical reality may be that the explosion of blockspace supply from 60M to 200M gas limit seems likely to absolutely crater the L1 gas price. It will take time for demand to grow to meet the new supply, including from net new entrants (eg. GENIUS and institutions), induced demand from lower prices, and the coming next gen of return-to-mainnet-type eth native apps. 

By the time L1 blockspace demand catches up, we will be exploding supply again as we get closer to the full lean eth vision. That's eth's vision: postquantum and postAI ETH SoV, supported by ethereum's hypergrowing capacity, which is supported by best-in-class security and formal verification.

Looking back, it's unfortunate that we provided these affected contracts with a footgun that has put them in the situation where they were *able* to rely on fake guarantees that ethereum never promises (afaik, essentially just gas introspection). We're sorry.

imo it's time to roll forward on this. Let's do what we can in an appropriately scoped capacity for the affected contracts, then activate Glam asap, and continue our excellent progress towards global ubiquity.

This is the first Ethereum talk I've watched this year, and uuugh...

Lemme speak as an outsider, who for whatever reason still has most of his net worth in ETH. This entire Ether issuance discussion is so stupid.

There is this bigass skeleton in the closet, and everyone pretends we don't see it. Let me shine some light: there is fuck-all to do on Ethereum. <gasp>

The reason so many people have ETH is because they believe in this shit - I believe in this shit -, and the reason everyone stakes ETH is because there isn't anything else to do with it!

Sure, you can shove it in the casino and hope it doesn't get drained; or when shit hits the fan, that you're awake to pull out before the cards fall. Who in their right mind would consider that a store of value?

The entire Ether issuance discussion is trying to remedy the symptom instead of the root of the problem. The symptom is that everyone wants to stake instead of using the network, so there's no economic activity being generated. Your thinking is that by reducing the staking rewards, you are stimulating economic activity. No dum-dum, by reducing the issuance you're making people choose between the casino or exiting. This isn't fiat where you're forced geopolitically into a specific currency; you can just sell this shit.

Stop fucking with monetary policy and start making useful shit that people want to use in their day to day lives. Improve the human condition and they will spend ETH on it and generate economic activity. Improve the reliability of the ecosystem so people aren't afraid of losing their saving while they sleep. Figure out recourse mechanisms so when shit hits the fan, the little guy doesn't crash and burn. Maybe then people will also use Ether, not just keep it under the pillow.

The problem isn't that staked Ether isn't generating activity; the problem is that active Ether's is fucking risky. People want to live their lives, not play onchain PvP against the entire world. I can't believe I have to be the one to fucking say this out aloud.

Cheers, hit like and subscribe for next year's post-devcon rant from Lisbon 🫡

text:
Finally solved the long-standing issue with Linux on Apple Silicon, power management

Neo during suspend now draws **0.05 W** on average, just like macOS. It cuts off the power rail to SoC while keeping DRAM in self-refresh loop and still supports wake over LAN/USB/BT, so it works well in docked setups too

And now it's finally possible to just let your Mac running Linux sleep for days without losing battery (well, negligible amounts)! Most of the time was spent covering all sorts of edge cases with USB / weird coprocessor gotchas across suspend

As expected, it wasn't too big like the GPU work was (just difficult to get right, and touches a fairly big amount of subsystems to implement suspend/wake in each) - needed me to sit down for a while and actually get it done... it took a lot of tiny details to get here, but I've finally developed a nearly complete understanding of how it works. 2 days into this rabbit hole and the result is, deep sleep works on Neo and expectedly super similar across M4-M6, where deep WFI looks a little different, others on team like Andreas and @tiredkebab have gotten it to work on M1/M2 as well

Technical deep dive in a blog post coming soon from me and @RyanTheTide regarding the whole Neo bringup we did in the matter of 2 months, it's been a lot of fun & it's just the beginning of what @AuroraSilicon team is doing with @OmarchyMac 

Will be working on shipping this feature to our mainline kernel now

text:
There were no lessons learned from what happened with EOF and that stack of EIPs was tame compared to the precedent being set here.

People that actually build on Ethereum start to understand the impact and it’s “testnets are live”, “too late to change”, “just ship it”.

No one is arguing that the intent of these EIPs - properly charging for state growth relative to other operations - is bad. The pushback is on how it erodes trust assumptions for builders and changes how they have to think about long term operations.

If we 5x storage costs and 5x black gas limits, did we really scale or did we just make bigger numbers? Sure, you can pack in more non-state ops if those stay the same but did anyone run the numbers on lowering the cost of non-state changing operations and keeping block gas the same?
author: 0xjustadev
quoted_text:
We should continue towards Glam activation asap.

A lot of research went into Glam's strategy to increase opcode gas prices for state creation.

It seems fair to say that the timing of this debate is irrelevant as to its correctness or rightness for eth and our users... Yet, why did some of us (eg. quoted author who is an ef board member) only start looking in detail at Glam EIPs eg. after testnet forks started? This isn't a personal attack, it's an observation that there's a collective responsibility-- for OP, for me, for all of us-- to steward fork strategy at the right times in the process.

imo ethereum's commitments to apps do not extend to gas pricing, or to total ETH fee levels, or to USD fees. And also not to opcode pricing or gas introspection that depends on those prices. We guarantee maximally credibly neutral, maximally live access to the correct state transition function. Those guarantees imply that we always use a neutral pricing mechanism to clear congestion wherever possible. However, pricing opcodes can't use a neutral mechanism, we need to pick magic number opcode gas prices. Some of our best people researched this extensively and picked updated magic numbers, and that's something imo we should stick with now and continue our larger plans that are on track to grow to global ubiquity.

The good news and practical reality may be that the explosion of blockspace supply from 60M to 200M gas limit seems likely to absolutely crater the L1 gas price. It will take time for demand to grow to meet the new supply, including from net new entrants (eg. GENIUS and institutions), induced demand from lower prices, and the coming next gen of return-to-mainnet-type eth native apps. 

By the time L1 blockspace demand catches up, we will be exploding supply again as we get closer to the full lean eth vision. That's eth's vision: postquantum and postAI ETH SoV, supported by ethereum's hypergrowing capacity, which is supported by best-in-class security and formal verification.

Looking back, it's unfortunate that we provided these affected contracts with a footgun that has put them in the situation where they were *able* to rely on fake guarantees that ethereum never promises (afaik, essentially just gas introspection). We're sorry.

imo it's time to roll forward on this. Let's do what we can in an appropriately scoped capacity for the affected contracts, then activate Glam asap, and continue our excellent progress towards global ubiquity.

text:
What’s interesting is that trust in software so far has been based on human networks of trust. 

Do I trust this guy? Do I trust this project? Do I trust this company? Do I trust this public key?

It’s all social based. 

It’s not going away because we still use services all over the place, but more and more can be audited/verified thanks to agents now. 

We already see people auditing all their dependencies (and we are doing it in https://t.co/7cXiT26cQQ for our users now), or people even inlining their dependencies. 

I guess there is a trade off that people are getting at: should I trust agents rewriting and auditing this code for me, or should I trust other humans to maintain this part of the code for me. 

Hopefully we can help with that part soon as well.
author: cryptodavidw
quoted_text:
Frontier cyber agents are getting better at two things at once: finding vulnerabilities and staying inside the rules researchers set. The harder part is no longer just model capability; it’s where the system still fails once the model is good enough to act.

1) OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, up from 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and 40.3% recall on a new offensive web vuln-discovery eval vs 32.0% for GPT-6 Astra. They also report 99.93% out-of-scope avoidance without the deployment prompt, and 100% with it. The release also claims it helped develop 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits and identify 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulns. These are vendor-reported numbers, so the takeaway is capability is rising, but the claims still need independent validation.

2) Signed but Not Safe shows what happens at the handoff layer in multi-agent systems. In a preregistered study, signed requirement manifests cut unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% with Qwen3-8B, and the verifier beat an LLM checker on the same trajectories. But signing only protects requirements in transit: when the orchestrator extracted the wrong requirement before signing, the signature faithfully preserved the mistake. The residual risk is extraction.

3) SPILLWAY makes a similar point for tool-using agents. It separates target admission from sanitization, using deterministic checks on typed tool returns plus a sanitizer that strips injected instructions before the model reads them. Across the tested backbones and suites, in-scope attack success went to zero. Its limitation is explicit: it covers identity targets, depends on declared tool roles, and still leaves some cases to a judge and delegation rules.

Taken together, these are not proofs of a universal shift, but they do show where the practical trust boundary is moving in evaluated agent systems: provenance, extraction, typed tool outputs, and deterministic enforcement around the loop.

Shanghai is officially joining my annual rotation, it’s the greatest T1 city.

I’ve started building a personal list of places I want to revisit every year for as long as I can: Miami, Shanghai, the Côte d’Azur and Dubai.

The idea is simple: every year, rotate one destination out and bring somewhere new in.

After 10+ trips to the US over the past few years, I removed NYC (although I’ll land there for business reasons regardless). I’m starting to feel a little burnt out. The value for money just isn’t there anymore.

Anytime I’m in the US I spend 20k USD for essentially not that much, visiting 2-3 cities, eating „good“.

Still Miami is awesome, bc I can easily escape for a low cortisol week to the great beaches in western Florida.

Shanghai, on the other hand, might be one of the best risk/reward travel decisions I’ve made in a while.

Haven’t been to Bangkok… or Kuala Lumpur but I doubt they fall into the category of a T1 place. I just think the quality matters more then a few % off in $.

On to Singapore / Kuala Lumpur next.

深扒了《持械入宋》，我自己看了 6 季，非常好看。成功绝非偶然，也不是一句“AI 平权”就能说完的。我深入发现了几个细节。

1. 主创张汉生 54 岁，2025 年 3 月才开始学 AI，之前多次创业失败，零影视经验。
2. 前面近一年他靠接承制订单练手，团队做了近 40 部剧，流水剧时期一个月最多约 20 部，直到 2026 年 3–4 月自己做的两部剧分别破千万、破亿，才算真正打出来。
3. 从这时候起他开始组建团队，队伍从 1 个人慢慢变成 3 个人，做第四部剧的时候变成 5 个人，思路也变了：不做流水剧了，做精品剧。
4. 精品剧是怎么做出来的？先花半个月通读原著、多轮改剧本、打磨人设，先做 10 集内部确认方向对了，才大面积铺开。
5. 考证下得非常细：官服什么品色、配饰、鞋履、户籍和路引、礼仪位次，还有剧里的医学知识、宋朝背景，全都查过。
6. 他们还取消了穿越剧标配的“系统”，没有金手指，一个无穿帮的片段内部可能只有 60 分，没情绪就是废卡，第六季一场送葬戏，总导演做的时候自己哭了。
7. 每做完一季，他们先看评论区、粉丝群和原著粉群的反馈，再决定下一季往哪里调。
8. 团队 30 多人分散在广东、安徽、湖北、江西、福建、河北，全靠微信群加网盘协作，没办公室，没固定工资。
9. 自 8 月上线走红以来，全员一次都没成功聚过，几个月前就想找个山清水秀的地方吃顿饭，一直没成行。
10. 火了之后主创最怕被当成神话，张汉生说 AI 平权只是模型使用机会的平等，不会自动拉平故事判断，更不会替人完成长期练习。

The story keeps getting crazier. To recap everything that has been reported so far: 

- The US intelligence community discovered that Jensen Huang, the CEO of the largest company in the world, was sleeping with Alice Huang, a Chinese spy and an executive at Megaspeed. (FT)
- Multiple independent investigations have concluded that Megaspeed is likely a Chinese cutout, which helps Chinese companies access AI chips or circumvent export controls. (NYT and Bloomberg) 
- The US intelligence community also concluded that Alice Huang’s goal was to convince Jensen to lobby the U.S. government to loosen export controls on advanced AI chips. (NYT)
- The intelligence community relayed this information to “a small group of top US government officials” earlier this year. (FT)
- Over the last year, Jensen Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to loosen export controls on advanced chips. @BISgov has done so, not only by permitting the export of H200 chips to China, but also not enforcing export controls that would have required a license for exports of the most advanced Blackwell chips to Megaspeed and Southeast Asia.
- Although @CommerceGov leadership was presumably briefed on this information by the U.S. intelligence community, @BISgov has taken no actions to tighten controls on Megaspeed or Southeast Asia. 
- Megaspeed remains a preferred cloud partner of Nvidia, and continues to receive Nvidia Blackwell chips despite employing a Chinese spy who reportedly is romantically engaged with the CEO of Nvidia. 
- Tens of billions of dollars worth of AI chips have been exported to Southeast Asia this year alone, and Malaysia and Singapore are now two of the four largest importers of AI chips in the world. 

What is going on here??? We need answers. The question of who gets the most advanced AI chips in the world is literally the defining strategic question of our time. And not only does it seem like the MSS may be directly influencing the debate on export controls in the United States, but also @CommerceGov is refusing to listen to the warnings of the IC on this issue. What is a POSSIBLE good explanation for why Megaspeed is still receiving chips? Why is there not a license requirement for AI chip shipments to all of Southeast Asia? This is beyond strange at this point. 

The fallout from this story will be massive. Obviously, the motivations underpinning Nvidia’s policy views opposing export controls must now all be questioned. But also, how did @BISgov sit on this information and has still taken no actions? We need answers.

text:
This sounds extreme and I wouldn’t have believed it even a year ago, but we’re starting to see plenty of examples of productivity gains that are an order of magnitude or two above output levels pre-AI. 

With the right harness, a deep understanding of your domain of what you want to build, likely a relatively new codebase (with some exceptions), a fluency of how to work with multiple agents at once, and a setup that makes it so you can test and deploy with limited friction, outputs on this level feel realistic in coding.  

What’s crazy is this gap doesn’t appear to be diminishing over time. You’d think that we’d see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before -and willingness now to take a different approach- gives you crazy leverage. And that is only compounding as the models can take on larger work and harder problems.

Right now this is most pronounced in software engineering for the obvious reasons. But there’s no reason we don’t start to see this in a number of other computer-use-sensitive domains like other scientific fields, AEC, finance, cyber, and more. Going to get quite wild.

text:
$ASTS is building its own rocket 🚀 👇 

AST SpaceMobile just announced Blacklift, a ~20-ton reusable launch vehicle powered by $FLY Firefly Aerospace's Miranda engines.

The deal:

• Up to 5 BlueBird satellites per launch
• Target: operational by late 2028
• Perpetual license to build Miranda + vacuum Vira engines in-house, at a new U.S. facility
• ~$800M upfront ($400M cash + 10–14M Class A shares)
• $250M for engines for the first 3 rockets
• $250M for 3 years of engineering services

 👉 Roughly $1.3B in total commitments

What it means for AST:

AST wants full vertical integration: satellites, manufacturing, and now launch. Licensing a ground-tested engine, instead of building one from scratch, is meant to skip the usual 5–10 year development cycle.

✅ Bull case

• Launch is the biggest bottleneck for constellation rollout. Owning it de-risks the long-term deployment schedule.
• Better launch economics at scale
• Opens doors beyond direct-to-device: U.S. government radar, secure comms, IoT, emergency services, edge compute
• Sovereign U.S. launch capability is a strong asset with defense customers
• The engine: 175+ hot-fire tests, ~20 first-stage flights' worth of runtime

⚠️ Bear case

• Capital intensity: ~$1.3B committed before a single launch
• Dilution: 10-14M new shares to Firefly
• Execution risk: rockets are hard. The engine is ground-tested, but the vehicle doesn't exist yet.
• Late 2028 means zero impact on the near-term rollout. 2027–28 still runs on external launch contracts covering 100+ satellites.
• Target: operational by late 2028: Most likely by 2030 or later.

My take:

This is a long-term strategic bet, not a near-term catalyst. If Blacklift works, AST becomes a far more defensible, fully integrated space infrastructure company. If it slips, it's an expensive distraction. I'm closely following the unveiling on Nov 12 in NYC for cost-per-launch, the launch site and the funding plan.

7 years ago everyone said that the BlueBirds won't happen. The truth is: Never Bet against Abel! 

Not financial advice. I'm long $ASTS.

整个过程只有 3 分钟，高度自动化

《$BEM：披着 Meme 外衣的狼——币圈第一个真正“破圈进 AI”的项目》

铭文时代，ordi 是代表，后面无数铭文，不过是各家项目方的炒作噱头。

而链上电路 / PoD 挖矿这条赛道，代表币只有一个：$BEM。

很多人误读了官方那两种晶体管。它们不是终点，是“概念 NFT、基础插件”——作用是证明这套东西跑得通：链上电路元件可以运行，新规则、新边界被开出来了。就像 ordi 当年证明了比特币链上能刻图片，牛的是这一步本身。

真正的价值在第三方。

以后市场上无数新晶体管，才是“真实 NFT、实用高效插件”。因为要发行它们，你必须质押并消耗 BEM——链上电路领域唯一的代表货币。这就像铭文圈发币不能只烧 BTC，还得消耗 ordi，才能决定新 Meme 的产量。

所以，从此分成两个圈：

第一个圈，官方晶体管 + 官方矿机，散户投资。本质是押注一件事——链上电路这个概念，会被 AI 圈的程序员和真实应用需求真的拿过去用。BEM 的供应，从来不指望炒币的来拉盘。

第二个圈，是创始人和这个行业。挖矿四年减半，就是给四年时间，让 AI 圈彻底开始用链上电路。“扩展插槽”这词太唬人、听着很菜，但它才是真正的王——官方晶体管只负责证明概念，插槽晶体管才能做出市场真正需要的链上处理器。

再往远看一步：

TapeOut 想做的是链上机器宪法。

你的 AI 项目需不需要一个第三方审核软件？让用户零电费调用链上处理器，24 小时不停帮你验算。协议公开透明、算法无法篡改、结果无法被改，比任何人类公司和法院都更冰冷、公正——用来审判 AI 的每一步决策是否“道德”。

这才是真正的铭文：程序律法溶解进区块链。

假设有 4399 条链上律法，每个 AI 领域的人按需引用，去验证真实世界的东西。

ordi 炒的是小图片和收藏，到链下有什么实用工具？没有。

铭文破不了币圈。TapeOut 看着是 BNB 链上的 Meme，实际做的是破整个币圈。

别因为它在 BNB 链，就觉得不如 BTC 链。它的价值不由链本身束缚——币圈几万亿美金的总市值，会因为这场与 AI 的联姻，增长几万亿。

我的建议：买一些 BEM，然后忘掉它。
