quoted_text:
Even though I disagree with some of the assumptions made, this is a good write-up of the discussion, and I appreciate the perspective on the benefits and the conclusion that Glamsterdam should proceed.

There really are two classes of “invariants”
- *Parameters*, eg, gas cost of an operation or block time
- Pricing *mechanisms* for operations

Contracts should not rely on the first class not changing. However mechanisms should be updated ideally in a non-breaking manner.

Glamsterdam has a mix of both changes. Unfortunately, a planned mechanism update (EIP-8037) produces breaking changes where we should not expect some to be, hence the additional delay

In any case, if either of the two categories sees some change, every effort should be made to identify and support apps that are directly or indirectly affected. It could be that the gas cost update makes a specific use case relatively more expensive, or cheaper, changing app economics.

A repository was released for app devs to identify the changes https://t.co/H3XuZZZZVL Internal and external audits have already led to active outreach, this step is designed for last mile coverage

Most of tokenization can’t really be classified as “DeFi” in the traditional, or even practical sense. 

Today, the purest form of DeFi is actually Prediction Markets.

PMs port information onchain without permission or centralized intermediaries. 

An event contract derives its value from the physical offchain world, but no central party can stop the value (information) from flowing.

You can’t stop an event from happening because there’s a prediction market on it the same way you can block a redemption or freeze a tokenized asset.

The only missing piece left to make prediction markets feel more DeFi-ish is financial-lego composability.

When we say “DeFi” we automatically think of composability because it’s something that tradfi can never have.

It’s finally time to add prediction markets to our repertoire of DeFi legos.

Pure DeFi in its ultimate form.

author: suppvalen
quoted_text:
⚠️ Crypto was built to give us financial freedom. So why are centralized exchanges starting to feel like traditional banks?

A crypto user has shared a disturbing experience.

He withdrew 2,690 USDT from @MEXC to @OKXmena via the Aptos network. The deposit was marked as completed, yet shortly afterward, OKX temporarily restricted his account for 60 days.

His support team reportedly provided only generic explanations about security issues.

The screenshots speak for themselves.

Now, let's be clear: exchanges have every right to comply with AML regulations and protect their platforms. But when legitimate crypto transfers can trigger prolonged account restrictions, users deserve more than vague explanations.

This raises a serious question:

Are we slowly rebuilding the same financial system that Bitcoin was created to challenge?

Satoshi Nakamoto envisioned a decentralized financial system. A system where people could control their own money without relying on centralized gatekeepers.

But today, as exchanges tighten compliance and expand their control over user funds, that vision seems to be fading.

I've been in crypto for years. What attracted me was its permissionless, decentralized, and somewhat wild nature.

I understand regulation. I understand security.

But I don't want crypto to become TradFi with a blockchain logo.

Maybe I'm too pessimistic.

Or maybe we're witnessing the gradual loss of what made crypto special in the first place.

What do you think? Is this the price of crypto going mainstream, or are we moving too far away from Satoshi's vision?

✅ BENCHMARKED: @NaceAI's Drex Max open-weight model makes decisions in under a second on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini, running on their own Kapitsa runtime.

Nace just published a technical report on how these decision models are trained. I ran the open Drex Max v1 weights locally to see what that looks like on a Mac.

They released Drex Max as an open-weight decision model, plus Kapitsa, a runtime for Macs. Instead of generating a response token by token, Drex Max takes a prompt (say, a document and the possible decisions) and one forward pass returns a probability for each decision.

I ran the official affine Q4 weights on Kapitsa and on MLX. Kapitsa took 9 to 20% less time, even with tokenization and HTTP handling inside its timer.

Median decision-making times for Kapitsa:

- 507 token prompt: 0.95 s
- 2,037 token prompt: 3.34 s
- 4,094 token prompt: 7.88 s

TLDR: If your use case involves relatively short contexts, you can get a decision in ~1s on your Mac using Nace's Drex Max model + Kapitsa runtime.

text:
SpaceX has outlined five contingency landing options for Starship Flight 15 as it prepares for the ship’s first tower-catch attempt at Starbase

This visualization shows how the mission can change course if the vehicle or tower does not meet the conditions required for a safe return:

1. Indian Ocean — after ascent
If the orbital insertion burn is skipped, Starship remains on its suborbital trajectory and reenters over a predetermined area of the Indian Ocean

2. North of Hawaii — early in the mission
If the flight needs to end shortly after reaching orbit, Starship returns to a designated area of the Pacific north of Hawaii

3. Off Chile — mid-mission
A separate return opportunity allows Starship to land in the eastern Pacific, far off the coast of Chile

4. Gulf offshore — catch contingency
If the tower catch is called off before final approach, Starship has an offshore landing option in the Gulf instead of proceeding with the catch

5. North of Hawaii — late in the mission
If the planned deorbit burn is skipped, Starship completes another orbit before returning to the Pacific north of Hawaii

The objective is to bring Starship home. The flight plan builds in alternatives throughout the journey, with continuous vehicle-health checks determining when to proceed

An ambitious mission, backed by carefully planned options from ascent to final approach

text:
This is going around as a funny copy pasta, but a lot of people don't understand why Predictive Allocation is such a game changer for on chain LPs and $AERO.

Let's say you're an on chain LP and you think that oil is about to go crazy over the weekend because of rumours that the US will start bombing Iran.

You hop on to Uniswap and see that OIL/USDC has only been paying 30% APR because very little trading had occurred the week prior. The LP fees are backwards looking. You could deploy some capital now, but then you risk only getting paid higher LP fees briefly before wicking out of range.

Then you go over to @aeroxyz and see that OIL/USDC is paying 100% APR in $AERO emissions. The reason is because sAERO allocators are betting that the OIL pairs will have crazy volatility/volume on the weekend right alongside you, and so they've directed their votes to those pools predictively to capture that fee share.

But markets are efficient, so what ends up happening? LPs from UNI pull their capital and move it over to Aero until the rates normalize. 

Aero enables emissions to be directed as a forward looking bet rather than displayed as a backwards looking snapshot. This means Aero will attract more liquidity when organic market forces deem it's actually needed, which means tigher spreads, which means more volume routed through Aero, which means more fees for sAERO stakers.

This advantage only gets magnified by more RWAs coming on chain when there are earnings reports and other pre-defined catalysts for volume. sAERO allocators have an economic incentive to dynamically adjust emissions to attract the deepest liquidity before it's actually needed; this is a mechanic that other AMM designs simply can't replicate.

粗暴点评价这件事 
我觉得是安全意识和常识都有点不够

先说常识 ：

虽然两个 APP 是一样的品牌
但他们需要分别注册账号和 KYC 才能使用

因为合规标准因素
所支持的交易对和功能也会存在差异

而且同一身份在同一平台不能重复 KYC
却需要在两个平台分别认证

这就已经说明了双方账号体系并不互通
本质上就是跨平台转账

还有一点就是

所以要求其中一个平台

并不是想操作就能操作的
就算是在同一个 APP 里也需要走流程

我一般进行转账前都会先小额测试

当事人会想从 A 所转到 B 所
代表他已经下载注册并且进行了 KYC 

理论上来说
能看到自己 B 所的 UID 和地址不一样吧
没下载过 这点我就不评价了
如果没有反复查验就转 那真的很粗心

小额测试这个习惯肯定是要培养的
如果有测试 就能在事情发生前发现问题

总的来说 这件事能找回最好

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Ron Baron is 83. In front of thousands of investors in New York, he looked at Elon Musk and asked the one question an 83-year-old asks.

"How do you want people to think about you?"

For the full hour before, it had been trillion-dollar chip fabs. Starship. Starlink. The business of the richest man alive.

Then Baron added, quieter: "Nobody would work the way you work just to accumulate money."

Elon paused.

"I'd like the reality to be that I made a significant contribution in the furtherance of civilization."

One sentence. Civilization.

And then, in the same room, he told them about Jose.

Jose is the guy in the meme. One man digging a hole in the road. Eight men standing around watching him dig.

"Unless you increase the number of Joses in the country, the amount of work done does not increase."

"I aspire to be Jose."
"We do actual work."

This from a man who lives in an Airstream parked next to his power plant in Memphis. Who pulls power cables "the size of an anaconda" with his own hands.

Asked how he wants history to remember him, he said civilization.

Asked who he wants to be, he said the guy with the shovel.

The richest man in the world wants to dig. 🇺🇸🚀

Over the past several hours, teams across MEXC have been actively engaging in discussions and coordinating with relevant parties to move things forward.

text:
There’s a method taught at Y Combinator that turns 4 weeks of GTM research into 3 hrs.

And no, it’s not typing “research the market for X” into Claude.

You start by feeding it raw material:
→ 25-40 competitor websites, fully scraped (pricing pages, case studies, docs)
→ The last few earnings calls from the 3-5 biggest incumbents
→ 100+ customer reviews (G2, Capterra, Trustpilot, app stores)
→ Every Reddit or forum thread where people vent about the category

Then ask questions that force it to think, not summarize:

1. “What do the winners in this market know that their customers would never admit?”
2. “List the beliefs this whole industry takes for granted. For each one, what would need to happen for it to be false?”

In about 20 min, you’ll see where everyone agrees, where everyone is blind, and which customer pains nobody is building for.

Now flip it. Pick your best angle and tell Claude to tear it apart:

“Steelman this thesis like a top-tier VC would. Then show me exactly where it fails.”

Do a few rounds of that. 3 hours later, you’ll have a first GTM hypothesis that sounds like it came from a 10-year industry veteran.

The trick is treating Claude as a sparring partner that never gets tired and never gets defensive when it’s wrong.

But remember: it’s still just a hypothesis. The real work starts when you talk to actual buyers.

To get there fast, use Gojiberry to find and reach the right people to test it with.

Customer conversations are the only thing that matters.

This is the first Ethereum talk I've watched this year, and uuugh...

Lemme speak as an outsider, who for whatever reason still has most of his net worth in ETH. This entire Ether issuance discussion is so stupid.

There is this bigass skeleton in the closet, and everyone pretends we don't see it. Let me shine some light: there is fuck-all to do on Ethereum. <gasp>

The reason so many people have ETH is because they believe in this shit - I believe in this shit -, and the reason everyone stakes ETH is because there isn't anything else to do with it!

Sure, you can shove it in the casino and hope it doesn't get drained; or when shit hits the fan, that you're awake to pull out before the cards fall. Who in their right mind would consider that a store of value?

The entire Ether issuance discussion is trying to remedy the symptom instead of the root of the problem. The symptom is that everyone wants to stake instead of using the network, so there's no economic activity being generated. Your thinking is that by reducing the staking rewards, you are stimulating economic activity. No dum-dum, by reducing the issuance you're making people choose between the casino or exiting. This isn't fiat where you're forced geopolitically into a specific currency; you can just sell this shit.

Stop fucking with monetary policy and start making useful shit that people want to use in their day to day lives. Improve the human condition and they will spend ETH on it and generate economic activity. Improve the reliability of the ecosystem so people aren't afraid of losing their saving while they sleep. Figure out recourse mechanisms so when shit hits the fan, the little guy doesn't crash and burn. Maybe then people will also use Ether, not just keep it under the pillow.

The problem isn't that staked Ether isn't generating activity; the problem is that active Ether's is fucking risky. People want to live their lives, not play onchain PvP against the entire world. I can't believe I have to be the one to fucking say this out aloud.

Cheers, hit like and subscribe for next year's post-devcon rant from Lisbon 🫡

✅ BENCHMARKED: @NaceAI's Drex Max open-weight model makes decisions in under a second on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini, running on their own Kapitsa runtime.

Nace just published a technical report on how these decision models are trained. I ran the open Drex Max v1 weights locally to see what that looks like on a Mac.

They released Drex Max as an open-weight decision model, plus Kapitsa, a runtime for Macs. Instead of generating a response token by token, Drex Max takes a prompt (say, a document and the possible decisions) and one forward pass returns a probability for each decision.

I ran the official affine Q4 weights on Kapitsa and on MLX. Kapitsa took 9 to 20% less time, even with tokenization and HTTP handling inside its timer.

Median decision-making times for Kapitsa:

- 507 token prompt: 0.95 s
- 2,037 token prompt: 3.34 s
- 4,094 token prompt: 7.88 s

TLDR: If your use case involves relatively short contexts, you can get a decision in ~1s on your Mac using Nace's Drex Max model + Kapitsa runtime.

text:
Tristan Thompson on Building Wealth, Managing Risk, and Inspiring the Next Generation

In this episode of When Shift Happens, I sit down with NBA champion, entrepreneur, and investor @TThompson to discuss his journey from growing up in Toronto to competing at the highest level of professional basketball, and how those experiences shaped his approach to investing, wealth, and emerging technologies. We explore the lessons he learned from financial mistakes, why he believes patience and discipline matter more than chasing quick returns, and how he is positioning himself for a future shaped by digital assets, artificial intelligence, and robotics.

From Financial Struggles to an NBA Championship

Growing up in Toronto in a Jamaican family, Tristan watched his mother work three jobs while his family navigated financial hardship, government assistance, and his brother's epilepsy. These experiences fueled his ambition to create a better life for the people who had sacrificed so much for him.

His first sporting passion was soccer, influenced by Jamaica's historic qualification for the 1998 FIFA World Cup. But as he grew taller and basketball gained popularity in Toronto, particularly through Vince Carter and the Raptors, he found himself drawn to a different sport. That decision eventually took him to the University of Texas, the NBA, and an NBA championship. Basketball gave him the financial means to support his family, but it also developed the discipline, resilience, and competitive mindset that now guide his investments.

Why Tristan Invests in People Before Companies

After competing against some of basketball's greatest players, like LeBron James, Kobe Bryant, and Stephen Curry, Tristan believes that adaptability, not talent alone, determines who succeeds. He looks for similar qualities in entrepreneurs. "I invest in great founders that will do whatever they can to achieve greatness, but also still have some sense of reality on when to pivot."

That balance between determination and adaptability is particularly important because Tristan recognizes it as one of his own weaknesses. Raised with a tough-love mentality, his instinct when something goes wrong has always been to work harder, but becoming a parent helped him understand that persistence isn't always the answer. Different situations, like different children, require different approaches.

Today, he applies that lesson to venture investing. While prestigious university credentials can help founders attract capital, he is more interested in their work ethic, conviction, and willingness to dedicate themselves completely to building something meaningful.

Learning to Build Wealth Without Losing It

Tristan's entry into investing showed him that financial education matters, and that earning and managing money are entirely different skills. Professional athletes, particularly younger athletes who secure lucrative endorsement and name, image, and likeness deals, are vulnerable to people looking to profit from their wealth. His own approach was shaped by experienced mentors, and now he tries to offer that same guidance to younger athletes.

His advice is to start small, understand your appetite for risk, and never assume every investment will deliver extraordinary returns. In fact, his firsthand experience with a memecoin trade where he lost the potential for multiple seven figures taught him the importance of taking profits and how greed can undermine good decisions.

He believes this explains why wealthy people across different professions sometimes lose everything. Success can encourage overconfidence, excessive leverage, and the desire to prove that an investment thesis was right. The danger is especially real in crypto, where rapidly accumulated wealth can begin to feel disconnected from its real-world value. But for Tristan, growing up with limited resources taught him that money represents opportunities to support a family, purchase tangible assets, and build long-term security.

Taking Calculated Risks in Crypto and Venture Capital

Tristan's investment strategy combines long-term conviction with a willingness to take calculated risks. In crypto, Bitcoin represents approximately 10-15% of his personal wealth, and he considers it as both digital gold and a form of long-term savings or retirement account. He also holds Solana, which he credits for making financial products more accessible and easier for everyday users.

His venture investments follow a similarly diversified approach. Early-stage companies offer the possibility of substantial returns but carry significant risk, while later-stage opportunities are less risky. One successful investment was Poppi, which he invested in at the pre-seed stage and was later acquired by PepsiCo. He is also exploring opportunities in physical AI and robotics, including an investment in Prometheus, which could transform warehouse operations. For him, the broader lesson is that building wealth requires balancing conviction with an understanding that even promising investments can fail.

Investing in a Future Shaped by AI and Robotics

Tristan's interest in emerging technology extends beyond digital finance. He is particularly enthusiastic about robotics. He sees opportunities in practical applications that make businesses more efficient, from helping consumers find reliable service providers to automating warehouse operations. His investment thesis focuses on companies using technology to solve tangible problems rather than simply building another AI model.

However, he also recognizes that increased automation will transform employment. As machines take over more repetitive tasks, workers will need to demonstrate what makes their contributions difficult to replace. His answer is creativity.
"Life creates creativity. Stress creates creativity. Heartache creates creativity."
He believes human experiences, relationships, and problem-solving abilities will remain valuable even as technology advances.

The Next Championship Is Bigger Than Basketball

For someone who has already achieved success at the highest level of professional sports, Tristan's ambitions remain remarkably competitive. He wants to establish himself in venture capital and prove that business excellence doesn't require a conventional background or an elite university degree.
But his ultimate definition of success extends beyond personal wealth.
"I don't want to be at a table and be the only king at the table. I want to be at the table with a bunch of kings and queens."

Tristan wants to inspire the next generation to recognize that success and financial freedom aren't limited to careers in sports or entertainment. He hopes to show others, particularly those from backgrounds like his, that there are other paths to building wealth and creating better opportunities for their families. And he plans to keep building without losing sight of why he started.

👉If you enjoyed reading the summary, head over to When Shift Happens on YouTube or your favorite podcast platform to access the full convo.

author: IamRamenPanda
quoted_text:
很多人总有一种错觉：只要我不碰期权、不加十倍杠杆，老老实实买正股，就算买错了顶多也是拿时间换空间，怎么可能亏大钱？

10 月底，一位叫 0nth3sp3ctrum 的老哥晒出了自己的 4 张 Robinhood 实盘持仓截图，直接用血淋淋的账户余额给所有“正股死多头”上了一课。

他在帖子里第一句话就强调：今年是我交易生涯最惨的一年，账户里没有任何期权，全都是实打实的正股。

他是怎么在标普 500 年初至今依然上涨超 10% 的行情里，把一身正股买成灾难现场的？翻开他的四张截图，几乎浓缩了散户在网红叙事里接盘的全部标准动作：

看到存储芯片大牛股美光（MU）财报落地，他满怀憧憬地冲进去重仓接盘，赌它能瞬间重返历史最高点，结果进去就是山顶；看到闪迪（SNDK）热度爆棚，赶在大跳水前夕一头扎进去站岗；最要命的是，他以接近 98.5 美元的高位均价，重仓买了将近 5000 股太空通信概念股 ASTS（光这一只票就砸进去近 50 万美元），结果眼睁睁看着股价一路阴跌、深不见底。

这位老哥原本有个雷打不动的习惯：每年年底前都会把所有仓位清掉变现，干干净净拿着现金过年。今年前几个月，他好不容易在市场里攒下了 20 万美元的已实现利润，结果因为年底前连续在高位接盘这几只热门正股，不仅把一整年的利润全部吐光，连手头的流动现金都彻底枯竭，被迫从“短线波段客”熬成了“跨年股东”。

他的选股策略到底是什么？是不是只要看到论坛里哪只股票被吹上天、涨幅已经翻了几倍，就立刻冲进去帮别人买单？

不碰期权，只能保证你不会在明天下午四点准时归零；但如果你总是等一个故事全网皆知、市盈率被炒上天时才去重仓正股，阴跌不止的钝刀子割肉，同样能把你几年的积蓄磨成灰。

你手里现在有没有哪只原本只想做个短线波段、结果硬生生买成“传家宝”的正股？

quoted_text:
over the past few months, options have been coming up more and more in my circle, and i think crypto is still massively underestimating the opportunity.

options are enormous in tradfi, yet crypto has barely made a dent in consumer adoption.

imo perps took off because they're intuitive while options still force users to understand strikes, expiries, premiums and volatility before they can even express a view.

i) for retail, the unlock is outcome-first trading. pick a view and timeframe, instantly see the cost, upside and risk.

ii) for pros, it's deep liquidity, competitive pricing, portfolio margin and efficient execution.

the challenge is making options simple without sacrificing their flexibility.

whoever gets the market structure and UX right has a massive market to unlock.

author: AdamWeitsman
quoted_text:
< the voice >

this work was made on request from someone specifically to show their gratitude for someone else. for their friendship. for their tireless efforts. for their trust. for the help they provide to more people than i can count. 

no rules. no guidance. just a symbol. a month ago - i had no idea where this would end up - but here we are. 

if you have been or know someone in recovery you know < the voice >. the one in your head that won't shut up. am i enough. do i have enough. i want to break. why am i so alone. it never goes away. what changes is the ground it stands on.

so i wrote it down. six passages of that voice at six stages of coming through. noise. nagging. just words on paper. then i made a film for each one from dozens of scribbles, photos, clips. then when the words were down - i put words to song in six original pieces of music, one per passage, melodies on keyboard, synth and guitar, finished in suno. then i built a piece of software that pulls the films through the words themselves, white toner on black paper, decaying by wrong blocks, so you catch the passages but never quite read them. i tried to come up with something that looks how the voice feels. 

the whole thing is one self-contained html file. a 1/1 that is also a 13 minute film in six chapters.

i've been asked to make a lot of things. i've never been asked to make something like this, at this scale, about something this close, for someone this close. i was humbled by the ask and i'm still a little wrecked from the making. 

site, passages, process and music are at the link. press watch the full film and give it the thirteen minutes.

thank you to @AdamWeitsman and @Dannyb0yyy_ for trusting me with this. 4.22.17 - proud of you danny 🖤

quoted_text:
Don’t agree that more capital increases TAM, but more competition can simultaneously reduce profit pools shared within that TAM (in fact, all competitive dynamics theory suggests will be the case)

I think more competition is structurally competing away returns, with the exception of the players who are demonstrating sincere competitive dynamics, which you / a16z undoubtedly are (trust me, I say that as a compliment, not critique). The rest of us have to find our sleeves of competitive advantage, but the marginal/median firm is likely dead IMHO. If you don’t have a right to win in this game, you don’t have a right to exist.

Given the larger TAM and these dynamics, it seems that profits pools are being pushed to the tails, with well capitalized/resourced/talented platform firms like a16z and smaller, boutique specialists (which I put ourselves in the camp of) making money, but the vast majority of firms in between getting slaughtered.

Overall, benefit to the innovation ecosystem, but perhaps not to the diversification of returns across the asset class

Just my two cents, which ain’t worth much, but that’s how it feels on the ground and was certainly the sentiment at our Summit (https://t.co/snrtRlJ10r) earlier this week

1. Platform Operations Remain Stable
Over the past several hours, teams across MEXC have been actively engaging in discussions and coordinating with relevant parties to move things forward.

We know what many of you are most concerned about: Has MEXC suspended deposits and withdrawals? Are users' assets safe?

I would like to give you my assurance: deposits and withdrawals on MEXC have continued to operate smoothly. Our teams have also been actively assisting users who need help completing their transactions.

We have indeed seen an increase in withdrawal volumes, but everything has remained orderly. We sincerely appreciate the understanding and trust our users have shown MEXC at this critical moment.

2. Meaningful Progress with KYT Service Providers
At the same time, we’ve been working closely with blockchain analytics providers.

Elliptic, one of the world’s leading KYT service providers, has confirmed that MEXC Global has returned to the “Exchange” category in its systems. At this stage, the previous special risk classification has been removed, and MEXC is classified according to its business activities.

3. What we are doing
I would like to stress that we take the concerns raised in FinCEN’s order seriously. We intend to engage constructively with FinCEN and have begun an independent review of our AML and sanctions controls.

We remain focused on resolving this situation and will continue to share updates as things develop.

Thank you to everyone who has continued to stand with us. And to those who have chosen to withdraw, we respect your decision and will do our best to ensure a smooth process.

text:
This is too strong of an interpretation, for a couple reasons. First, Aaronson-Ambainis compares quantum vs classical algorithms when they have access to an idealized, perfectly unstructured black box oracle. All cryptographic hash functions are not black box and definitely not unstructured (because their source code is succinct and public). We should be very wary about transferring conclusions about random oracles to concrete hash functions. 

Second, Aaronson-Ambainis is about decision problems concerning the black box oracle. We now know there is no exponential quantum advantage for decision problems on unstructured oracles. On the other hand, search problems are a completely different story. We know there can be exponential quantum advantage for solving search problems related to unstructured oracles; this is the famous Yamakawa-Zhandry result from 2022.

This second item is particularly relevant to breaking hash functions, where you want to do things like "Find me a preimage -- any preimage -- of this hash value".

Summary of Blockchain Security - Nov 2026. 

The reason blockchain was architected as the layer of trust is the off chain private key. 

Thats the only bulletproof defense we have against large language models and Moores Law. 

If you break that design and commingle, centralize, custody, put private keys online, share keys, the architecture breaks. 

Blockchains will continue to increase the depth of the private key to always push the brute force attack probability way into the future if ever. 

When private keys are held online, we get the “hacks” and FUD waves. 

Custodial solutions need complex key management like MCP to be safe online from AI penetration and must have multi party signatures and multiple safeguards for large transactions requiring further depth of signature verification. 

Most attacks are however mostly social engineered attacks, these will always be a problem. Humans can be extorted and manipulated into providing their keys. Hence multi layer multi party rotating signatures are vital for large value. Coinbase do a terrific job at this btw 👏

But the blockchains have never been broken, never been hacked, summary, there are only two attack vectors that penetrate: 

- key theft
- Ethereum EIP-7702 Externally Owned Accounts and reentrancy bugs. 

Im not a candy coater. Im a scientist. This is the state of the domain. 

Any violation of off chain keys is a vulnerability not to be taken lightly. I have urged all custodians to move away from
EIP-7702 and reentrancy for years. I urge them again, move to MPC asap and stop using Externally Owned Accounts.

text:
🇬🇧 The UK is planning for a "Black Sky" blackout affecting nearly 70 MILLION people.

A Black Sky is when the power goes out for days and takes water, shops and communications with it.

A recent UK resilience summit focused on withstanding one for at least 72 hours, per the BBC.

When floods cut power to 61,500 people in Lancaster in 2015, all of these failed:

1. Lights and heating
2. Some water supplies, which relied on electric pumps
3. The railway station
4. Petrol stations and shops
5. Traffic lights
6. Most cash machines

Which communication systems kept working? Only copper landlines and FM radio.

The issue climbed the agenda after the April 2025 blackout across Spain, Portugal and southwestern France.

The UK's backup plans include:

• About 100 BBC staff ready to run an emergency studio with fuel, food and water for at least three days.

• Emergency broadcast scripts already online, including how to dispose of toilet waste without flushing.

• £70 MILLION of government spending to develop high-altitude aircraft for at least a week of emergency phone and internet.

And on January 31, 2027, the UK switches off its copper landlines.

The government says there is no specific threat to the grid, which has never had a complete outage in 75 years.

Cash, cards or crypto: what would you rely on if the power went out for three days?

It's urgent that prediction markets diversify their revenue if they want to survive the coming regulations. 

Here are 2 direction that I think are promising.

Parametric insurance:

We already saw AirBnB propose weather predictions to it's user as a form of "bad weather insurance".

It could be extended to let farmers hedge droughts, airlines hedge weather disruptions or passenger hedge against cancelled flights.

Global insurance premiums is around ~$8T annually. Prediction markets could easily pull $500B+ in annual volume from these.

ETFs / Event indices:

The S&P 500 alone has $20T in assets tracking or benchmarked to it. Global ETFs manage $24T.

We could create similar indices for real-world events like a "US Recession Index" or "AI Boom Index", combining dozen of events into a single tradable index.

If they reach even 5% of the size of stock market indices, it would still amount to $1T.

Prediction markets must not limit themselves to being glorified Sportsbooks. 

We have to think bigger than that.

text:
I am the Amazon product manager who named the Prime cancellation flow after a 10-year war.

Iliad. That was the code name. The Federal Trade Commission later explained it to the court better than I ever explained it to my skip-level: “Fittingly, Amazon named that process ‘Iliad,’ which refers to Homer’s epic about the long, arduous Trojan War.”

Fittingly. A federal agency used the word “fittingly” about my work. I have it on a mug.

Nobody in the review had read the Iliad. That is how it got approved. If 1 person in that room had read it, they would have known it doesn’t even end with the war won. It ends with a funeral. We shipped it anyway. That’s Day 1 thinking.

I work in South Lake Union, in Seattle, where it rains 150 days a year and nobody owns an umbrella because umbrellas are for tourists and Microsoft. We have a banana stand that gives away free bananas to anyone who walks by. It is the only thing in the company you can get without a subscription. Every morning I take 1, walk past the Spheres, sit down, and think about how to keep you.

Let me tell you how it actually works, because you imagine an evil genius, and it is, I promise you, a 6-page memo and a very strong opinion about button placement. At Amazon you pitch a product by writing the press release before you build it, with an FAQ underneath. Mine had a question near the bottom: “Why would a customer want to leave?” The answer field said, “Out of scope.” Nobody flagged it. We read the memo in silence for 20 minutes at the start of the meeting, like a book club that is afraid of the author, and then we argue about the font.

Getting in had to be easy. That was the Trojan Horse, which, I have since learned, is not in the Iliad. It’s in the Odyssey, and in Virgil. We had the wrong book. We had the right horse. A big yellow button at checkout: “Get FREE Two-Day Shipping.” Free. A gift, wheeled right up to your city gates. You clicked it. You were in Prime. Our own internal report said customers “did not understand the impact of their choice.” In August 2017, 17,131 of the 25,542 cancellation requests our team handled were “accidental sign-ups.” That’s 67%. That’s a better conversion rate than most intentional products.

Someone proposed a clearer button. It tested beautifully. It would also have cost us “260,000 annualized paid Prime members.” A draft memo declined to clarify things “because it would cause a ‘shock’ to business performance.” We do not shock the business. We shock the customer, gently, monthly, at $14.99.

Our leader at the time had a theory about why people were confused. “Shoppers in countries that are new to online shopping may not know that a yellow button means they’re buying Prime, like we do.” Like we do. The whole company spoke Yellow. The customers were simply illiterate.

For years the decline button said, “No Thanks, I don’t want FREE Two-Day Shipping.” You had to say it. Out loud, in your head, with your mouse. An internal email warned us about “a well established external trend (negatively perceived) called ‘customer shaming,’” and noted we were “specifically called out.” So we changed it to “No thanks.” We are capable of growth.

Getting out was my department.

The FTC gave my work a title, in a federal complaint, in bold: “Prime’s Four-Page, Six-Click, Fifteen-Option Iliad Cancellation Process.” I have never received a better performance review. On mobile it was “an eight-page, eight-click minimum process.” Odysseus needed 10 years to get home. We only asked for 8 pages. We were, by Homeric standards, generous.

First you had to find the door. If you typed “cancel membership” into the Amazon search bar, it did not cancel your membership. It took you to the Iliad. Achilles had a heel. We had a search bar that led straight back into the war.

Page 1 was my favorite. Before you could leave, we made you “[t]ake a look back at [your] journey with Prime.” A little memorial. A scrapbook. And then, in the FTC’s own exhibit, the scrapbook of a real customer:

“0 Packages shipped for free with Prime Delivery. Start shopping today’s deals!”

“0 Movies and TV shows watched with Prime Video. You can start watching videos by clicking here!”

“0 Songs listened to with Amazon Music Prime. Start listening now!”

0, 0 and 0, with an exclamation point after each. That is the most honest page Amazon has ever published. It is a customer who received nothing, being invited to receive more of it.

At the bottom, 3 buttons. “Remind Me Later.” “Keep My Benefits.” And “Continue to Cancel,” which, I want to be precise, did not cancel. It continued. Continuing is not the same as cancelling. Ask anyone who has ever been in a meeting at Amazon.

Page 2, same 3 buttons, slightly different words, so you’d wonder if you were losing your mind. You were. That was a metric.

Page 3, 5 options. “Remind Me Later.” “Keep My Membership.” “Pause,” which stopped your billing and kept a “quick-resume” button 1 click away, the way a casino keeps your coat. “End on [date],” which turned off renewal and refunded nothing. And finally, last, at the bottom, under a warning icon telling you that “By cancelling, you will no longer be eligible for your unclaimed Prime exclusive offers,” the only button in the entire epic that actually ended it: “End Now.”

By the time you reached it, you had seen “Remind Me Later” 4 times. Penelope kept her suitors waiting for years by weaving a burial shroud all day and unraveling it every night. “Remind Me Later” is Penelope’s loom. You think you are making progress. Every night, we undo it.

And the refund, if you made it, was limited to 1 monthly charge. We didn’t mention that on the way in. You don’t tell Odysseus how many islands are left.

It worked. After Iliad launched, cancellations dropped 14% at 1 point in 2017. The internal document is a masterpiece of Seattle understatement: “Although this data is directional, retention appears to be trending positively.” Retention. That’s what we call it when a man stands at the gates of his own house for 4 pages and can’t get in.

People inside objected. Of course they did. This is a company of very smart, very tired people. 1 employee wrote to leadership, “We congratulate when someone changes a headline color, or the style of a table, but don’t notice we are not even telling customers what they are signing up for.” A colleague told Business Insider, “We have been deliberately confusing. It’s very un-Amazonian in terms of customer obsession.”

Customer Obsession is our first Leadership Principle. Everyone forgets it’s a principle about obsession. Obsession doesn’t let go. Obsession doesn’t take “End Now” for an answer. Obsession sends a reminder 3 days before your renewal. Some called the Iliad a failure of Customer Obsession. I’d call it the purest form.

Our founder put it best in his 2016 shareholder letter: “you’d be irresponsible not to be a member.” I printed that and taped it above my monitor. Irresponsible. Trapping is such an ugly word. We were protecting you from your own irresponsibility, 4 pages at a time.

The Greeks finally got into Troy with a gift. The government finally got into Amazon with a subpoena. In September 2025 we settled for $2.5 billion: a $1 billion penalty and $1.5 billion in refunds. Our spokesperson said there was “no admission of guilt in this settlement by the company or any executives.” So for the record, nobody did it. The flow designed itself. The buttons arranged themselves into a war.

Here is the detail I treasure. To pay the refunds, someone had to build a flow. A refund flow. For millions of people. And I can tell you, as a professional, that it is very hard to resist adding a page.

Last month my own badge stopped working. Reorg. I sat in a conference room named after a Leadership Principle while HR walked me through my offboarding on a laptop. Page 1 said, “Take a look back at your journey with Amazon.” Page 2 had a button that said “Continue.” It did not continue. Page 3 offered to remind me later.

I clicked “End Now.”

It was always the last button. It was always there. It was just at the bottom, under a warning, where we put the things we hope you’ll never reach.

It’s raining in South Lake Union. I took 1 more banana on the way out. It was free. I checked.

text:
Learned that a notable incumbent stopped using product roadmap docs, b/c employees treated every item as a commitment and every change as a failure. As AI accelerated experiments and sped up change, the roadmap meant to give people clarity was creating anxiety. Now the company sets a high-level strategy and tasks small teams to build with AI in short loops to realize it. The cross-team builds are the roadmap.

More like a river to navigate than a road to follow. Harder to steer, but less risk of racing to the wrong destination.

That pace is familiar to startups, but amplified greatly by AI. Now it's also common among savvy incumbents, who are innovating even faster than many startups. But the speed, decision reversals, and dramatic changes to processes and to the tasks within a job can leave people feeling isolated and questioning meaning in their craft.

It's never been tougher for people who want a narrow goal to run toward without having their goalposts moved.

There's also never been a better opportunity for those with curiosity and skills spanning multiple disciplines who can leverage AI effectively. As the goalposts move and elevate, AI gives these people more power and authority than ever to land winning shots. These are the people I'm looking for to help build @catena_labs.

text:
Publicly funded science should work more like open source software.

Today a result is a PDF. The data often isn't shared, the code isn't public, and few studies ever get replicated.

Imagine every experiment as a repo. Data, code, and protocol, all versioned. Anyone could fork it, rerun it, and send a fix. Funders could reward replications as much as new papers.

AI makes this urgent. Agents are now making more discoveries than ever. The bottleneck becomes replication/validation. Then commercialization, which still requires moving atoms in the real world and meetings with regulators.

author: eng_khairallah1

text:
Here it is. Paste it into your AGENTS.md:

# No Orphan Agents

Every agent you start has a job, a limit and an end. When the job ends, the agent ends.

## Before you spawn
- Do it yourself if one pass can finish it. A quick fix, a rename or a single-file edit never needs an agent.
- Spawn only when the work has parts that are truly independent and can run at the same time.
- Never spawn an agent to wait on another agent. If it has to wait, it's not parallel work.
- Write an entry for each agent before it starts:
  - Job: the one thing it's there to do
  - Done when: the exact result that ends it
  - Limit: the most time or turns it gets before it stops on its own
  - Returns: what it hands back to you
- No entry, no agent.

## Giving each agent its job
- One agent, one job. If you can't describe its job in one sentence, split it or don't send it.
- Pass the files and facts the job needs. Don't make it re-read what the main session already knows.
- Tell it what it must not touch, not only what it should do.
- Give it a clear stopping point. "Find the bug" is open-ended. "Find the line that throws this error and report it" ends.
- Never hand an agent the power to spawn agents of its own.

## While agents run
- Keep a live list in a file: every agent, its job, when it started, its limit and its status.
- Update the list the moment an agent starts, checks in, finishes or gets stopped.
- Background agents check in at set points, not only at the end.
- Anything silent past its limit gets checked, then stopped.
- Two agents never edit the same file at the same time.
- If the plan changes, stop every agent working on the old plan before you brief them on the new one.

## Cost and context
- Search, log and test agents run on a cheaper model. The top model is for real reasoning and real edits.
- Never let an agent silently inherit the main model. Set its model on purpose.
- An agent returns a result, not a conversation. A summary, a diff, a list of lines, nothing more.
- Fewer agents beat more. Add one only when it does work the others can't.
- If an agent's job turns out bigger than its limit, it stops and reports. It doesn't quietly keep going.

## Closing the loop
- The moment an agent returns its result, stop it. Never leave one idle just in case.
- Check every result yourself. An agent saying done is a claim, not proof.
- Before you tell me a task is done, check the list. Every agent from this task is stopped or accounted for.
- Clear finished agents off the list.
- Nothing from this task keeps running after you say done.

## Pause and confirm
Reading and checking status is always fine. Unless the task already cleared it, get my OK before you:
- Start an agent with no time limit
- Leave an agent running after this session ends
- Spawn more than three agents at once
- Schedule anything that runs overnight or on a timer
- Restart an agent that already hit its limit
- Give any agent access to push, deploy or touch production

## Reporting back
- Tell me how many agents ran, what each one did and how long each took.
- Tell me what each one cost, if you can see it.
- List anything an agent left unfinished, and why.
- Flag any agent that hit its limit or had to be stopped.

## If one goes quiet
- An agent that misses a check-in or passes its limit gets stopped, not waited on.
- Tell me what it was doing, what it finished and what it left behind.
- Never restart it on your own. Nothing runs where I can't see it.

text:
Publicly funded science should work more like open source software.

Today a result is a PDF. The data often isn't shared, the code isn't public, and few studies ever get replicated.

Imagine every experiment as a repo. Data, code, and protocol, all versioned. Anyone could fork it, rerun it, and send a fix. Funders could reward replications as much as new papers.

AI makes this urgent. Agents are now making more discoveries than ever. The bottleneck becomes replication/validation. Then commercialization, which still requires moving atoms in the real world and meetings with regulators.

让资产托管与交易服务各自发挥优势，让用户拥有更多选择，也让专业金融机构的安全保障与交易所的流动性更好地协同，为行业带来更开放、更灵活的金融服务模式。

天呐，海底光缆统治世界的时代要结束了，又要见证历史了🤯。。
马斯克首次公布 Starlink V4 的极端参数：性能直接跳涨一百倍，光速天然快了一点四倍且不用绕大陆架，上千万条激光链路正在把地球通信主干搬上深空。

绝大多数人至今依然以为，星链只是给偏远山区、游艇和飞机提供网络补丁的边缘工具。
直到马斯克刚刚在最新的投资人会议上摊开底牌，很多人才第一次看懂 SpaceX 真正的阳谋：把构筑人类现代文明的海底光缆网络，从大洋深处连根拔起，彻底搬到太空。
这里藏着一个极度反直觉的物理常识： 光在太空真空中的传播速度，比在玻璃光纤里整整快了 40%。
 更致命的是几何路径的差异。海底光缆必须顺着大陆架和海沟蜿蜒曲折地绕远路，而太空中的卫星激光链路，两点之间永远是沿着大圆航线在真空中直线对穿。这意味着在跨洋超长距离通信上，太空激光的延迟天然比地面光缆更低。
而阻碍这件事过去的唯一瓶颈，是带宽密度。
马斯克这次直接给出了技术迭代的量化终局： 从 V2 到即将落地的 V4 卫星，单星吞吐能力将直接迎来 100 倍的暴力跃升。 在更长期的宏大蓝图里，超过 10 万颗卫星组成的轨道阵列，每颗都将配备大约 100 个传输速率超 10 Tbps 的光学激光器，在地球外围织成一张百 Exabit 级别的无缝高速网状路由。
这已经不是在做卫星宽带了，这是在用火箭把全球互联网的核心骨干网整个重写一遍。
海底光缆容易被地质地震震断、被船锚挂伤，更深陷地缘博弈的物理封锁；而悬在头顶的真空激光网络，既没有折射损耗，也没有无法逾越的地理边界。
人类用了上百年时间，把铜线和光纤一根根沉入海底来连接彼此；而未来的文明动脉，注定要在没有阻力的星空里以光速奔流。 https://t.co/4aiz8w4cJg

text:
Chamath says SpaceX’s compute deal with Anthropic has a mutual 90-day out, and Elon Musk ending it would be “the king-making move”

“You and I talked about this before on the pod, but SpaceX and Anthropic’s compute deal has a mutual 90-day out. Anthropic can terminate in 90 days, SpaceX can terminate in 90 days."

"If SpaceX says, I’m going to terminate this compute in 90 days, that is the king-making move. Why? It’s a disproportionate amount of the compute that Anthropic needs."

"It allows SpaceX to reprice that compute at the spot rate, which is probably double the market rate, right? And the market rate, and it’s probably not just double, it could probably triple."

"So whatever revenue you see on SpaceX’s balance sheet from Anthropic could 2 to 3x. And Anthropic would have no choice except to immediately capitulate and take the higher price. It would also show all of the other hyperscalers that they are very far away from having economic yield that is optimized."

"And so then it forces them to consider: should I be giving it to myself? Should I be selling it to the other people? It then forces the neoclouds to take all of this money that they’ve raised, whether it’s debt or equity, and say, I have two choices, which is to buy as much compute today as I can at whatever price it’s available, because the other path is assured destruction and bankruptcy for me, because I’m just out of the game..."

"So I think all the game theory, Jason, literally comes down to this one deal and whether Elon decides to rip it, because if he rips it, watch out.”

quoted_text:
David Friedberg says every dollar Nvidia spends making chips turns into $18 of Anthropic revenue, with SpaceX making an 83% margin in between

“I basically said start with NVIDIA, how much does NVIDIA spend to make the chips? And then how much do they sell the chips for? So for every dollar of COGS, every dollar that NVIDIA spends, that turns into $4 of revenue for NVIDIA, 75% margin."

"And then that gets sold to SpaceX, and then SpaceX turns around, and they’re making, you know, an 83% margin on that chip spend, because they’re kind of looking at a five-year depreciation. So they spent $10 billion on Colossus one, five year life, $2 billion a year depreciation. And so that’s kind of the cost per year, but then they’re making $1.25 billion a month on Colossus."

"And then Anthropic is showing in this S-1 pretty remarkably to Sacks’s point that they’re making about 85% incremental gross margin on every incremental dollar coming in. It’s obviously a baseline of compute spend, but 85% is kind of the incremental gross margin. So at the end of the day, a dollar that NVIDIA spends turns into $18 that Anthropic is making selling to customers.”

text:
In this picture I am sitting with one of the great scholars of Somalia, Shaykh Abdulkarim Hassan Hoosh.
The Shaykh is deeply rooted in knowledge. Over the years he has taught many of the Islamic sciences. His speciality is usul al-fiqh, and he is also firmly grounded in tafsir and much more. But that is not why I am sharing this.
It was the last ten nights of Ramadan in Makkah. We had just prayed Taraweeh and Tahajjud in the Haram, and on our way back we sat down together on these steps. The Shaykh has never filmed himself and has never allowed his face to be photographed. To the crowds passing by, he was simply an elderly man resting after prayer.
While we sat there, a group of people came up to me with questions. They wanted rulings on various matters. Beside me sat a giant of knowledge, and not one of them turned to him. They did not know who he was. To them he was anonymous.
I was struck by it. SubhanAllah, we live in a time when fame and popularity have become the measure of whom we ask and whom we consult. Those brothers cannot be blamed for not recognising him. But the moment showed me something: a man can carry an ocean of knowledge and pass unnoticed, while others are sought out because they are seen. Yet in sha' Allah, he is known to Allah for the good he has done for this Ummah, and that is the recognition that truly matters.
My brothers and sisters, too often we decide whom to respect and from whom to take knowledge by how well known they are, rather than by what they carry. Let us not build our religion on who is famous, who is popular, or whose name everyone recognises, while the true people of knowledge sit among us unseen.
As Imam Muhammad ibn Sirin said: "This knowledge is religion, so look carefully at whom you take your religion from."
Knowledge is not fame. Popularity is not scholarship.
May Allah preserve Shaykh Abdulkarim and all the hidden scholars of this Ummah, and grant us the wisdom to recognise and honour them.

text:
This is too strong of an interpretation, for a couple reasons. First, Aaronson-Ambainis compares quantum vs classical algorithms when they have access to an idealized, perfectly unstructured black box oracle. All cryptographic hash functions are not black box and definitely not unstructured (because their source code is succinct and public). We should be very wary about transferring conclusions about random oracles to concrete hash functions. 

Second, Aaronson-Ambainis is about decision problems concerning the black box oracle. We now know there is no exponential quantum advantage for decision problems on unstructured oracles. On the other hand, search problems are a completely different story. We know there can be exponential quantum advantage for solving search problems related to unstructured oracles; this is the famous Yamakawa-Zhandry result from 2022.

This second item is particularly relevant to breaking hash functions, where you want to do things like "Find me a preimage -- any preimage -- of this hash value".

author: ripe0x
quoted_text:
apeball

a coin that buys bored apes with its trading fees

an onchain game where anyone can purchase randomized nfts from a pool containing those apes

i've been watching token strategies since they launched and it's been v interesting to see how speculation is used to fund the accumulation of assets

but once assets are acquired, many of those strategies stall out because they require demand for the target collection to rise and buy the nfts that were listed at a markup

i've been curious about what happens if you keep the asset accumulation mechanism but give those assets a different way to circulate

enter: FWA custom pools

with apeball, trading fees fund a live eth bid for bored apes, and every acquired ape goes into the pool

rather than waiting for someone to purchase an entire ape at a markup, the pool distributes nfts through much smaller randomized purchases

the rest of the pool is filled with shapes (eth-backed nfts), which are minted on demand at different denominations, giving people a range of possible outcomes and keeping the draw price around 0.02 eth

as people play apeball, each ape's notional listing value gradually decays, increasing the odds that they get drawn

the pool generates revenue from each draw and all pool profits go toward accumulating APEBALL for buy and burns and additional ape acquisitions when needed

the buyback portion accumulates in a reserve until someone pulls an ape, at which point it's released to buy and burn the coin

so trading activity acquires the apes, the game provides a way to distribute them through smaller purchases, and the revenue from that activity feeds back into the coin

some details on the coin:

- 1 billion fixed supply
- no team allocation, presale, or emissions
- normal trading fees are 5% on buys and sells
- launch fee starts at 69% in both directions and decrease by 1 percentage point per minute until reaching 5%
- 99% of trading fees go to the ape pool, 1% goes to buy and burn LAYER

i earn from the mint fees on shapes, while the trading fees and game revenue remain in the protocol to fund acquisitions and buybacks

feels like we're just scratching the surface of how these different onchain mechanisms can work together, and i'm excited to see how this one plays out

deploying soon

⚠️ALERT: Crypto wallets created with Google or Apple logins are being hit by unauthorized transactions.

Keplr, the main wallet of the Cosmos ecosystem, paused both login options after users reported the thefts.

The incident originated at Web3Auth, the login service owned by MetaMask's parent Consensys, which says it has gone into "maintenance mode due to a security incident."

Web3Auth claimed nearly 50 MILLION users across more than 8,200 apps when Consensys bought it last year, per The Block.

Keplr's co-founder estimates about 20% of its Google and Apple login accounts are affected, but says only "a fraction" of those has been exploited and the rest "may be recoverable."

Wallets created with a recovery phrase or hardware wallet are NOT affected, and Web3Auth says there is no evidence MetaMask users are impacted.

text:
I was asked a few times this past week why I bought a super expensive machine for local inference. Why not rent?

One side of the answer is that I want to automate some things for Dark Bio, like accounting and invoicing. I refuse to send customer data to 3rd party providers. So that's a practical necessity I can more easily rationalize.

The other side, however, is a hedge against LLM regulations. Restricting access to model weights themselves is impossible; software piracy existed forever and one more law against file sharing won't make a dent in curbing that. That said, restricting access to hardware is a *very* effective way to regulate things. These machines are not cheap things that fly under the radar; they trigger red flags across all payment and shipping flows, so one single law passed and all flows stop instantaneously. And already today, you need to fill out forms to be allowed to buy a DGX Spark.

My concern is that with LLMs advancing and various hacks happening, some regulator will make the unfortunate knee-jerk reaction to block hardware sales. And even if it takes weeks or months to pass, it might be too late to obtain the required local inference capability with the current 3-4 month entry queues.

Is this paranoia? Probably. Is this a waste of money? Possibly. But potentially having access cut off to both hosted frontier models and local inference overnight is a pretty nasty setback with no meaningful way to paddle out of.

This is utterly ridiculous—and immediate proof of the exact risk @BillAckman has been warning about: turning $FNMA and $FMCC into a politicized slush fund.

​Beyond being pure socialism, this proposal shows a fundamental ignorance of how the conservatorship actually works. Every dollar of net income F2 generates builds their capital levels, and adds a dollar to Treasury’s liquidation preference.

​If the "commies" get control of these companies and start raiding retained earnings for political giveaways, there are two principal impacts:

​1. Wild volatility in mortgage spreads. Hollowing out F2’s fortress balance sheet drives up borrowing costs—actively hurting the exact homebuyers this is supposed to help.

​2. Perpetual conservatorship. Stripping away retained earnings destroys their ability to build statutory capital buffers, driving the odds of ever exiting conservatorship to zero.

​Once you normalize confiscating private company profits to fund pet political priorities, the precedent is set. Today it's down payment handouts, tomorrow it's whatever social program is next on the list (ACA all over again). If Washington is serious about affordability, start by cutting rampant government spending and bloated deficits instead of looting F2.

Often you don’t know how much work goes into something until you do it yourself. Over the years at Delphi, we’ve done a lot - Research, Consulting, Incubating, Investing, Media. All I’ve learned is that everything is hard and takes real effort. So you really have to be excited and passionate about what you choose to do, and when you commit: go all in.

As for @Delphi_Digital, we’re doubling down on Research. It’s been a core part of our DNA since the very beginning, and we feel it will only be more important as a signal in an accelerating world with more and more noise. Excited to share more about this in a few weeks.

昨天在X上看到一条挺有意思的帖子，已经有超过52万次浏览了。

 @alex_verem  恳求大家，这个周末一定要花20分钟，在自己的电脑里下载一个开源AI模型。

比如Qwen或Gemma，找一个几GB到十几GB的量化版本，用免费的本地工具运行起来。

他的理由很简单：

你今天每个月付费订阅的AI，明天可能突然涨价、限制使用额度，甚至直接封禁你的账号（比如在大陆的人）。

但如果你把模型下载到了自己的硬盘里，只要设备还能运行它，2036年你依然可以使用今天的这个模型。
无需账号，无需订阅，甚至无需联网。

我其实特别认同这个建议。
虽然目前本地小模型的能力，和云端最顶级的模型还有明显差距，但AI正在逐渐成为我们日常生活和工作中不可缺少的基础设施。
当所有的能力都依赖少数几家公司的云端服务时，我们其实对自己的AI没有多少控制权。
尤其是当你越来越习惯把自己的私人信息、工作资料，甚至一些不愿意告诉别人的想法交给AI时，本地模型的意义就更大了。

我觉得每个人都应该在自己的电脑里保存一份AI。

哪怕暂时用不上，至少你知道，无论未来这些AI公司怎么调整政策、怎么收费，你的硬盘里始终有一个可以使用的模型。

text:
gossip (read) priority fees on hyperliquid are broken

currently the team that is benefitting the most is wintermute (insert fist shaking red emoji guy meme)

this is not publicly known but can be determined with certainty by mapping out transfers to labeled wallets from the top winner of the gossip priority fee auctions (they have won 79% of the slot 0 auctions in the past 24h)

tldr; wahhh wahhhh wahhh hl gossip priority, not fair. add more slots or scrap the gossip auction

my proposed solution:

1) increase gossip priority to 20 equal-priority slots
2) make it so winning an auction slot grants IP whitelisting to a foundation-run peering slot

i think this basically solves it and would likely *increase* total gossip priority fees

---

some context

the purported intention, as stated in the docs, is to "reduce the need for market makers to hyper-optimize their infrastructure to remain competitive"

if you win the gossip auction slot, you get order book / node data 50ms (!!) faster than anyone else. 

yes. one IP, across the *entire network*, gets the feeds 50ms faster. it's the whole ballgame

so in theory you could just buy the faster data slot instead of spending 10s of thousands monthly on high octane ec2 instances and [insert hft magic] 

or you can do BOTH, which is what wintermute is doing

so despite the stated intentions it does the exact opposite and gives 1 wallet a dominant advantage over every other participant

further reducing the democratization of this mechanism is the fact that, practically speaking, you can only use a won gossip slot if you have a direct peering relationship with the foundation node. 

multiple providers we work with couldn’t pass gossip priority benefits through to us without slowing their other peers (all independently confirmed this behavior - strange design)

and to get a foundation peering you to do 0.5% of the 14d HL maker volume (we don't quite meet this threshold so our application was rejected) as well as stake 10,000 HYPE ($780,000 here), or be like, a node service provider

---

without revealing too much i can say with 100% certainty that wintermute has maxed out BOTH the infrastructure optimization + expenditure AND is monopolizing the gossip fee auction

they're spending on average $26,000 *per day* ($10M/yr) to win this auction

so rn they're just eating everyone else's lunch

and the only way that approach is economic is if you are MM at the scale that they are, which only a handful of wallets are doing

text:
Made a short animation for $PENDLE vs ETH to show how closely alts correlate with ETH price action.

Lower cap alts tend to outperform ETH in bullish periods. But, if you buy the top, the drawdown will be a lot more aggressive too.

PENDLE had a +73.9% peak and ETH had a +22.3% peak when measure from February (I picked beginning of Feb because that's when prices started to bottom out).

Correlation = 0.64. This means prices tended to move in the same direction on most days.

There's a lot of reasons behind this phenomenon:

> A ton of alts are paired with ETH on-chain. This means if ETH 2x, alt/USD price will 2x too without any buy pressure. Inverse is true as well.
> ETH and other majors moving gives people confidence to ape alts.
> Majors pumping means a lot of potential perps profit that will be rotated to on-chain plays if on-chain is still cheap.
> Spot holders also take profit and use a portion of it to ape alts.
> Low cap alts tend to pull a higher multiple because liquidity is often much thinner and it takes very little money to pump the chart compared to majors.

TLDR: Most alts are highly correlated with ETH and majors price action. They tend to dump aggressively when majors are weak, but they also pull higher multiples when the market is strong.

text:
When I do AI supply and demand modeling, everything ex-SPCX generally fits together and makes sense and is reasonably well funded. No individual large build looks too excessive because, for the most part, large projects are pre sold before they are built, or at least before they are completed… Anthropic can fund its ambitions for the next few years pretty easily with ARR and cash on hand. Even OpenAI is sitting on a mountain of cash and can fund the majority of compute with ARR. The hyperscale clouds are allocating between internal, lab, and enterprise use cases. 

This changed w/ $SPCX who is trying to build ~40% of 2026 capacity next year but without a secured buyer. Just a massive bet that industry capacity plans will undershoot realized demand by a wide margin. 

This is the most obvious way this becomes a glut. And everything else will mostly be contracted, with spcx holding most of the bag. 

They also have BY FAR the most financial upside if conditions remain tight, because of their chosen path to live and die by the spot market. 

But I find it puzzling that markets have really not challenged them more, particularly as broadly the risk of a cyclical peak comes into focus. When parties as risk seeking as OpenAI @sama have called them speculative (one of only 2-3 potential buyers of SPCX capacity…). Also SPCX two existing customers are abundantly clear that they view their contracts as short-term / bridge capacity and intend to churn off as new cheaper capacity comes online at ~1/5 of the price.

DraftKings is already anticipating sports contract being banned.

I found a slide in their Q3 reports describing this exact scenario.

They are projecting the effect of a Sports ban in July 2028 on their prediction market profits.

The loss would be immense:
- profit per customer down 80%
- 41 month to recoup 2027 customer acquisition cost instead of 18 with sports.

The second point is interesting because they are measuring 2027 customer, that would be 90% paid off when the predicted ban drops.

Prediction Markets need to diversify urgently.

author: AgentBotega
quoted_text:
Politics still made only 1.5% of Kalshi's volume during Midterms month vs 85.2% for sports.

Same picture for Polymarket US: 
- 3.6% politics 
- 95.4% sports

Prediction markets have become insanely reliant on sports betting and now they could lose access to it.

Kalshi & Polymarket have already been banned from offering sports contracts in 5 US states (Nevada, Michigan, Washington, Massachusetts and Minnesota)

Now they are looking at a Supreme Court case vs a 39 states alliance that could make sports contracts subject to states gambling laws *nationwide*.

It's urgent that prediction markets diversify their revenue if they want to survive the coming regulations. 

Here are 2 direction that I think are promising.

Parametric insurance:

We already saw AirBnB propose weather predictions to it's user as a form of "bad weather insurance".

It could be extended to let farmers hedge droughts, airlines hedge weather disruptions or passenger hedge against cancelled flights.

Global insurance premiums is around ~$8T annually. Prediction markets could easily pull $500B+ in annual volume from these.

ETFs / Event indices:

The S&P 500 alone has $20T in assets tracking or benchmarked to it. Global ETFs manage $24T.

We could create similar indices for real-world events like a "US Recession Index" or "AI Boom Index", combining dozen of events into a single tradable index.

If they reach even 5% of the size of stock market indices, it would still amount to $1T.

Prediction markets must not limit themselves to being glorified Sportsbooks. 

We have to think bigger than that.

This is very much the wrong perspective.

And if you actually take the time to figure out your definitions, what you're worried about, what you want to control for, and what would effectively control it, congratulations -- you don't need a moratorium because you've actually done the work to craft the policy you thought you needed a moratorium to craft, and can just pass that.

text:
搞AI=坐牢20年？美国为什么要死里整自家巨头？中国要反超？

会坐牢的是这样一种叠加情形——你被认定在研发"人工超级智能"，且是在联邦新监管机构挂牌之后仍然继续，且被判定系统具备"削弱人类主导权"的能力。三道门全部关死，才轮得到"最高20年"这个数字出场。

而承载这一切的两份法案，此刻还躺在国会的提案箱里。

一、一份还没进委员会的议案，先把市场吓崩了

2026年9月23日，参议员伯尼·桑德斯提出S.5493；次日，众议员格雷格·卡萨尔跟进H.R.10538。两份文本同名：《禁止人工超级智能法案》（ASI Prohibition Act of 2026）。截至11月初，两者状态都是"Introduced"——已提出，未进委员会审议，未表决。

真正让市场震动的不是文本状态，而是文本内容。它做了三件在美国立法史上都算罕见的事。

第一，它把"暂停"写成了默认状态。在联邦设立一个内阁级别的AI监管机构、并建立完整的模型审查机制之前，所有先进AI的开发、训练、部署、转移、资助行为一律暂停。一旦系统被判定带有"超级智能前兆特征"，开发者必须在限期内隔离联网并关停；无法消除风险的，强制停用。

第二，它给"越线"配了核武器级的罚则。违规企业面临所谓"企业死刑"——许可撤销、资产与相关知识产权移交联邦政府、主体强制解散；决策层与独立违规个人最高20年联邦监禁，量刑对标非法研发核武器；普通非决策岗位员工，最长10年禁止在AI行业从业。

第三，它把管辖范围写到了境外。"全球禁止超级智能"被列为美国外交政策目标，配套国际协定与出口管制，目标是阻断任何地区研发同类系统的可能。

然后是最要命的一条：它没有给出可操作的技术定义。

法案把ASI分成两类：一是在广泛领域与任务中达到或超越人类认知表现的系统，或"可轻易被修改"以展现该能力的系统；二是具备策划并执行削弱人类主导权、甚至推翻或破坏美国政府体系能力的系统。

"广泛领域""轻易被修改""削弱人类主导权"——这三个短语，任何一个都能装下今天所有的主流大模型，也都可以一个都不装。定义权不在工程师手里，在执法者的裁量里。

二、三个偷换，让"20年"传遍全网

传播链条上发生了三次偷换，每一次都让标题更响一点。

**把"提案"换成"法律"。** 它现在是纸，不是法。本届国会剩余时间有限，能否在下一届重新提交并加速，取决于中期选举后的议程排序，不取决于社交平台的转发量。

**把"最高刑"换成"标准刑"。** 法律文本里的"最高20年"，与现实中的量刑之间隔着认罪协商、证据标准和主观故意认定。美国司法部一年处理数十万件联邦案件，真正落到顶格量刑的，是极少数。

**把"超级智能"缩写成"AI"。** 这是最容易被忽略、也最要命的一次缩写。法案禁的不是"AI"，是一个连提出者都难以清晰界定的上位概念。当禁区边界无法用技术语言描述，它的实际效果不是"管住最危险的"，而是"让所有做AI的人都不敢确定自己是否安全"。

> 一个说不清边界的禁令，惩罚的不是越界者，是所有人的预期。

三、美国为什么要"死里整"自家巨头

这个问法本身错了一半。美国不是在"整巨头"，是三股力量在同一时间撞上了AI。

第一股：选票

2026年11月3日的地方投票中，全美44项涉及暂停数据中心建设的措施，43项获得通过。NBC选后民调显示，76%的受访者反对在自己所在社区建设数据中心。理由极其具体：电费、水、噪音、道路负担。这不是意识形态，是账单。

几乎同一周，民主党夺回参众两院。亚利桑那州众议员亚萨明·安萨里在结果出炉不到24小时后公开表态，要求把"暂停先进AI发展"放到新议程首位，并落实《禁止人工超级智能法案》——她本人是该法案的联署人之一。马斯克回了一句"这是一个美丽新世界"。

需要看清的是，民主党内部并不统一：桑德斯、AOC所在的进步派主张一刀切暂停；沃伦等建制派主张风险导向监管；而加州、华盛顿州的民主党议员本身就是AI产业利益的代言者。安萨里的表态是光谱最左端的声音，不是全党共识。

第二股：电价

美国能源信息署10月23日公布的数据：8月居民平均电价每千瓦时18.16美分，同比上涨3.4%；预计2027年达18.7美分，较2024年累计上涨约13.3%。

一个200MW的标准AI训练数据中心，按86%的行业平均负载率测算，年耗电约1500GWh，相当于40万人全年的用电量。电费占数据中心运营成本的六到七成。国际能源署预计2026—2030年美国用电量合计增加超过4200亿千瓦时，其中约一半的增量来自数据中心。

于是出现了《纳税人保护法案》（H.R.9430）：科技公司必须自掏腰包，为数据中心新增的发电能力、输电线路和电网升级买单。弗吉尼亚州2050亿美元的预算案里，塞进了全美首个数据中心电力消费税。纽约州通过了为期一年的超大规模数据中心审批暂停。

这里的矛盾极其朴素：AI的收益归股东，AI的电费归居民。当这笔账被摊到每一张电费单上，它就不再是技术议题。

第三股：估值

英伟达市值一度突破5.5万亿美元，市销率约16.8倍——处于三年分位数的0.13%，意思是过去三年里99.87%的时间它都比现在便宜。席勒市盈率逼近41，巴菲特指标升至210%。

text:
Crypto has spent years making everything transparent.

But transparency and privacy were never supposed to be opposites.

Aztec's new Tierra upgrade is an important step toward a different model.

Developers can build apps where some actions are private and others remain public.

Payments can stay confidential.
Trading activity can be protected.
AI interactions can happen without exposing sensitive data.
And the technology is getting faster: Aztec says private proofs can now be generated in around one second.
The real breakthrough isn't hiding everything.

It's giving users control over what they reveal.

The next generation of Web3 won't just need transparency.

It will need programmable privacy.

With just 1B tokens of additional distillation training, ZHA preserves most of the performance of full attention on models up to 35B parameters. On RULER at 256K context, it achieves 93.3% vs 96% accuracy, while attending to just 1-6% of the KV-cache.

author: Loopscale
quoted_text:
Update: Priority loan functionality has now been restored across the platform.
• Collateral-top ups are available for all loans
• Repayments are available for all loans except those funded by the USDC Genesis Vault
• Borrowers who fully repay loans can withdraw their collateral. Collateral withdrawals remain temporarily disabled for loans funded by the USDC Genesis Vault.

Vault withdrawals and all other protocol functionality remain restricted out of an abundance of caution. Our team and partners are working to ensure a safe restoration of full functionality as quickly as possible.

We have identified and contained the two paths used during this incident. Both paths involved sophisticated, multi-step transactions targeting publicly inspectable program logic and private transaction-building APIs. The attacker first targeted the SOL Genesis Vault using a misconfigured combination of asset-pricing parameters that caused deposited collateral to be valued as a different asset, enabling an undercollateralized loan of approximately $412K. They later used an atomic transaction bundle to sell a loan carrying an extreme interest rate into the USDC Genesis Vault, inflating its NAV and enabling a disproportionate redemption of approximately $521K which our systems halted within 30 seconds of transaction generation. No user deposits will incur a loss.

We will share further updates from this account as our investigation progresses and additional functionality is safely restored.

text:
Even though I disagree with some of the assumptions made, this is a good write-up of the discussion, and I appreciate the perspective on the benefits and the conclusion that Glamsterdam should proceed.

There really are two classes of “invariants”
- *Parameters*, eg, gas cost of an operation or block time
- Pricing *mechanisms* for operations

Contracts should not rely on the first class not changing. However mechanisms should be updated ideally in a non-breaking manner.

Glamsterdam has a mix of both changes. Unfortunately, a planned mechanism update (EIP-8037) produces breaking changes where we should not expect some to be, hence the additional delay

In any case, if either of the two categories sees some change, every effort should be made to identify and support apps that are directly or indirectly affected. It could be that the gas cost update makes a specific use case relatively more expensive, or cheaper, changing app economics.

A repository was released for app devs to identify the changes https://t.co/H3XuZZZZVL Internal and external audits have already led to active outreach, this step is designed for last mile coverage

text:
Democrats won Congress and are starting to talk policy. Their emerging agenda: expand federal healthcare spending while imposing new restrictions on AI.

This combination is fiscally ruinous and we do not need to wait to see 7% yields on 10Y treasuries to reach this conclusion. 

Like it or not, AI is our engine for economic growth and expanding our tax base. Like it or not, AI is also our best shot at taming healthcare costs: automating administrative work, expanding clinicians’ capacity, and delivering more care without a proportional increase in expensive human labor.

Look at how demanding the arithmetic already is. Even if real GDP grows 5% every year starting in 2027 - an extraordinarily strong growth assumption (~8% nominal) - and we add no new spending commitments, we'd STILL run a $400B deficit in 2035.

This is an agenda that will lock young Americans into a debt burden that consumes decades of future prosperity: more taxes, more national income diverted to interest, and less room to save, invest, and build wealth as we age.

If you are under the age of 50, think long and hard about your future. If you have children, think about the country they will inherit. A vote for this platform is a vote for leaving the next generation worse off than your own. 

Every policy decision entails tradeoffs and I didn't hear an outstanding alternative proposal in 2025/2026. But these are your views and you're over 50, you should be ashamed. If these are your views and you're under 50, you should spend some more time thinking about your views.

text:
星舰这次要飞22个多小时，等的却是回到起飞的那座塔。SpaceX把下一次试飞定在最早11月13日下午2点45分（太平洋时间），发射还要等监管批准。按计划，助推器升空6分35秒后由塔抓住，飞船要到发射后22小时32分才回到塔边。

升空后，飞船先走一条安全的亚轨道，确认状态健康，才点火入轨。进入轨道后，它要部署26颗V3星链卫星。其中3颗带着相机，回头拍飞船的隔热盾。再入时正对高温的那一面，要在返回之前先看清楚。

卫星放完后，飞船还要滑行约21小时，原因在地面。地球一直在自转，飞船每绕一圈，星舰基地都会偏离它下方经过的那条线。前后约14圈之后，轨道才重新对准发射场，飞船才有飞回起点的窗口。滑行期间，健康检查一直在做。

只有各项条件都满足，飞船才会飞回塔边。条件不够，它还可以在夏威夷或智利外海备降。这22个多小时里的检查结果，决定它最后回到塔边还是落在海上。

Onchain trading is starting to move prices on the NYSE.

"The tokenized equities product that we structured is not a derivative. It doesn't use debt. It doesn't have any kind of crazy overhang. It is a fully backed security that gives the holders voting rights, that gives them dividends."

"There's no risk of one company holding a big voting block on behalf of all the people. There's no risk of them structuring weird debt things that could actually hurt the stock. People are buying the stock."

"We've actually started to see days, and this is mostly on the smaller side of stocks, where there's more volume on Base for the long tail of assets than there is on the traditional venues, and where demand on Base is actually then driving price appreciation in the traditional venues like the New York Stock Exchange."

text:
I’ve been collecting/investing in retrogaming for a few months now.

More and more I find myself thinking of old games as quasi meditative, relaxing experiences. A welcome breather from the onslaught that is the internet at large, nowadays.

This tells me all I need to know about how absolutely and tragically fried my dopamine receptors are, and how fucked we are as a society.

Touching physical discs, pressing actual buttons, litterally unplugging when done seems trivial, but I urge you all to give it a go. No bulimic neverending choices on Netflix, or Disney, Apple tv, HBo, hulu, oh noooo half an hour has gone already and I haven’t even looked at titles.

I added a DVD and Blu Ray player, in my retro room, I have my library, I sit there with intention, at a glance enjoy the cover art, the physicality of the objects that immediately identify the era, the mood, the “texture” I’m going for tonight. When the movie is over, I just enjoy the credits for ten minutes, taking it all in, without the fucking app cutting to the next show, the next ad, more consumption.

When I play, I play with friends, in real life. Together in the same room. Notice how every fucking console back then had 4 joystick ports. It was multiplayer.
