text:
I believe the direct catalyst behind this $CLAUDIA rally was indeed Elon repost, but the significance of this event is worth studying beyond simply receiving another round of celebrity attention.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

The reason is that what Elon amplified this time was not a promotional video made by Anabology himself, but a contest entry created by an external creator around Claudia.

That distinction matters. Previously, we had been discussing whether Claudia could evolve from an AI character created by Anabology into an open IP that other creators would also want to participate in. This event provided the first relatively direct example: an external creator produced content, the content entered a contest and spread through the community, SXSI published it, and it eventually received direct exposure through Elon.

I believe this is precisely one of the most promising parts of our previous thesis, but also one that had lacked concrete evidence until now.

On November 7, Elon Musk posted on X: "Who put your beliefs into your head? It probably wasn’t you." The post quoted an SXSI post featuring a contest entry created by PinelandLabs for the CLAUDIA video contest, titled Who Is Prompting You?

As of the time I was preparing this post, the original SXSI post had received approximately 1 million views, 1,100 likes, and 278 reposts. PinelandLabs subsequently publicly thanked SXSI and Anabology for giving the work a platform. Elon’s account clearly expanded the exposure of this content.

But I want to emphasize one detail: Elon did not explicitly express support for CLAUDIA, comment on the token, or indicate any investment interest. He amplified a piece of creator content related to Claudia. However, for an AI-native IP, this type of exposure could be more valuable than simply receiving a like from a celebrity on the project’s official account.

Because it shows that Claudia’s content now has the opportunity to spread beyond Anabology’s own publishing channels, reaching third-party creators, content platforms, and broader social networks.

This is also why I believe this was the main reason behind the current rally. The GLIF signing, creator contests, and tool updates have strengthened the fundamentals, but they were not substitutes for the direct catalyst behind this particular Elon event. The immediate price reaction primarily came from this external attention shock.

Compared with our previous analysis, what has actually been validated?

My original thesis for CLAUDIA was that it had the potential to evolve from an AI music video character into an AI-native entertainment IP. The biggest question at the time was whether Anabology could continue producing content, but if he remained the only person creating it, Claudia’s potential reach would ultimately be limited by his individual creative capacity.

Now, this situation is beginning to change.

The first development is creator participation.

Anabology is not just publishing his own work. He is also lowering the barriers for other people to participate through Claudia MCP. He previously announced a video creation contest, offering $420.69 in XMoney to the creator of the best entry and $69.42 to the runner-up. Later, he also added a $100 community-voted award.

The first contest ended on November 6 and entered the judging stage. Anabology subsequently launched a second round, maintaining the same prize structure: $420.69 for the best judged entry, $69.42 for second place, and $100 for the top community-voted video. The second round will end on November 13.

The prize amounts themselves are not particularly large, but I believe the value of this initiative should not be measured by the prize money alone.

It is effectively a creator bootstrapping strategy: encouraging external users to use Claudia MCP to produce music videos, then using contests, voting, and X distribution to spread attention that was previously concentrated around Anabology among a wider group of creators.

PinelandLabs’ work being selected by SXSI and subsequently amplified by Elon is a good example.

Of course, I would not say that Claudia already has an established independent creator ecosystem. What we can confirm now is that people are willing to participate, and their work has the opportunity to receive exposure far beyond the original community. What needs to be observed next is whether these creators will continue making Claudia-related content after the contests end.

The second direction receiving validation is that Claudia’s content creation tools are becoming genuine entry points for participation.

We previously discussed Claudia’s MCP, Grok Bot, and the creative toolchain that Anabology continues to improve. Version 0.3.6 introduced Earshot audio analysis, allowing Opus to identify song structures and beats, as well as detect issues between audio and video editing. ElevenLabs provides additional voice, sound effect, and music production capabilities. At the same time, the team has addressed issues involving duplicate generations, rendering, file compatibility, and task recovery.

The value of these updates is that external creators no longer need to build an entire AI production workflow from scratch to create content around Claudia.

But the real test is not how many tools are released. It is how many people actually use them and whether those people keep coming back.

GLIF signing is another particularly important development in CLAUDIA’s fundamental improvement.

In early November, GLIF first hinted that Claudia might be joining its AI Modeling Agency, before subsequently announcing the official signing.

GLIF added Claudia to its AI Characters lineup and made her available for users to cast in commercial creative projects, including advertisements, short dramas, and other video content. The team also stated that Claudia had accumulated 44 million views and released a Claudia debut trailer produced entirely using Glif.

I think this development is more worth watching than simply adding another KOL collaboration.

Previously, Claudia’s content was mainly centered around AI music videos, and her ability to gain exposure depended heavily on Anabology continuously producing new work. GLIF now provides a new distribution channel: other users can directly cast Claudia in their advertisements, short dramas, and creative projects.

This effectively gives Claudia another identity. She is no longer just an AI virtual singer publishing music videos, but is also becoming an AI model and content character that other creators can use.

If brands begin using Claudia in advertisements, and independent creators continue featuring her in different short dramas and videos, her exposure could expand from music content into the broader AI entertainment and commercial creative industries. This would significantly increase the range of potential distribution channels available to her.

However, I would not interpret this signing as proof that Claudia has already generated commercial revenue. GLIF has indeed opened the Casting entry for Claudia, but specific commercial orders, revenue-sharing arrangements, copyright authorization, and partnership terms have not been sufficiently disclosed. The 44 million views reported by GLIF also should not be interpreted as 44 million unique users.

What I would rather see is whether Claudia can actually secure commercial content orders, rather than simply being included in an AI modeling directory. If we eventually see brand advertisements, recurring Casting demand, or even other platforms inviting Claudia to participate in content production, then the significance of this signing will be much more fully validated.

As for what the market is currently betting on, I believe it has moved beyond just Elon’s attention. There are three possibilities gradually coming together.

First, can Claudia become an AI-native IP with sustainable distribution and attention?

As the cost of AI content production declines, there will be no shortage of AI tools capable of generating visually impressive videos. However, the problem with most AI characters is their lack of continuity: one appearance today, another tomorrow, leaving audiences with little reason to remember them.

Claudia has already accumulated a certain level of visual recognition, a collection of music works, and her own social media account. Anabology is also continuing to produce content around her. If these works can make audiences remember a specific character rather than just another AI-generated video, she may have the opportunity to establish a lasting influence similar to that of a virtual pop artist.

Second, can external creators become Claudia’s second content production engine? This is the direction I am most interested in right now.

If Claudia’s content continues to be produced exclusively by Anabology, the project’s growth potential will easily be limited by his individual capacity. But if MCP, open character materials, and creator contests can attract more independent participants, content production may no longer depend on a single person.

More importantly, different creators can give Claudia different styles and stories. Some may produce music, others may create short dramas or derivative content, and some may even develop their own content series around her.

Once this starts happening, Claudia has the opportunity to evolve from a character managed by one creator into an IP collectively expanded by a community.

Third, can AI IP enter the commercialization stage?

GLIF’s involvement gives this direction a concrete product entry point. In the future, Claudia may not only gain views through music videos, but also receive exposure through advertisements, short dramas, and other creative projects.

If these three directions can reinforce one another, what the market is trading will no longer be just another AI Meme, but an AI character attempting to establish a system encompassing content production, external creator participation, and commercial distribution.

Of course, this is still what the market is betting on, not an already completed business model.

So, here are the developments I will be paying attention to next.

First, the second round of the creator contest ending on November 13.

The first round has already ended, and the second round continues to offer judged prizes and community voting rewards. More than the prize money itself, I am interested in whether the second round can attract more high-quality work from independent creators and whether that content can gain exposure beyond Anabology’s existing community.

If people continue creating Claudia content voluntarily after the contest ends, that would be a sign that creator participation is beginning to become sustainable.

Second, GLIF’s actual commercialization progress.

Claudia has already entered the Casting lineup of the AI Modeling Agency. What we should watch next is whether genuine brand advertisements, commercial short videos, and other user-generated projects begin to emerge.

If commercial content with meaningful distribution results appears, it would expand Claudia’s narrative from an AI music IP into AI Talent and AI Entertainment.

Third, external distribution beyond Elon.

Elon’s repost has brought considerable attention, but in the long run, I do not want the entire project to remain dependent on him.

What would be much more encouraging is seeing other major creators, AI content accounts, music communities, and even brands begin using Claudia voluntarily. That would demonstrate that her appeal has expanded beyond the original crypto community and creator circle.

Finally, the economic connection between content production and the token.

Previous official Claudia materials stated that trading fees would be used to fund film production. This is a design worth watching: token trading activity could provide funding for content production, while the content itself could generate new attention.

However, there is still insufficient data to establish how much of the trading fees actually enters the production budget, how those funds are spent, or whether these investments result in continuous content output.

Also, the rewards for this contest are paid through XMoney, so they should not be treated as direct on-chain value capture for CLAUDIA.

If we eventually see a clear and verifiable relationship between fee revenue, creative funding, and actual content production, my confidence in the token’s long-term economic thesis would increase further.

As for the risks, I believe the biggest one right now is not that Claudia lacks content, but that the success of that content may ultimately have nothing to do with the token.

Even if she really becomes a popular AI virtual artist, that does not mean CLAUDIA will automatically receive the corresponding revenue or value. If the economic relationship between the IP, creators, platforms, and token remains unclear, the project’s fundamentals may become stronger without a corresponding improvement in the token’s value capture.

In addition, competition in the AI virtual artist sector will continue to intensify. Claudia needs to establish a recognizable identity and maintain consistent content quality. A single Elon repost or one creator contest is not enough to build a lasting competitive advantage.

Finally, my overall judgment: the fundamentals have strengthened considerably, but the most important validation is only just beginning.

Looking back at our previous analysis, I believe several of our original assumptions have received new support.

Previously, we believed that Anabology’s continuous content production capability could allow Claudia to move beyond relying on one-off viral events. The growing collection of works, her own social media account, and new distribution opportunities now support this view.

We also believed Claudia had the potential to evolve from Anabology’s personal creation into an open IP. PinelandLabs’ contest entry receiving external exposure, SXSI participating in content distribution, and the MCP creator contest entering its second round have now provided some initial real-world examples.

We previously believed that Elon’s attention could become a catalyst for Claudia to receive recurring external exposure. This latest direct reference from Elon to content featuring CLAUDIA further demonstrates that Claudia-related works still have the opportunity to enter his attention.

There is also another direction that we had not fully explored before, but which has now made progress: the GLIF signing is allowing Claudia to enter the distribution channels of AI modeling and commercial content production.

However, I still believe three things remain unproven.

First, whether independent creators will continue producing Claudia content after the contests end.

Second, whether GLIF can bring Claudia actual commercial orders and sustained external users.

Third, whether the growth of the IP can translate into CLAUDIA token demand through a clear and verifiable economic mechanism.

So my current assessment is that CLAUDIA’s fundamentals have strengthened considerably, and the project is more interesting than it was in my previous analysis. This change is not simply another Elon interaction. It is the fact that external creator participation, celebrity attention, and AI commercial distribution are now appearing along the same development path.

What I am more willing to bet on now is whether Claudia can become an AI character that is continuously used by different creators, distributed across different platforms, and eventually called upon by commercial brands.

If the only development is Anabology continuously producing new videos while Elon occasionally interacts with them, the market will keep trading the same attention narrative. But if other creators begin actively building content around Claudia, GLIF brings commercial applications, and more audiences begin recognizing and following the character, then her growth will no longer be limited by the creative pace of a single person.

I believe the most important development worth watching is that Claudia is beginning to move from an AI character that people simply watch into an AI IP that allows others to participate in creating.

The valuation potential of these two models is completely different.

The next thing I most want to see is whether Claudia can continue generating new community-created content after the second round of the contest ends on November 13. Because that will directly determine the outcome of our biggest long-term thesis: whether Claudia can truly build her own creator ecosystem.

What matters most to me about $CLAUDIA at this point is no longer whether Anabology can produce another video that catches Elon's attention.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

It's whether he can turn Claudia from a character that continuously produces AI content into an IP that other creators are willing to participate in.

The former determines how hot a single rally can get; the latter determines whether this story can keep generating new catalysts.

Based on the progress so far, I believe CLAUDIA's fundamentals have strengthened compared with its early stage. However, while its content production capabilities are beginning to take shape, three questions remain unresolved: whether the community can expand independently, whether the product can generate sustained demand, and whether these developments can translate into value for the token.

Looking back at Claudia’s development, Anabology initially established the character’s identity through AI music videos, followed by multiple interactions with Elon and attention from Marc Andreessen, co-founder of a16z. The significance of these signals goes beyond exposure. They have led the market to consider a new possibility: can AI creators build virtual artist brands with their own characters, bodies of work, and audiences through continuous content production? Traditional entertainment IP often requires substantial production costs and long development cycles, while AI tools are lowering the barriers to producing music, videos, and visual content. If a character can continuously release new work and gradually build a consistent audience, it has an opportunity to move beyond the distribution cycle of a single video.

But celebrity interactions are catalysts, not a complete investment thesis. Elon being willing to comment on a video does not mean he endorses the CLAUDIA token, nor does it guarantee that future content will receive the same treatment. Rather than waiting for another external figure to bring in traffic, I care more about whether Anabology has developed a repeatable creative process: understanding what kind of content is likely to attract attention, turning those insights into new work quickly, and sustaining that attention through subsequent releases. If this capability becomes consistent, celebrity interactions could serve as an additional distribution channel instead of being the only thing the project depends on.

Recent updates have given me a clearer picture of this direction. Claudia is no longer just the protagonist in music videos. She now has her own X account, where she posts daily updates, expresses her personality and ambitions, and attempts to build a social relationship with her audience that feels closer to that of a real artist. Meanwhile, the official website continues to organize her work, visual identity, and creative materials. Several music videos have now formed a relatively continuous body of work, including new releases such as “DON'T LET ME SCROLL” and “WHITEPILL.” Different releases are increasingly built around the same character rather than introducing an entirely new AI identity each time.

This distinction may seem minor, but it matters for Claudia’s ability to build long-term recognition. Even a technically impressive AI video can quickly be replaced by the next piece of content with a stronger visual impact. A character with a consistent appearance, personality, musical style, and growing body of work has a better chance of being remembered and giving people a reason to follow its next release. Claudia’s black hair, orange streak, and star-shaped hair clip keep recurring, while her outfits, settings, and themes can change. This approach is gradually establishing continuity around the character, which is an important distinction between an IP and an ordinary content account.

What particularly interests me is the project’s recent investment in creative tools. Anabology has made the claudia-bot toolkit public and continues to improve the workflow covering everything from creative concepts, lyrics, and music production to image generation, shot composition, lip-sync, editing, and final rendering. Version 0.3.6 introduced Earshot audio analysis, enabling Opus to analyze song structures, identify beats, and check the alignment between audio and video cuts. ElevenLabs adds capabilities for voice generation, sound effects, and music production. The team has also addressed practical issues involving duplicate generations, rendering dimensions, video compatibility, task recovery, and API usage alerts.

The importance of these improvements is not that every new tool will directly drive the token price higher, but that they could reduce the time and cost required to produce content continuously. A more interesting possibility is that Anabology will no longer need to create everything related to Claudia personally. Other creators could use the publicly available character materials and tools to produce songs, short films, images, or derivative stories. If participation gradually expands, Claudia’s content supply could shift from being driven by one creator to being expanded by multiple creators.

However, open-source tools do not automatically create a creator ecosystem. What we can confirm now is that the tools and character materials are becoming more accessible and the production workflow is improving. What we cannot yet confirm is how many independent creators are using these tools consistently or how many derivative works have attracted meaningful attention. The signal I would most like to see is not another batch of new features, but Claudia appearing in content created by people outside the original team and attracting audiences of her own. Only when others begin creating around her voluntarily does Claudia have a chance to evolve from a character continuously produced by Anabology into an IP with its own independent distribution power.

This is also why I still find CLAUDIA worth watching. The project has established a certain level of content production capability, character recognition, and external attention, but it has not yet proven that it can continue growing independently of its original creator. The long-term advantage of AI-native IP may not simply be the ability to produce content more cheaply. It may lie in allowing characters to accumulate work, attract participants, and gradually become cultural symbols maintained by a community at a faster pace. If Claudia can reach this point, its attention will no longer depend entirely on whether Anabology’s next video goes viral.

The token itself requires a more cautious assessment. The official website positions CLAUDIA as a community token and states that trading fees will be used to fund video production. This establishes a potential connection between token activity and content creation: market trading can provide funds for production, while new releases may attract additional attention and trading activity. But whether this cycle is actually functioning still needs to be verified through records of fee revenue, fund flows, and spending on video production. CLAUDIA also cannot currently be treated as an asset with clearly defined intellectual property rights or a share of film revenue. Holding the token does not automatically give holders ownership of Claudia or rights to its commercial income.

For this reason, I would not assume that token value capture is strengthening in parallel simply because the number of releases is increasing. Even if Claudia continues to grow as a content property, the IP’s success may remain disconnected from the token price if new attention does not translate into token demand, or if the token economy lacks a verifiable connection to the project’s actual revenue. The project’s reliance on third-party AI models and production tools also means that ongoing content creation must contend with costs, service reliability, and commercial licensing requirements. An open approach to character creation also requires clear copyright boundaries; otherwise, expanding community participation could make usage rights and commercial-use rules increasingly ambiguous.

Looking at the current price, CLAUDIA has a market capitalization of approximately $3.33 million, compared with an all-time high of around $11.93 million, representing a drawdown of roughly 72%. Its 24-hour trading volume is approximately $1.2 million, with liquidity of around $258,700. The price is below the MA10 and MA20 levels of approximately $3.56 million and $3.59 million, respectively, while the RSI stands at 48.76. This suggests that the market has not yet established a clear short-term bullish structure, and the recent rebound is insufficient to confirm a trend reversal. Trading activity remains present, but relatively limited liquidity means that capital entering or leaving the market can still cause significant price fluctuations.

I would not conclude that CLAUDIA is cheap simply because its market capitalization is below $4 million. What matters is whether the content production capabilities and distribution potential implied by this valuation can continue to improve. The market has already traded on Elon’s attention, the circulation of AI-generated music videos, and the possibility of Claudia becoming an AI-native artist. A new revaluation requires fresh evidence: subsequent releases continuing to attract external attention, independent creators beginning to participate, the social account developing a more consistent audience, and a clearer connection emerging between content production and the token economy. If these developments gradually materialize, the market will have stronger reasons to reassess its long-term potential. Without continued content distribution and actual demand, however, the price may continue to fluctuate around the existing narrative.

My current assessment of CLAUDIA is that its content fundamentals are strengthening, but token value capture remains unproven. I am not betting on whether it can replicate the rally triggered by celebrity interactions. I am betting on whether it can establish a sustainable creative model in which Claudia continuously produces new work and gradually attracts participation beyond the original creator. Celebrity exposure can introduce the character to a wider audience, the production toolkit can improve creative efficiency, and open participation can broaden distribution. What ultimately determines its long-term potential is whether these three elements can converge into a continuously growing character ecosystem.

For me, the most important thing to watch next is whether Claudia can continue attracting new audiences and creators without another interaction from Elon. If it can, the project may have a chance to break free from its dependence on a single creator and external celebrity catalysts. If, however, all the attention continues to depend on Anabology’s next video, then even as its content production capabilities improve, its growth ceiling may remain constrained by one person’s creative pace.

YC 今年新晋的 17 家独角兽，几乎快被 AI 包圆了。

Y Combinator 公布了 2026 年 1—10 月诞生的 17 家新独角兽名单，里面有几个挺有意思的信号：

最贵的是 AI 训练数据公司 AfterQuery，估值 32 亿美元；其次是做 AI 医疗福利的 Angle Health，27 亿美元；AI 原生保险公司 Corgi 则达到 26 亿美元。

更值得注意的是，这份名单里不仅有 Emergent 这样的 AI 应用生成平台、Exa 这样的 AI 搜索基础设施，还有 HappyRobot、Avoca 等深入企业具体业务流程的 AI Agent 公司。

甚至连保险、银行、卫星通信、太空数据中心这些看起来相距甚远的行业，也都出现在了名单上。

一个很明显的变化是：AI 创业正在从「帮人完成某项任务」，走向「直接接管某个行业的业务流程」。

过去的 SaaS 公司卖软件，让客户自己干活；现在的新一代 AI 公司，越来越想直接把活干了。

而 YC 这份名单真正有意思的地方，或许不在于又制造了多少家十亿美元公司，而在于独角兽的生产方式正在改变。

以前，创业公司需要证明自己能服务足够多的人；现在，它们开始证明自己能替代足够多的工作。

软件曾经按席位收费，AI 正在试图按工作成果收费。下一代软件巨头，可能看起来越来越不像软件公司。

text:
One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

text:
The Jensen Huang story keeps getting crazier.

US intelligence reportedly discovered that Nvidia’s CEO was romantically involved with a suspected Chinese spy.

Here's where things get insane:

1.) The woman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed, a company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms circumvent US chip export restrictions.

2.) US intelligence believes she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its primary intelligence agency.

3.) Intelligence officials reportedly suspected her objective included gathering information about Huang and potentially influencing Nvidia to push for looser US chip export controls.

4.) Huang has spent the past year repeatedly lobbying Washington to loosen those exact restrictions.

5.) US officials reportedly prepared an intelligence memo detailing the relationship and circulated it among senior government officials shortly before Trump's summit with Xi Jinping.

6.) Trump had reportedly already been briefed on the suspected espionage operation and chose not to act on the information.

7.) Huang has met with Trump repeatedly, reportedly even accompanying him aboard the presidential aircraft on a trip to China.

8.) Megaspeed's Malaysian affiliate reportedly purchased at least $4.8 BILLION in equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026.

9.) Federal authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024, with the Justice Department reportedly taking over the Commerce Department's investigation this year.

10.) Investigators reportedly found Nvidia equipment in boxes that appeared ready for shipment rather than installed in operational data centers.

11.) Alice Huang's name was reportedly removed from Megaspeed's corporate documents as scrutiny intensified. Her continuing involvement with the company remains unclear.

12.) Nvidia maintains that it investigated Megaspeed's chip deployments and found no evidence of illegal diversion.

13.) Three congressional committee chairmen are now demanding that Huang appear for a closed-door briefing on November 18.

We're talking about the CEO of the world's most valuable company, a suspected Chinese intelligence operation, billions of dollars in advanced AI chips, and the US government's efforts to control China's access to the technology.

There is still no public evidence that Huang knowingly cooperated with Chinese intelligence or that the alleged operation successfully influenced US policy.

But the questions surrounding this are extraordinary.

text:
4,843 backtested trading strategies.

Free.

Ranked by Sharpe ratio. The top one sits at 3.39.

Here's what's inside:

→ every strategy tested over decades of real data
→ Sharpe ratio, t stat and years tested for each one
→ full Python code and data
→ 136 libraries for backtesting, bots, market data and broker APIs
→ 55 trading books, beginner to pro

And here's how to turn one into a live bot with Opus 5.5:

1. Pick from the 61 strongest strategies, sorted by market: stocks, bonds, forex or crypto

2. Create a free account to unlock the Python code and data

3. Paste the code into Claude Code and ask Opus to explain every rule in plain English. When it buys. When it sells. Why.

4. Ask Opus to rerun the backtest with REAL fees on the last 3 years. If it doesn't make money after costs, stop here.

5. Have Opus convert the research code into live code that reads real prices and fires real signals

6. Connect a broker from the libraries, like Alpaca for stocks or Binance for crypto

7. Add a risk layer: fixed position size, a stop loss on every trade, a daily loss limit and a kill switch

8. Paper trade for 2 weeks with fake money. If live results don't match the backtest, the strategy isn't ready.

9. Add Telegram alerts so your phone pings on every trade. Only then go live, and start small.

A great backtest is a starting point, not a promise.

Most strategies die in step 4 or step 8.

That's the point. Better they die there than with your money.

Full guide on building an AI trading system below

Calif CEO @XorNinja says cybersecurity has no playbook for stopping 1,000 AI agents attacking a network simultaneously, even if defenders can detect them:

"Attackers always adapt faster and earlier than defenders. Even the AI companies themselves don't have great security."

"Imagine you enter a cage fight, but you are blindfolded and the other guy stay in the dark, and every once in a while they would come out and punch you and then disappear."

"How could you win that fight?"

"I was at Google and that's basically the mantra at Google. In security you have three things: prevention, detection, and response. And Google accept that prevention gonna fail at scale."

"You can detect them, but does it help you if you find that there's maybe a thousand agents hacking you right now inside your network? How can you contain them without a full shutdown of your system?"

"This actually requires defense to come up with a new paradigm. I haven't seen anybody come up with a good idea here. We're not there yet."

text:
I think a lot of people are completely wrong about what caused this midterm "blue tsunami."

I also believe that much of the hyperbolic, misguided analysis is coming from people who have hated Trump for a long time and who have been eagerly waiting with bated breath to declare the end of Trump and MAGA.

"It was obviously the Iran War. Trump didn't put America first. He betrayed America. It was gas prices. Only a fool would think otherwise."

Ok. Fair enough.

Allow me to present a hypothetical scenario. Let's pretend that Trump #2 never started the war with Iran.

Imagine if the price of gas was not around $4.00 a gallon but instead, let's say something low, assume $2.70 a gallon.

Pretend inflation was at a near perfect 2% for the year and GDP was cruising along at a 15 year high.

Assume wages were up and unemployment was at about a 50 year low.

No war. Great economy. That would have won Republicans the midterms right?

That would have prevented Democrats from flipping 41 House seats and 5 Governorships?

Those hypotheticals I listed above are what was happening in 2018 before the midterms. And yet, Democrats flipped 41 House seats and 7 Governorships during the midterms.

The Senate races turned out differently because Democrats were defending races all around the country in 2018. Republicans took back a couple red states. But the 2018 midterms were considered a massive blue wave for Democrats. No Iran War, economy booming, and still, that's how the midterms turned out.

Here's a fun fact. There were approximately 35.5 million Democrat votes during the 2014 midterms. There were approximately 61 million Democrat votes during the 2018 midterms.

25 million more Democrat votes during a booming economy. Do the current criticisms of Trump's second term explain that?

Trump went from 63 million votes in 2016, to 74 million in 2020, to 77 million in 2024. During each of his three midterms (2018, 2022, 2026), the Republican vote has increased substantially. But those increases do not compete with the additional 20 million Democrat vote bumps that happened in 2018, 2020, and 2026.

The question for Republicans becomes why do these gigantic Democrat vote bumps happen. How are they doing it? Is it because people hate Trump? They hate his policies? If those things were true, he would not continually gain support for himself and for the Republican Party.

Without even touching voter fraud, I believe that there is a clear, multi-faceted strategy that Democrats employed in 2018, 2020, and 2026 to drive insane amounts of people to polls, regardless of economic conditions. It's not difficult to identify, but Republicans don't talk about it and certainly don't have an answer for it. And Democrats can do it at will when needed.

Yes Trump won in 2024, but he was the only Republican that would have won and his win was helped by some unprecedented circumstances. Democrats were caught off guard. They did not make that mistake this time around.

Trump's second term has been far from perfect. Lots of mistakes and unforced errors. And once again, many terrible personnel choices by Trump.

That being said, I also believe that things could have been close to perfect right now and Republicans would have still gotten crushed during the midterms. Look at 2018. 

Perception is everything. Republicans are not prepared or even willing to step on to the field with Democrats in this regard.

The Democrats are a cohesive, well oiled, united machine working in perfect harmony with the MSM. Together they can create and push any narrative they want to push. Republicans not only have no answer to this, they instead spend their time fighting each other.

Democrats don't argue about policy. They create mass hysteria and fear. It's all emotion. It's their entire platform. Most Americans don't like their policies. But they are playing a game in which policy and ideas and reality do not factor into the equation. And there are very clear strategies that they use to create this mass hysteria and to drive voter turnout.

Republicans are just going to keep helplessly watching this happen over and over again. They learned nothing from Trump's first term. The exact same lies, smears and hoaxes were used again, except this time around they replaced Russia with Epstein. Same game plan to the tee. For example, they created the same immigration hysteria that they did in 2018. Everything happened again. 

Democrats were doing No Kings/Fight Fascism protests back in 2018 over immigration. People don't remember this but they were. I've posted videos about it. Bernie proudly declaring "No Kings." The immigration hysteria is especially effective at getting women riled up. 

People don't remember Kamala Harris taking a ladder to climb a fence to break into an ICE facility in 2018 or Rachel Maddow fake crying on TV, AOC crying at the fence, or Oprah holding her book club at the border. Protesters literally glueing themselves to the ground in protest (over nothing). A Time Magazine cover with Trump menacingly towering of a crying migrant child. The audio recording of a baby crying that the MSM played on repeat for weeks before the midterms. The British PM Theresa May publicly condemning "kids in cages" (the same cages that Obama built and used).

Republicans just sat idly on their hands and watched it happen all again, making no attempt at rebuttal. Democrats are on TV every hour of every day. Republicans politicians can't even bring themselves to post on social media in defense of enforcing the law. No matter who the next Republican President is, if he or she attempts to enforce immigration laws, Democrats will turn it into a midterm win. Guaranteed. And that's just one weapon in their playbook.

Republicans don't even know how to deal with the sabotage coming from their own side, let alone unite in a perception war with the Democrat Party.

Before the 2022 midterms inflation had reached a 40 year high, gas was above $5.00 a gallon, more people died from Covid in 2021 than in 2020, the botched Afghanistan withdrawal happened, the border was wide open and Biden was struggling to walk and talk. Still, Democrats only lost a few House seats and even picked up a Senate seat.

With all that happening, why didn't 20 million more Republicans vote during the 2022 midterms than in 2018? If economy matters so much, why was there no red wave? Have an election "expert" answer that one.

People who are playing Monday morning quarterback and criticizing everything Trump has done this time around are so not prepared for or even aware of the war that is being waged. They most likely care. They are ok with losing and many just want to declare all things Trump dead and buried. Maybe next election they will decide to fight back against the incredible machine Democrats. Good luck with that.

The Republicans who are so joyfully celebrating the end of "Trumpism" are in for a rude awakening when he's gone. Trump has increased his support and Republican support in every Presidential and midterm election he has been involved in.

I'm going to lay out in another post some detailed thoughts on the strategies Democrats have used to turn out massive amounts of votes and what Republicans might consider doing in response. It's nothing genius but there is a clear, detailed method to the Democrat madness and nobody seems to be talking about it or even care about it.

Granted, I'm just a guy on X who doesn't know much, but it doesn't hurt to post my thoughts so I will.

MEXC抹茶通往美国金融系统的资金通道将被切断，切断的不只是美元，也包括加密货币。美国财政部11月6日宣布，旗下FinCEN把MEXC认定为涉俄罗斯非法金融的"首要洗钱关切"。命令在《联邦公报》刊登30天后生效，届时美国受监管金融机构不得向MEXC发送或接收资金。

财政部指控，2021年5月至2026年5月，MEXC涉及至少160亿美元的制裁规避、网络犯罪等非法活动资金，其中近15亿美元与俄罗斯规避制裁有关。MEXC回应称运营正常，并已启动反洗钱和制裁控制的独立审查。

真正的连锁反应可能来自美国以外。其他地区的银行、支付通道和交易平台不少也有美国业务或美元往来，为免受牵连，可能主动加严审查、收缩与MEXC相关的往来，而且未必等到生效日才动手。

对不在美国的普通用户来说，"运营正常"是平台的回应，站内余额和交易可能一切照旧，外部肯不肯接收是另一回事。入金和卖币出金时，能用的银行卡和支付渠道可能变少；把币提到其他平台时，对方可能追问来源、拖长处理，甚至直接拒收。

数据里有一个参数是地址路径（hops），就是看你的个人钱包和非法地址经过了几个路径，所以你提到个人钱包后在充值交易所也会被涉及关联地址被风控
